The senior equerry to the King and Queen, who captured widespread attention online, is to step down from his role supporting the royal family.

Lieutenant Colonel Jonny Thompson, a popular figure among admirers who created an Instagram fan page dedicated to him, will depart his position at the end of the year following seven years in the royal household.

The equerry serves in the Royal Regiment of Scotland and is also leaving the armed forces to pursue a new career in the private sector, after spending more than 20 years as a soldier.

A spokesperson for Buckingham Palace stated: "Their Majesties were of course aware of this plan in advance and I know they are most grateful to Jonny for his support over the past seven years and wish him all the best for the future."

Lt Col Thompson featured in the King and Queen’s official party during their state visit to the United States in April, where he became notably popular.

open image in gallery The King’s equerry Major Johnny Thompson in 2023 ( PA Archive )

Lifestyle authority Martha Stewart posted praise and a picture featuring the equerry once the state tour concluded, writing on her Instagram account: "Can’t believe I got this close to the ‘hot equerry’…"

She appeared to have met the officer during a New York event celebrating the work of the King’s Trust and showcasing the UK’s cultural impact on the city.

The businesswoman added: “We actually spoke while waiting for King Charles to get to us for a few words. Totally charming, completely cool. Exceedingly handsome.”

The senior equerry was commissioned into the Royal Regiment of Scotland in April 2006 and served on operations in Iraq and Afghanistan before commanding Balaklava Company, the regiment’s 5th battalion, based in Edinburgh.

open image in gallery Lt. Col. Jonny Thompson attended the US state visit of King Charles III and Queen Camilla ( Getty )

While in command, he led the ceremonial and military support for the late Queen’s annual residence at Balmoral in 2018 and the following year, and in December 2019 was appointed equerry to Charles and Camilla.

He became the King’s equerry on Charles’s accession to the throne in September 2022 and two years later was promoted to the role of senior equerry to the King and Queen.

News.title: Man accused of stalking woman for 13 years had human skulls and part of John Wayne Gacy’s brain in his home: police
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A Wisconsin man accused of stalking his ex-girlfriend for more than a decade was allegedly found with a disturbing collection of human skulls, skeletal remains and a jar purportedly containing part of serial killer John Wayne Gacy’s brain.

Benjamin C. Larson, 47, of Fond du Lac, is facing a felony stalking charge in Dane County after the woman contacted Madison police on July 31 and reported what she said was years of unwanted contact following their brief relationship in 2013, according to a criminal complaint obtained by WBAY.

The woman told investigators she dated Larson for nearly two months before ending the relationship. Larson allegedly continued to attempt to contact her for the next 13 years through unsolicited letters, cards and emails. He also allegedly filed complaints against her with professional licensing boards in several states after she stopped responding.

In November 2025, Larson allegedly sent a card to the woman’s workplace saying he would “continue to try contacting” her or show up at her home. A month later, he allegedly sent another card to her home, an address she said she never gave him, referencing her husband and child by name. It also allegedly indicated he was wandering around Madison as part of his therapy.

The allegations became even more disturbing after detectives executed a search warrant at Larson’s home on August 14.

open image in gallery Benjamin C. Larson, 47, of Fond du Lac, Wisconsin, faces a felony stalking charge after police found human skulls, serial killer memorabilia and journals detailing alleged stalking behavior in his home ( Fond du Lac County Sheriff's Office )

Investigators said they discovered an extensive collection in the basement, including a grave rubbing connected to serial killer Edward Gein, 10 binders labeled “Edward Gein Book” and items reportedly taken from Gein’s grave.They also found cartridges similar to those used by the Zodiac Killer, according to the search findings, WBAY reports.

Among the items were a mummy labeled “Princes Taheb 1600 BC” and a jar labeled as containing a piece of Gacy’s brain. Gacy was executed in 1994 after being convicted of murdering 33 boys and young men in Illinois.

What appeared to be six human skulls, a partial skull, a human jawbone and additional skeletal remains were also found inside a glass casket, according to authorities.

The remains’ origins are still unclear. A forensic anthropologist is examining them to determine their authenticity and whether they are modern or ancient Native American remains, WBAY reports.

Inside a padlocked basement bedroom, investigators further found a lifelike silicone doll lying beneath a blanket on a bed, with a painting of a naked woman resembling the alleged stalking victim hanging above it.

A black portfolio found during the search reportedly contained 25 pages of handwritten journals belonging to Larson. In one entry, he allegedly wrote about his frustration over the woman’s marriage and child, saying, “it’s at times like this where I really ache to take their skulls, all of them.”

In another entry, Larson allegedly described driving to the woman’s Madison home at night dressed in black, wearing gloves and a mask. He wrote that he watched the house while carrying a machete, recorded her license plate and took three bags of her trash. Officers later found a plastic bin in his bedroom containing items belonging to the woman, including paper towels with dried blue flowers, a single earring, and discarded soda and beer bottles.

When questioned by police, Larson said his contact with the woman was civil and that his therapist suggested the licensing complaints to get her to respond. He said he now understood that her silence was an answer itself, WBAY reports.

Larson has been charged with one count of stalking. If convicted, he faces up to three years and six months in prison and a fine of up to $10,000, according to authorities.

News.content:

An anonymous federal official has warned members of Congress that Donald Trump’s “secretive, rushed” and “chaotic” plans for the U.S. Postal Service to implement new rules for mail-in ballots could disenfranchise millions of voters this fall.

Tuesday’s whistleblower report outlines “potentially catastrophic problems” with the administration’s brand-new system, including a “zero-percent failure policy” that could reject tens of thousands of ballots at a time if any single mistakes are made, including misread barcodes or inadvertent errors from postal workers.

Postal officials and IT specialists called it a “mess” and a “s*** show” that illegally defied court orders against putting the new ballot-tracking system in place ahead of crucial midterm elections, according to the report.

“We are crossing the Rubicon of American elections,” said Libby Liu, CEO of WhistleblowerAid.org, which is representing the anonymous official who submitted the complaints.

“This dangerously defective mail-in ballot process could disenfranchise millions of voters, ensnaring ballots in red tape under the guise of solving a non-existent problem,” she added. “People in states that rely heavily on vote-by-mail will have a more difficult time making their voices heard in our challenged democracy this November. The whistleblower’s service to our nation is warning the public that their ability to vote is in serious jeopardy.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump’s new mail-in ballot rules for the US Postal Service, which have been temporarily blocked in court, could pose enormous risks for millions of voters this fall, according to a new whistleblower report ( AFP/Getty )

Federal courts have repeatedly blocked the Postal Service from implementing Trump’s executive order on mail-in ballots, which called for the creation of a national voter registration list that would be used to decide who is eligible to cast a ballot.

On August 21, the USPS published its new certification requirements, changes that could not go into effect until federal courts lifted an injunction against them. The Supreme Court allowed Trump’s executive order to stand, for now, leaving the door open for lawsuits to proceed against the new USPS rules themselves.

Three days after the Supreme Court’s decision, District Judge Indira Talwani issued a temporary restraining order that blocks the changes, but the administration is continuing to fight the case in court to overhaul mail-in voting rules just weeks before Election Day.

Dozens of election officials from across the country have repeatedly warned that a last-minute scramble to upload lists of voters into an online portal designed by USPS would amount to an unconstitutional attack on election administration that would only sow more confusion and introduce potentially catastrophic errors.

If the plans are allowed to go into effect, USPS workers would be required to scan barcodes on a sample of envelopes to ensure the voters appear on the state’s list, according to the whistleblower report. If there is even one mismatch, that whole batch of ballots — which could be in the thousands at a time — could be rejected, the whistleblower said.

“As designed, the process is entirely unforgiving,” according to the report. “It could delay ballots by the thousands in repeated verification cycles — and thus prevent states from mailing enormous numbers of ballots.”

States are constantly updating their voter rolls, the lists sent to USPS could be out of date shortly after voters re-register with new personal information or addresses, or if new voters sign up but aren’t reflected in the already-approved list designed by the administration.

open image in gallery Trump’s executive order compelled USPS to develop an online portal for a national voter registration list that would be used to decide who is eligible to cast a ballot, but officials have warned that potential errors could risk disenfranchising voters ( AFP/Getty )

USPS and the Department of Justice have repeatedly defended the program, though election officials fear the government’s list could be dangerously too slow to reflect changes from the states.

“Their system is set up to fail — and risk the right to vote for millions of Americans who cast their ballots by mail,” according to Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal, whose office received the whistleblower report.

“Given this new information, such sloppiness and haste seems clearly part of a purposeful attempt to create chaos and prevent people from voting,” he said in a statement Tuesday. “I am demanding answers and accountability.”

Voting rights groups fear the president’s efforts to centralize control over election administration, which is left to the states under the Constitution, is an attempt to boost Republican candidates and suppress Democratic turnout during an election that is likely to determine the balance of power in Congress — and the fate of Trump’s remaining years in office.

open image in gallery Connecticut Democrat Senator Richard Blumenthal, whose office received the whistleblower report, says Trump’s mail-in ballot rules are ‘set up to fail’ in a ‘purposeful attempt’ to sow chaos in midterm elections ( Reuters )

Trump spent years baselessly insisting that voting by mail is ripe for fraud, and that manipulated ballots were “rigged” against him in elections he lost. He complained throughout 2020 elections that Republicans would “never” win without changing rules for voting by mail, which he has called “inherently corrupt” and “cheating” despite routinely casting his own ballots by mail.

The administration is pushing for mail-in ballot changes in court while the president simultaneously demands Senate passage his SAVE America Act, which would also severely restrict mail-in voting and impose nationwide voter ID rules, among other changes.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune has repeatedly expressed doubts about sacrificing the filibuster to pass Trump’s bill. Still, Trump has tried to argue for its passage in increasingly desperate terms, including not ruling out the possibility of a national emergency to put the rules in place.

“The crown jewel of American democracy, our historic record of free and fair elections, deserves so much better than this slipshod effort,” WhistleblowerAid.org senior vice president and special counsel David Kligerman, who is representing the whistleblower, said in a statement.

States are scrambling to prepare for midterm elections, with impending deadlines for voters to receive ballots that can be filled out and returned in time to count by November.

Officials in North Carolina have already started preparing ballots under a new state law requiring voters to start receiving them 60 days before an election. More states are set to start mailing out ballots in the coming days and weeks.

But the “slapdash rollout” of Trump’s new system “could prove a major threat to voting rights in upcoming midterm elections,” Kligerman said. “We hope that the courts across the country looking at this issue are able to take note of these fundamentally troubling revelations.”

News.title: Lindsay Clancy jury ordered to keep deliberating after failing to reach unanimous verdict
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

The judge in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial has ordered jurors to keep deliberating after they said they could not reach a unanimous decision.

The jury sent the judge a note Tuesday around the start of the fourth day of deliberations. It marked the first time the jury gave any indication they were at an impasse on whether to hold the Massachusetts mother criminally responsible for killing her three young children at her home in 2023.

On Friday, the jurors had asked to look at a knife that Clancy used to cut herself and bags with empty prescription pill bottles found in her house.

Clancy stared straight ahead as the jury entered and then looked toward them as the judge spoke to the panel.

open image in gallery Lindsay Clancy, 36, a former labor and delivery nurse, is charged in the 2023 deaths of her three young children at the family's home in Duxbury ( via REUTERS )

“I know that this was a long trial, all right,” Judge William Sullivan said in response to the jury’s note Tuesday. “I know there were over 80 witnesses. There were over 300 exhibits. But because of that, I’m going to ask you to go back out.”

Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse, doesn’t deny strangling her children but says postpartum psychosis led to her actions. Prosecutors argue she knew what she was doing. Clancy, 36, has pleaded not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility.

Lindsay Clancy verdict options

The jury could convict her of murder or manslaughter, or acquit her if jurors believe her deteriorating mental health was to blame. A conviction could lead to a life prison sentence. If she is acquitted, a judge could still order her confined to a mental health facility if an evaluation determines she is a danger to the public.

The jury began deliberating on Thursday afternoon. There had been little indication of whether they are making progress, outside of asking on Friday to look at a knife that Clancy used to cut herself and bags with empty prescription pill bottles found in her house.

open image in gallery Clancy had sought treatment from multiple providers and checked herself into a psychiatric hospital in the months before killing Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy, ages 5, 3 and 8 months ( Facebook )

Clancy's lawyer argued at the trial that she loved her children, but killed them because she lost her grip on reality — and on herself — due to postpartum psychosis, a rare mental illness that can follow childbirth. In the months before the killings, Clancy sought treatment for her worsening mental health, including a stay in a psychiatric hospital.

Prosecutors said Clancy strangled the children because she was depressed and tired of living, and made a conscious choice to kill them before attempting suicide.

Lindsay Clancy sought help before children’s killings

During more than four weeks of testimony, jurors heard differing views from medical experts about Clancy’s mental state after the birth of her third child and her culpability.

Both Clancy’s mother and sister testified that she became anxious, paranoid and suicidal.

Clancy had sought treatment from multiple providers and checked herself into a psychiatric hospital in the months before killing Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy, ages 5, 3 and 8 months.

Less than three weeks after being discharged, she sent her husband out on an errand and killed the children with exercise bands in the basement of their home south of Boston. She then jumped from a second-floor window and remains paralyzed from the waist down.

A forensic psychologist who testified for the prosecution said he concluded that Clancy killed the children because she wanted to kill herself but didn’t want to leave them behind.

open image in gallery Prosecutors argue that Clancy strangled the children because she was depressed and tired of living, and made a conscious choice to kill them before attempting suicide ( GoFundMe )

A psychologist who took the stand for the defense said Clancy didn’t recognize the “wrongfulness” of killing her children because of her mental health issues.

Clancy chose not to testify. She watched the proceedings from the defense table, occasionally weeping, as when prosecutors showed autopsy photos of the children to the jury.

Jurors spent two days listening to testimony from her former husband, Patrick Clancy, and his anguished 911 call. He was still on the phone when he discovered the children's bodies, minutes after finding his wife badly injured in the yard.

Patrick Clancy has said in interviews that he forgives his ex-wife, whom he viewed as ill rather than evil. The trial marks the first time he has seen Lindsay Clancy since the killings.

Postpartum psychosis, the condition that Clancy’s attorney says she had when she killed the children, is more serious and less common than postpartum depression.

Researchers estimate that the condition afflicts 1 to 2 out of 1,000 women after delivery. Although most who develop it don’t harm their children, mothers with severe cases might try to harm themselves or their kids.

The BBC has announced that popular winter sports programme Ski Sunday will no longer be produced after nearly 50 years on the air.

The show, which rounds up the latest alpine skiing action alongside features exploring a wide array of snow sports, has been a staple of the broadcaster’s output since first airing in 1978.

But while the channel will continue to show parts of the Winter Olympics, the seasonal weekly programme has been axed as the BBC continues to evolve its sport output.

Ski Sunday’s demise follows that of Football Focus, which came to an end after 52 years on air earlier in 2026.

“Ski Sunday has been a truly iconic programme and a much-loved part of BBC Sport’s output for many years,” Philip Bernie, head of events at BBC Sport, said. “Generations of viewers have enjoyed its coverage of the best in winter sports. We are enormously proud of the role it has played in bringing these moments to audiences across the UK, and extremely grateful to the brilliant people who have delivered them, not least the current outstanding team.

“These decisions are never easy, but as audience viewing habits evolve and we work to deliver value for licence fee payers, we have to make tough choices. We remain committed to bringing audiences the very best of winter sport, above all at the Winter Olympics, across BBC Sport’s platforms.”

Originally launched in 1978 to follow on from the 1976 Games in Innsbruck, the programme later formed part of Sunday Grandstand. It was fronted for many years by David Vine, with former skier Graham Bell and snowboarder Ed Leigh later forming a popular presenting partnership.

Four-time Olympian Chemmy Alcott joined the programme alongside Leigh in 2021.

Canada’s governing Liberals have secured victories in three special elections on Monday, providing a significant boost to Prime Minister Mark Carney amidst an intensifying trade dispute with U.S. President Donald Trump.

The Liberal Party claimed victory in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord in Quebec, Beaches-East York in Toronto, and North Vancouver-Capilano in British Columbia.

Carney framed the election results as a clear endorsement of his administration's trajectory.

"At this consequential time for Canada, voters have placed their trust in our government’s plan," he said in a statement.

The biggest shift occurred in Quebec, where Liberal candidate Daniel Gobeil won decisively in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord.

The district had been held by the opposition Conservatives since 2018, but the party fell to third place on Monday. The local economy relies on aluminum production and dairy farming, key sectors affected by the trade conflict.

Nelson Wiseman, a professor emeritus of political science at the University of Toronto, said Carney enjoys higher approval ratings in Quebec than anywhere else in Canada, noting that Trump’s remarks about annexation resonate deeply there.

"Quebecers have the most to lose in an apocalyptic scenario where the U.S. absorbs Canada, and the status of the French language disappears," Wiseman said.

The Liberals maintained control of the other two ridings. In British Columbia, Braeden Caley, Carney’s former deputy chief of staff, took North Vancouver-Capilano.

"The United States is getting a message tonight. Our leader has the support of the Canadian people," Liberal lawmaker Hedy Fry told the Canadian Broadcasting Corp. in an interview.

Cross-border trade negotiations broke down on Aug. 21 after negotiators failed to reach a compromise, leading Trump to enact 50% tariffs on approximately $20 billion of Canadian exports. Canada countered by announcing intended tariffs on U.S. goods.

Trump has broadened his attacks since the negotiations broke down.

He signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America," while U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent remarked Monday that Canada has sparse leverage because the U.S. economy is roughly 13 times larger.

Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’ ( Getty )

Trump has frequently floated the idea of absorbing Canada as the 51st U.S. state.

Carney has consequently accelerated efforts to build stronger trade partnerships with Europe and other international allies.

The three victories bring the Liberal caucus to 173 seats in the 343-seat House of Commons, solidifying the party's position in Parliament. The special elections were prompted by lawmaker resignations earlier in the year.

Daniel Béland, a political-science professor at McGill University, suggested the strong Liberal performance in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord stemmed partly from local backing for Carney’s Aug. 21 choice "to pull the plug on trade negotiations with the White House."

Béland observed that the sharp drop for Conservatives creates trouble for party leader Pierre Poilievre. The Conservatives captured the riding with 34% of the vote last year, but dropped to roughly 13% on Monday. "These numbers do look bad," he said.

Carney won office last year amid widespread public indignation over Trump's annexation rhetoric, promising to lessen Canada's economic reliance on its southern neighbor.

News.title: Transfer deadline day LIVE: Arsenal miss out on Alvarez alternative, Enzo Fernandez to Man City, Liverpool latest
News.content:
Transfer deadline day has arrived with two of the biggest sagas of the summer still to be resolved: will Arsenal sign Julian Alvarez and could Enzo Fernandez be swapping Chelsea for Manchester City before tonight’s 11pm deadline?

Premier League champions Arsenal have pursued Alvarez all window but are running out of time to submit an offer to Atletico Madrid, despite selling Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to free up space for the 26-year-old forward. It means the Gunners could be left short in attack if they do not meet Atletico’s €150m asking price and so have explored alternatives – though they have turned down a possible deal for Malick Fofana. The Lyon forward is now set to join Crystal Palace, who hijacked Sunderland’s move.

Manchester City, meanwhile, will need to submit a bid that is higher than £120m to sign Fernandez from Chelsea and a deal is said to have now been agreed between the clubs. Fernandez has been left out of Chelsea’s last two squads but Xabi Alonso’s side want to ensure they have a suitable replacement lined up, with Monaco’s Lamine Camara top of their list and talks continuing over a £60m deal for the 22-year-old midfielder.

Manchester United have still not signed a left back, but have made swift progress over a possible deadline day deal for Leicester City youngster Louis Page, while Liverpool’s business appears done after signing Bradley Barcola and rejecting Manchester City’s approach for Cody Gakpo. City have agreed a £60m deal with Everton to buy Iliman Ndiaye. That could have an impact on Everton’s pursuit of Richarlison, with Tottenham still wanting to sign a new forward too.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

Sports.title: Matias Fernandez-Pardo seals £51m Newcastle transfer with Nick Woltemade set for deadline day exit with Juventus loan
Sports.content:
MATIAS FERNANDEZ-PARDO is Newcastle’s new No20 after completing his £51MILLION move from Lille.

The forward, 21, jetted to Tyneside on Monday and passed a medical late last night before penning a five-year contract at Toon.



The Belgian is in line to make his debut for Matthias Jaissle’s team at home to Bournemouth on Saturday after his move was confirmed on deadline day.

Fernandez-Pardo said: “I’m really, really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club.



“I spoke to the head coach and he really showed how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my own career progression, it made complete sense to come so I didn’t hesitate at all.

“I know the club, I know about the stadium, I know it’s a fantastic atmosphere. I’ve followed the team. What I’ve seen is a team that’s very ambitious, wants to attack, get forward, really chase teams and go after them, and that’s really something I want to take part in as well.



“I’m still young, I’m still hungry, and that’s why I’m here, and I want to make that progress with Newcastle. I can’t wait to start the wonderful adventure here.”

The deal completes a huge reset at St James’ Park following a major summer of change.

Things looked grim for Newcastle after the exits of head coach Eddie Howe and the sales of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes.

However, Fernandez-Pardo is the EIGHTH new signing and his ability to play anywhere across the frontline made him new boss Jaissle’s top target to fill the void left by Gordon.



Newcastle United head coach, Matthias Jaissle, said: “I am very happy to welcome Matias to our club.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal.

“Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage, and he has the ability to take players on.

“We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.



“He has already shown in Lille that he can perform on the big stage, and we will work closely with him to keep developing his game further.

“We are excited to see him in a Newcastle United shirt.”

Sporting director Ross Wilson, who has led Newcastle’s overhaul this summer, said: “Matias is a really important signing for us.

“As I said last week, we waited patiently on Nico Gonzalez, and this time we’ve done the same – only longer.

“Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way.



“Back in May, he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him.

“Now, at the end of the window, he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United, and we are excited to welcome him.

“A lot of hours went into this one, but we’re clear on our Newcastle United identity, and Matias, at 21 years old, has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance.

“We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him, and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.



“I’m confident that with Matthias Jaissle and our staff, he will strongly develop and continue to grow here in Newcastle.”

Fernandez-Pardo’s arrival gave Toon’s flop record signing Nick Woltemade the green light to join Juventus on loan.

The striker, 24, faded after a bright start with the Mags following his £69m arrival from Stuttgart 12 months ago.

He will look to resurrect his career in Italy after the Serie A giants agreed to pay £3.5m and cover the giant German’s wages.



Though the loan deal does not include either an option or obligation for Juve to buy him permanently.

Meanwhile, Newcastle rejected a £15m deadline day bid from Nottingham Forest, who had an initial £10m bid turned down last week, for winger Jacob Murphy.

Newcastle’s longest-serving player, who arrived from Norwich in 2017, has entered the final 12 months of his contract on Tyneside.

Wilson is well-aware of the need to make financially prudent decisions and knows the veteran could leave for nothing next summer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, new boss Jaissle does not want to lose Murphy’s experience and leadership from his youthful squad rebuild.



Talks could now take place over a potential contract extension.

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus reveals he took ‘significant pay cut’ to £200,000-a-week Arsenal wages to seal Barcelona transfer
Sports.content:
GABRIEL JESUS has revealed he spoke with his former Manchester City team-mates Joao Cancelo and Rodri to get their views on joining Barcelona.

The striker, 29, has moved to the Spanish club for a £8.6m plus add-ons after Arsenal cashed in on him.



Jesus will join forces with his Brazil team-mate, Raphinha, at the Nou Camp and is reunited with his former City colleagues Cancelo, Rodri and Eric Garcia.

He said: “I spoke to them and they all told me good things, about the club, about the dressing room and about the staff.



“A week ago, when I received the message that it (a move to Barcelona) could happen, I was happy and had confidence in what could be done. When I saw that it would become a reality, I was very excited.

“These things happen in life. I don’t believe too much in coincidences. I was working and training hard, with the utmost respect, because I knew something good would happen to me.”



Jesus has also confirmed he took a pay cut after being on over £200,000-a-week at Arsenal.

The Brazilian added: “Not only me, but Barca also made a great effort to make this signing happen.

“I took a significant pay cut, but it’s a dream to be here at Barcelona.”

Asked about being Barca’s second choice after they chased Julian Alvarez, he replied: “It doesn’t bother me when they say I’m just another option.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“It offends me when they say I’m a bad guy. It bothers me not to play. I have a real opportunity to be at Barca.”

Five-time Premier League winner Jesus watched from the stands at the Camp Nou last night as Hansi Flick‘s side ran out 5-2 winners against Rayo Vallecano.

Two goals each from Raphinha and Lamine Yamal and a Jules Kounde strike meant Barca made it three wins from three in La Liga so far.

Jesus’ international colleague Raphinha was the star of the show playing as an unorthodox number nine, similarly to the way Ousmane Dembele plays for PSG.



The exhilarating Yamal played to the right, with summer signing Anthony Gordon, who registered another two assists to make it four assists in his first two matches for Barca, on the left.

Hansi Flick’s side needed reinforcements up top following the departures of Ferran Torres to PSG and Robert Lewandowski to Chicago Fire this summer.

It looks now as though those voids will now be filled by Jesus, and 18-year-old Egyptian striker Hamza Abdelkarim, who replaced Raphinha late on last night.

In 2016 whilst at Palmeiras, Jesus said it was his “dream” to one play for Barcelona at a time when his hero Neymar was playing at the Camp Nou, and he is now about to fulfil that dream.

Sports.title: Biggest transfer deadline day signings ever, from Mesut Ozil’s move to Arsenal to Cristiano Ronaldo’s return to Man Utd
Sports.content:
TRANSFER deadline day always brings the drama.

And in the final moments of the summer window, the Premier League’s top clubs are desperate to add to their squads.



As the clock ticks towards it closing, we’ve seen some spectacular last-minute moves made by the likes of Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea and more.

SunSport looks at the biggest transfers that have happened before the transfer window slammed shut.



Mesut Ozil

The German playmaker was recognised as one of the best No10’s in world football at Real Madrid.

So, it presented a major coup for Arsenal when they managed to lure him to the Emirates in 2013 in a £42.5million deal.



He claimed an assist on his debut against Sunderland, and registered 53 more in 184 Premier League games for the Gunners.

Ozil was also named Arsenal’s Player of the Season in 2015-16.

Cristiano Ronaldo

It was the homecoming all Man Utd fans wanted.

After 12 years, and spells at Real Madrid and Juventus, Ronaldo returned to Old Trafford in 2021.



A brace on his second debut against Newcastle set the tone, while a hat-trick against Spurs was another season highlight.

He managed 18 Premier League goals on his return, at 36, which was very credible.

However, a fallout with then United manager Erik ten Hag saw Ronaldo bombed out of the club a season later.

Wayne Rooney

He was the most wanted teenager in world football, thanks to his exploits with Everton.



That prompted Sir Alex Ferguson to spend £27million on the then-18-year-old in 2004.

And boy was that money well spent.

He won 13 major trophies including five Premier League titles, four League Cups and the Champions League, the FA Cup, Europa League and FIFA Club World Cup once.

Rooney also became the club’s all-time top scorer with 253 goals, surpassing Bobby Charlton’s longtime record.



Ashley Cole

One of the biggest, and arguably most controversial, saw England star Cole swap Arsenal for Chelsea in 2006.

It was a dragged out saga that eventually saw the Blues pay the Gunners £5million and swap William Gallas.

The deal was finalised so late that it was officially announced roughly 90 minutes after the midnight transfer deadline had passed.

Cole would lift the Premier League with Chelsea, as well four FA Cups, the Champions League, and Europa League.



Dimitar Berbatov

Back in 2008, United managed to squeeze Berbatov over the line for £30.75million.

The languid Bulgarian striker became a crowd favourite at Old Trafford, sharing the Golden Boot during the 2010-11 season with Carlos Tevez.

He would go on to score 56 goals for United in 149 games for the club.

Better still, he won two Premier League titles, the League Cup and the Club World Cup in his four seasons at Old Trafford.



Cole Palmer

The most recent standout deadline day signing at the time saw Palmer swap the Etihad for Stamford Bridge.

At the time, the £40million fee Chelsea paid Man City in 2023 looked like good business.

But Palmer has now established himself as one of the great mavericks of the Premier League.

He scored 22 goals in his debut season, and scooped up the 2023-24 Young Player of the Season award,



Claude Makelele

A man so good he practically invented the defensive midfielder position.

Makelele was a shock signing for Chelsea from Real Madrid in 2003 for around £17million, as Roman Abramovich’s era began to shake up English football.

The France legend was the midfield conductor for the Blues team that won the Premier League in 2004-05 under Jose Mourinho.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His work, sitting in front of the back four, helped Chelsea concede a miserly 15 goals in during that campaign.



They would claim back-to-back titles, while Makelele would also add two League Cups and the FA Cup to his medals cabinet.

Sports.title: Arsenal confirm Fabio Vieira transfer exit as Gunners prepare to flog four attackers in £75million deadline day firesale
Sports.content:
FABIO VIEIRA has joined Hamburger SV from Arsenal on a permanent deal.

On deadline day, the Gunners released a statement wishing the 26-year-old the best of luck in the Bundesliga as they look to tick off the regulatory processes.



Meanwhile, 19-year-old Ethan Nwaneri is all set for a season-long loan to German giants Borussia Dortmund.

The Arsenal academy product agreed to the club-to-club agreement on Monday night ahead of the transfer doors slamming shut.



Dortmund are set to hand the youngster more regular first-team minutes and Champions League football.

Gabriel Jesus is another name on the outgoing list, having landed in Barcelona on an £8.6million switch – which could be worth more in add-ons.

And last but not least, Gabriel Martinelli is set for a medical ahead of a £60m switch to Saudi’s Al-Hilal.

The fourth forward exiting the Emirates brings the final day total to around £75million.

Vieira joined the North London outfit from Porto in June 2022 and has since made 49 appearances for the title-winning side.

He returned to the Primeira Liga club – his boyhood team – for the 2024/25 season, before heading to Hamburger for the following campaign.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In the German top-flight, the ace scored seven goals and provided five assists as they found themselves back in the Bundesliga after seven years.

And in England, he even thundered home the winning penalty that saw Arsenal win the 2023 Community Shield, following a 3-1 win over Manchester City.

Arsenal’s transfer window has been making headlines, from their success with Bruno Guimaraes to their huge loss with Vinicius Jnr.

The Gunners saw the former Newcastle skipper walk through the door for £75m after a nervous few weeks.



Meanwhile, Ezri Konsa joined from Aston Villa for £51m and Christos Tzolis joined from Club Brugge on a £34m deal.

Sports.title: England legend’s son, 20, joins Sheffield Wednesday with dad still playing in star-studded Sunday League team
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY talent Jaden Heskey has made a deadline day return to Sheffield Wednesday.

The midfielder, 20, could not stop the Owls suffering relegation to League One when he spent the second half of last season at Hillsborough.



And Heskey has been sent back on loan to Wednesday for the rest of the season.

The up-and-coming gem revealed he was only interested in making a quickfire move back to the Owls in the final hours of the transfer window.



Heskey said: “I’m over the moon to be back after I got a taste of it last season. It’s definitely a place that I wanted to return to.

“It was really tough with the games and the situation that we were in, but I think the fans, the support that we had all the way through, it couldn’t really go unnoticed.



“The last day was a special day that I’ll always remember. I’ve already met the squad, and they’re really top lads. It’ll be easy just to fit in with the squad again.”

Heskey, who made 20 appearances for Wednesday during his initial loan move, could feature in tonight’s League One showdown with Wycombe.

Owls sporting director Simon Wilson claimed the City youngster snubbed offers from elsewhere to reunite with boss Henrik Pedersen.

He added: “Jaden was a target for the club from the day I arrived following a really productive loan spell last season.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“We are delighted that, after considering a number of offers, he has chosen to return to Sheffield Wednesday.

“Henrik and the staff felt he was one of the players who developed most during that period and the additional analysis we have done only strengthened that view.

“He joins what we believe is a terrific group of players competing for selection in midfield and brings different attributes that complement what we already have.

“More than anything, when he arrived this morning, what struck me was how quickly he had the whole training ground smiling.

“He is a hardworking, positive person who is desperate to do well for Wednesday, and we are really pleased to have him back.”



Heskey made his City debut with brother Reigan in a Carabao Cup win over Huddersfield Town last September.

And his dad, Emile, is still lacing up his boots in a star-studded Sunday League side at the age of 48.

The England legend is part of a Wythenshawe Vets side which includes Premier League icons Antonio Valencia, Danny Drinkwater, Papiss Cisse and Joleon Lescott.

Sports.title: Viral footballer Tara Mae Kirk channels inner Paris Hilton with defiant message to critics
Sports.content:
TARA MAE KIRK has channelled her inner Paris Hilton with a defiant message to her critics after another one of her social media posts went viral.

The West Brom star shared a video of herself wearing the Baggies training kit while Azealia Banks‘ 212 played in the background.



She had a very particular message for anyone who isn’t enjoying the ride.

The video featured the words: “If you’re not having fun, then just leave. That’s hot.”



Kirk mimed along to the words before flashing a peace sign at the camera and moving in for a close-up.

She also added the text: “proof of life after 12 million views on X lol” on the post.

Her caption was even more telling as it read: “In the words of Paris Hilton 🤷🏻‍♀️”

The quote is one of Hilton’s most famous pieces of advice, originally delivered while discussing 2000s fashion, nightlife and maintaining a positive attitude.

It has since become a popular social media line, often paired with Hilton’s iconic “That’s hot” catchphrase.

Kirk’s followers clearly approved of the message.



One fan wrote: “your beautiful 😍❤️”

Another posted: “Worldie ❤️”

A third simply declared: “Our Goat Tara”

Kirk, 23, has amassed more than 66,000 Instagram followers, with her online popularity exploding during her spell at Peterborough.



She joined the Baggies in February after four years with Peterborough, where she became something of a cult figure in women’s football.

In February, she spoke of her online presence and revealed: “I was going through the comments and trying to understand what all this hype is.

“I understood quickly that it was positive, but also crossing the line of borderline being sexist and sexualising me.

“So, yeah, it’s kind of balancing the good with the bad. That’s what I’ve had to learn.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kirk has since continued to embrace the positive side of her huge following while making a name for herself on the pitch.

Now, with another viral moment under her belt, the Baggies star appears determined to keep enjoying herself.

Sports.title: Why is Scott McTominay having heart surgery and when will he return to action?
Sports.content:
SCOTT MCTOMINAY will undergo heart surgery for a “mild benign arrhythmia”.

Napoli confirmed the news and the Scotland midfielder will be sidelined for a short period.



Why is Scott McTominay having heart surgery and what is mild benign arrhythmia?

Mild benign arrhythmia is described by the NHS as “when your heart beats too quickly or too slowly, or your heartbeat is not steady”.

To fix the issue, McTominay will undergo cardiac arrhythmia ablation.



The treatment involves heat or cold energy being used to create tiny scars in the heart.

This blocks faulty signals and restores a typical heartbeat.



Mild benign arrhythmia is not considered serious or life threatening.

When will Scott McTominay be able to play again?

Napoli expect the former Manchester United midfielder to be playing again after the upcoming international break.

However, this means he will miss Scotland’s upcoming matches, which are the first under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

The Scots play Slovenia twice, Switzerland at home and North Macedonia away in the Nations League.



McTominay will also not play as Napoli welcome Arsenal in their Champions League opener on Wednesday, September 9.

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott could still have a Liverpool future - but he had to leave this summer
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott could still have a Liverpool future - but he had to leave this summer

Harvey Elliott is joining Valencia on loan after Andoni Iraola said he preferred other options but he will still be hoping there is a chance his Liverpool career is not finished

View 3 Images Harvey Elliott will be playing for Valencia in La Liga this season (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Even for the traditionalists who become exasperated by the number of personnel in a Premier League dug-out nowadays, Mikel Arteta makes a compelling argument for expanding the number of players allowed in a matchday squad.

‌



The limit currently stands at 20 - it is 23 in Spain and 25 in Italy - and a Premier League club can register a squad of 25 senior players (those aged over 21). Assuming everyone is fit, the equation is simple. Five senior players have to be told they are not involved on a Premier League matchday.

‌



And that has happened to Harvey Elliott a lot in recent times. In fact, it happened most of the time when he was on loan at Aston Villa.

‌



Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

When it happened in the first two games of Andoni Iraola’s management at Liverpool, the writing was on the wall. Elliott is one of those players who might benefit from an expansion in the size of matchday squads.

‌



“I can only pick 20,” Iraola said recently. “I think it is a matter of finding balance on the bench. In Harvey’s case, I think he is trying. He is improving every week but I still prefer other options.”

At best, Elliott would have been very much a fringe player under Iraola. He would probably have had more of a chance of getting a game than he did at Villa, where Unai Emery essentially froze him out.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola said he preferred other options to Harvey Elliott (Image: Molly Darlington, Getty Images)

‌



But his loan move to Valencia is the right course of action for the player and a great opportunity for Elliott to prove himself an elite talent. His lack of game-time under Emery was linked to Villa not wanting to trigger a £35million obligation-to-buy clause.

That in itself was a blow to Elliott’s esteem. He would have rated himself as a player worth £35million in today’s market. And that Iraola has not been convinced by the 23-year-old’s value - just as Arne Slot was most certainly not convinced - has been another blow to Elliott.

But a crack at life in La Liga is an ideal way for Elliott to re-establish himself as a player with the potential to be a marquee operator. The loan deal represents a significant financial commitment by Valencia and he will be seen as a key player by manager Carlos Corberan.

‌



View 3 Images Harvey Elliott was barely given a chance by Unai Emery in his loan spell at Aston Villa (Image: Molly Darlington, Getty Images)

His debut is likely to come in Sunday’s La Liga game against Barcelona at the historic Mestalla Stadium, and Elliott has the sort of technical qualities that should help him thrive in Spain. It seems there is no obligation-to-buy clause in this loan deal and nor is there an option to buy.

Elliott’s confidence - of which he seemed to have plenty early in his career - has surely taken a hit over the past couple of seasons but this is a chance for him to rebuild that self-belief.

Article continues below

His Liverpool contract does not expire until 2028 and if he can play a major role in helping Valencia improve on last season’s ninth-placed La Liga finish, there is every chance he can still forge a future at Anfield.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 23 deadline day signings ranked including Chelsea surprise and three record-breakers
Sports.content:
Arsenal have been busy this summer, but there could be more to come from the Gunners. Mikel Arteta has added nearly £200m worth of talent to his squad and might not be done just yet.

Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and Ezri Konsa have all joined for big money, with Hincapie joining after a year on loan. Links with Julian Alvarez aren't going away, while others continue to be linked during the dying embers of the window.

If there's more late business, it would be the 24th time Arsenal have made a deadline day signing since the transfer window system was introduced in 2002. That's not including those who initially joined the academy rather than the first team.

There's been a real mix, however, when it comes to whether those late arrivals succeeded or failed. We've ranked them from worst to best.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta cites Aston Villa moment as the inspiration behind Arsenal's win READ MORE :

23. Emiliano Viviano (Palermo, loan).

Italian goalkeeper Viviano arrived on a season-long deal from Palermo but didn't manage a single minute. Wojciech Szczesny and Lukasz Fabianski blocked his path and he quickly returned to his home country.

22. Cedric Soares ( Southampton, loan)

Cedric never looked like a great fit and Arsenal wasted little time seeking a better full-back option. Somehow stayed on the books for four years without ever threatening to be a regular.

21. Raheem Sterling (Chelsea, loan)

Sterling joined from Chelsea in a surprise switch but couldn't find his best form. A return of just one goal made this a calculated risk but one which didn't bear fruit.

‌



20. Kim Kallstrom (Spartak Moscow, loan)

Swedish midfielder Kallstrom was injured when he joined and only returned late in the season. Still, he enjoyed his time at the club and scored an emotional penalty in a cup semi-final shoot-out.

View 5 Images Kim Kallstrom's Arsenal spell was short-lived (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

19. Andre Santos (Fenerbahce, £6m)

The Brazilian was a figure of fun at times but also earned cult hero status thanks to a goal against West Brom in May 2012. The effort was enough for Arsenal to clinch Champions League football at Tottenham's expense on the final day of the season.

‌



18. Lassana Diarra (Chelsea, £2m)

French midfielder Diarra had the opportunity to make an impression before departing. Arsenal turned a quick profit by sending him to Portsmouth but his success on the south coast may have had some wondering if he should have been given more time.

17. Julio Baptista (Real Madrid, loan)

The Brazilian forward joined via a loan exchange that saw Jose Antonio Reyes move to Madrid. He never really got going in the Premier League action but will be remembered for his part in a 6-3 League Cup victory over Liverpool.

16. Yossi Benayoun (Chelsea, loan)

Israel international Benayoun failed to secure a permanent switch after his loan spell. Enjoyed some encouraging moments, however, netting six goals across all competitions including four in the league.

15. Kieran Tierney (Celtic, £25m)

Scotland defender Tierney was great at times but injuries prevented him from making a greater mark in North London. Spent a year on loan in Spain and has now returned to Celtic.

‌



View 5 Images Injuries limited Kieran Tierney's involvement for Arsenal (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

14. Denilson (Sao Paulo, £3.4m)

Another Brazilian on the list, Denilson might have had more of an Arsenal career were it not for the emergence of Jack Wilshere. Made a real impact as a teenager in tough circumstances but eventually saw his time in England come to an end.

13. Takehiro Tomiyasu (Bologna, £16m)

The Japan international laid the framework for what a defender in a Mikel Arteta team looks like. He excelled when available but struggled with injuries and is now back in the Premier League with Crystal Palace after a stint at Ajax.

12. Jorginho (Chelsea, £12m)

Italy midfielder Jorginho helped Arsenal come close to the title in 2023 but the Gunners fell short. He was a big character off the field as well as on it.

‌



11. Thomas Partey (Atletico Madrid, £45m)

The Ghana midfielder was a big-money arrival from Atletico Madrid and had highs and lows on the pitch during his five years in England. Returned to La Liga with Villarreal in 2025 and is now in Saudi Arabia.

10. David Luiz (Chelsea, £8m)

View 5 Images David Luiz was one of a number of deadline day arrivals from Chelsea (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Yet another Brazilian, the centre-back played his part in the first trophy win under Arteta in 2020. Had some tough moments but showed his value on the pitch and in the dressing room.

9. Danny Welbeck (Man Utd, £16m)

A difficult departure for some United supporters and a well-received signing in North London. Was never prolific for Arsenal but delivered some big moments and is remembered fondly by a number of fans despite his numbers in front of goal.

‌



8. William Gallas (Chelsea, part-exchange)

The Gunners captain's behaviour at Birmingham in 2008 has overshadowed some of his better moments. However, there was good as well as bad after he arrived from Chelsea as part of the infamous Ashley Cole deal.

7. Andrei Arshavin (Zenit, £15m)

Signed a few months after impressing for Russia at Euro 2008 in what was then a record deal for Arsenal. Faded in his later years amid injury issues but will always have those four goals at Anfield.

6. Nacho Monreal (Malaga, £8.5m)

A bargain for a player who served the club admirably for the better part of a decade. Spain international Monreal became part of the furniture and played more for Arsenal than for any other club.

5. Piero Hincapie (Bayer Leverkusen, loan)

View 5 Images Arsenal continued their deadline day business by signing Piero Hincapie in 2025 (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



The Ecuador star has already done what he was signed for by helping Arsenal win the league, having done the same with Leverkusen. He could have a bigger role to play this term after joining permanently.

"When I spoke to Xabi just before we were going to sign him, I said if you have to describe him in one word, what would you use, and he said, 'He’s a warrior,'" Arteta told TNT Sports last season. "He will play through brick walls for you, and he’s one of the most competitive players that I have had.

4. Per Mertesacker (Werder Bremen, £8m)

A leader on and off the pitch. Mertesacker lifted Arsenal out of the doldrums in the latter half of the Arsene Wenger era and played a huge role after hanging up his boots.

In his role as academy manager, the German helped lay the groundwork for the likes of Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly to earn their place in the first team. There aren't many who have that kind of impact.

‌



3. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (Borussia Dortmund, £56m)

Another January deadline-day deal: Aubameyang followed his former Dortmund colleague Henrikh Mkhitaryan through the doors at Arsenal. The Gabonese international arrived in a club record deal and provided some star power.

The striker finished one season as the Premier League's top scorer and another as a cup winner after scoring both goals for Arteta's team in the final. The way things ended for him in North London shouldn't cloud that.

2. Mesut Ozil (Real Madrid, £42.5m)

The excitement around Arsenal when Ozil joined from Real Madrid will live long in the memory. The German creator was a really special player for a number of years, even if he couldn't help deliver a league title.

As with Aubameyang, the then-record signing left under a bit of a cloud. However, when he was good there were few in the league who could come close to him.

‌



1. Mikel Arteta ( Everton, £10m)

As with Mertesacker, Arteta's position is elevated by what came after he retired. What an impact, though.

There were plenty of positives on the field and in the dressing room, with Arteta providing leadership when it was needed most. Since he returned as manager, though, there has been so much more.

Sports.title: Arsenal set for timely transfer boost as two Premier League deals agreed
Sports.content:
Arsenal set for timely transfer boost as two Premier League deals agreed

Arsenal are not expected to welcome many new faces to the Emirates Stadium on deadline day but it could still prove to be an exciting one with a number of former Gunners on the move

View 2 Images Arsenal are set to see their coffers boosted on deadline day (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are set to bank around £9m on deadline day with a number of their former academy stars set for moves. The Gunners have had a busy summer transfer window this summer, having spent around £150m on new signings.

‌



Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincapie have all arrived for considerable fees. And with the transfer window coming to an end on Tuesday, attention has now turned to sales.

‌



Leandro Trossard, Jakub Kiwior, Fabio Vieira and Christian Norgaard are among those to have left, while Brazilian duo Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli are expected to switch to Barcelona and Al-Hilal respectively. Once those moves go through, that will see Arsenal bank over £100m in sales this summer.

‌



But the good news doesn’t stop there for the North London side, they are also set to boost their coffers due to prior agreements. Academy graduate Folarin Balogun is closing in on a switch to Everton.

Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Arsenal slotted a 17.5% sell-on clause into the deal, which will see them claim around £6.7m of his total £38.5m fee. Meanwhile, Brooke Norton-Cuffy is also expected to complete a £12m move from Genoa to Hull City before the end of the window, which will see the Gunners bank around £2.4m in total.

That news will certainly be welcomed by Mikel Arteta, who has suggested that his side need to balance the books. He said: "That's what we are trying to get as a club but the balance has to be right.

“There are areas that we have to improve to hit those numbers. And if it's not with sales, because maybe we don't want... We have to sell what we want to sell as well, not just to sell.

‌



"And then when we want to sell as well, we have to be very careful because some of the assets, after maybe they grow and we still want them.

View 2 Images Brooke Norton-Cuffy is set to join Hull from Genoa (Image: Getty Images)

“So maybe we can grow in other areas across the club as well. And commercially, we've done incredible. The fan base that we have is incredible. Our mass revenue is incredible. And there are other ways to grow and that’s the club's strategy.

‌



“But we want to improve in all of them, obviously, because it's going to give us a bigger room to be stronger financially."

While Arsenal will be boosted by their outgoings, they have already been met with frustration on deadline day, having been beaten to the punch by Premier League rivals Sunderland for Monaco’s Malick Fofana.
