Sports.title: Sky Sports News' deadline day coverage hits embarrassing new low as viewers switch off
Sports.content:
Sky Sports News' deadline day coverage hits embarrassing new low as viewers switch off

Sky Sports News has come under fire for its deadline-day offerings, with misplaced musicians and rhyming reporters forcing fans to change channels

View 3 Images Sky Sports News' deadline coverage has been ripped apart by viewers online (Image: Sky Sports News)

Viewers have made their feelings crystal clear as Sky Sports News' deadline day coverage hits a "new low." An appearance by a guitarist and reporter Gary Cotterill's bemusing live dialogue have subscribers up in arms.

‌



Sky Sports News was once a non-negotiable on deadline day. Presenter Jim White, who left Sky in 2021, would front their live programme, in which he'd cut to roaming reporters at training grounds and stadiums while donning his revered yellow tie.

‌



Unforgettable moments, like drive-by interactions with former Tottenham, Portsmouth and QPR boss Harry Redknapp, Peter Odemwingie's faux pas and Arsenal fans losing their minds as Mesut Ozil's arrival was confirmed, were nearly guaranteed each year.

‌



But with the broadcaster undergoing a handful of changes, it appears as though the glory days have passed, and its restructured coverage has not landed well with subscribers to its channels.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

UEFA rules block Arsenal from Champions League clause as deadline day deal nears READ MORE :

Man Utd’s private Lewis Hall transfer plan as Newcastle confirm price tag READ MORE :

As deadline day began on Tuesday morning, Sky Sports News enlisted the services of guitarist Ben Cipolla. Cipolla went viral during the World Cup with a song he wrote about England star Djed Spence, set to the tune of Bonnie Tyler's Total Eclipse of the Heart.

‌



Cipolla spoke to the channel's panel, including presenter Hayley McQueen and former Premier League striker Charlie Austin, before singing a new song about Liverpool recruit Bradley Barcola.

View 3 Images Cipolla's singing did not go down well (Image: Sky Sports News)

Barcola signed for the Reds on Monday in a blockbuster £123million deal from Paris Saint-Germain, and Cipolla commemorated the move with a song inspired by Crowded House's Don't Dream It's Over.

‌



It's safe to say those watching at around 8:30am were far from impressed. One claimed on social media platform X: "That channel has dropped right off a cliff."

Another concurred, writing: "Turned on Sky Sports News for transfer deadline and seen some p***k with a guitar. Turned it straight back off."

One more fan added: "Sky Sports News is one big joke these days. Deadline day used to be worth watching, but now it's just a gimmick." A fourth said: "Content from Sky Sports News hitting a new all-time low."

‌



But this song wasn't the only content that enraged subscribers. Cipolla also debuted another number about deadline day and some of the occasion's best moments. The lyrics included: "Deadline day is alive and kicking. So many deals, yeah, the clock is ticking."

In response to the song, a disgusted viewer wrote: "Genuinely the first time I've had to turn the television off out of pure second-hand embarrassment."

Reporter Cotterill, who was at Emirates Stadium on deadline day bringing fans updates about Arsenal's business, soon became the rotten cherry on top for some viewers.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Cotterill's antics were also criticised (Image: Getty)

When asked about any potential arrivals, Cotterill broke into song and, to the tune of Paul McCartney and Wings' Let 'Em In, sang: "No one's knocking at the door, no one's ringing the bell. No one's knocking at the door, no one's ringing the bell."

Cotterill then continued: "But then the fans are saying, 'If anybody does, open the door and let him in.'" One fan was particularly irked and wrote on X: "Who in their right mind would pay to watch that?"

Sports.title: Scott McTominay to undergo heart procedure as Napoli issue statement on ex-Man Utd star
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay to undergo heart procedure as Napoli issue statement on ex-Man Utd star

Former Manchester United star Scott McTominay has been a roaring success during his time in Italy but the Scottish midfielder is now set for a period on the sidelines

View 2 Images Scott McTominay has been a huge success in Naples (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Manchester United star Scott McTominay is set to undergo a heart operation to correct a 'mild arrythmia', Napoli have announced.

‌



A statement from the Serie A side on Tuesday read: "Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days. He will be available again after the international break."

‌



Fortunately, it has been suggested that the condition is not too serious, with a number of athletes suffering from it. It is not expected to impact his future career.

‌



McTominay, 29, is a product of the Manchester United academy and went on to make 255 appearances for the side following his breakout during the 2016/17 season. He netted 29 goals during his time in Old Trafford.

Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The Scottish midfielder moved to Napoli for £25m in 2024 and has gone on to enjoy a huge period of success in Italy, scoring 27 goals in 82 games, winning Serie A last season.

McTominay has also earned 73 caps for the Scottish national team and has scored 15 times. His most recent outing came for Napoli over the weekend, as they were beaten by Como at home. After the game, Napoli boss Max Allegri suggested that the midfielder had been suffering from blisters.

He said: “McTominay had some problems with blisters, so he’s been training on a limited basis. Hopefully, we can get him into the best possible condition as soon as possible.”

‌



View 2 Images Scott McTominay helped Napoli to the Serie A crown in his debut season (Image: Getty Images)

Napoli still have four more games to navigate before the first international break of the campaign, which has been scheduled later this year. They first take on Inter Milan this coming Saturday, ahead of a Champions League clash with Premier League champions Arsenal.

They then take on Bologna at home ahead of a showdown with Fiorentina. Napoli currently sit tenth in Serie A after a win and a defeat apiece from their opening two games.

‌



McTominay's first appearance back in the side could potentially come against Frosinone on October 10.

Napoli have endured a dramatic summer after finishing as runners up last term. They sacked Antonio Conte in favour of Allegri and have allowed the likes of Miguel Gutierrez, Romelu Lukaku and Giovanni Simeone to leave the club.

They have however been busy in the market, having signed Rasmus Hojlund permanently, while Chelsea's Benoit Badiashile has signed for the club on a season-long loan deal.

Sports.title: Man Utd hours away from failing to meet three transfer objectives in summer window
Sports.content:
Man Utd hours away from failing to meet three transfer objectives in summer window

Manchester United's summer business has centred around bolstering their midfield but several players who they were looking to get off their books remain

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has addressed his midfield issues - but other problems remain at Man Utd

Time is running out for Manchester United, who have completed the bulk of their transfer business, but have left boxes unticked ahead of the window closing.

‌



The Red Devils' major priority this summer was to bolster their midfield and they've spent £155million to do that. Michael Carrick has been backed with three new arrivals, all of whom have proven Premier League experience.

‌



That has been a key recent element in recruitment for United, who added Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha last summer after they'd been leading lights at Brentford and Wolves respectively.

‌



This summer Youri Tielemans arrived from Aston Villa. Andrey Santos signed from Chelsea and more recently Carlos Baleba has joined from Brighton. Baleba was on United's radar last summer but they were priced out of a move.

Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

‌



The recruitment decisions this summer, and 12 months ago, have left United with an attack that can cause the best teams problems and a midfield that, on paper at least, should be able to dictate games better than it has - but that has left certain individuals surplus to requirements.

Duo remain on books

After seeing Cunha, Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko arrive last summer Joshua Zirkzee was shunted down the pecking order. The Dutchman's career in Manchester has never taken off, despite a goal on debut, and last season he started just five league games.

The plan was to get him a new club, which ultimately suited United and the player, but a loan move to Juventus has broken down late in the day. Napoli have also expressed an interest given Zirkzee first made his name in Italy with Bologna, but United could be left with a situation where Zirkzee remains in Manchester.

‌



View 3 Images Joshua Zirkzee has been trying to find a route out of Manchester all summer (Image: (Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

The same could be said for Manuel Ugarte, who was going to be deemed surplus to requirements this season. United's new midfield trio, coupled with Kobbie Mainoo, are ultimately vying for two spaces in the starting XI. Ugarte was tipped to move on, but a knee ligament injury at the World Cup has curtailed plans to offload him.

It means both Zirkzee and Ugarte are looking like they'll remain in Manchester despite there being next to no minutes available for them given the depth that Carrick now has.

‌



No left-back signing

Alongside the midfield acquisitions, if the budget remained, United were hoping to land another left-back. Luke Shaw has been a regular in that position for years when fit, but is now into his 30s and was exposed for Ipswich's opener on Sunday.

Newcastle's Lewis Hall had been on the United radar, but after losing Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, they're refusing to sell anymore of their major stars. Any move would likely prove out of United's budget.

View 3 Images Newcastle have refused to entertain Lewis Hall's sale

‌



Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and youngster Jorge Salinas, who plays at Racing Santander, were also cited as possible targets but with just hours to go it looks as if United will miss out on adding any defensive reinforcements - but of course that could still change late in the day.

Gary Neville did concede that, despite the quality in attack, United's backline has the potential to cost them this season. He said: "I just would have liked to have seen Manchester United bring in a left back and a centre-back to advance the money from next season’s budget into this season and just make sure Michael Carrick is covered.

"So it’s not ideal. I’m shocked that Manchester United haven’t put at least one defender in. It would be perfect if they could find a left-sided centre-back that could play left back, but those players don’t tend to exist as much anymore."

Sports.title: Portsmouth legend Alan Knight dies aged 65 as tributes pour in for club icon
Sports.content:
Portsmouth legend Alan Knight dies aged 65 as tributes pour in for club icon

Portsmouth have paid tribute to club legend Alan Knight, who played for Pompey in all four professional divisions across four different decades before later returning as a coach

View 2 Images Alan Knight, who was a legendary goalkeeper for Portsmouth, has passed away (Image: Getty Images)

Portsmouth have confirmed the death of Alan Knight at the age of 65. The club legend died this morning, surrounded by his close family, after a battle with prostate cancer.

‌



Knight made his diagnosis public in October 2024, encouraging others to get tested should they notice any symptoms and raising awareness of the disease. The club helped raise £40,000 for prostate cancer charities last May with an Alan Knight XI drawing 8-8 with a Pompey Legends side at Fratton Park.

‌



He played 801 times for Portsmouth. Knight made more appearances for one club than any other goalkeeper in football history.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Pompey's statement says: "The word legend is often overused in football, but the fact that Alan was still known as 'The Legend' at Pompey more than 20 years after hanging up his gloves speaks volumes. He will be sadly missed by the Fratton faithful, teammates and all of us at the club who knew and loved him.

"Our thoughts are with Alan's wife Heather, his daughters Jade and Rebekah, and all his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, The Legend."

‌



The club also say they are setting up a book of condolence at Fratton Park.

View 2 Images Alan Knight, played 801 times for Portsmouth, has passed away

Born in the Balham area of south-east London, Knight joined Portsmouth aged 14 as an apprentice. He debuted two years later on the final day of the 1977/78 season and kept a clean sheet against Rotherham United as Pompey finished bottom of the Third Division.

‌



Knight played from them in all four professional divisions, winning promotion three times, including to the top flight in 1986/87. The goalkeeper also helped Portsmouth reach the FA Cup semi-finals in 1992.

They took the eventual champions Liverpool to a replay and only bowed out on penalties. Knight made his final appearance aged 38 in January 2000.

He is only second to Jimmy Dickinson, who played 845 times for Pompey, in appearances for the club. The goalkeeper was awarded an MBE for services to football in the 2001 New Year's honours list.

Knight went on to play three times for for Havant & Waterlooville before becoming Portsmouth's goalkeeping coach. He also worked in the same capacity for Aldershot Town, Bournemouth, the Major League Soccer side Dallas, Dorchester Town, Havant & Waterlooville and Horndean.

A short-term return to Portsmouth followed in 2013 under Guy Whittingham after leaving Dorchester. Later that same year he was appointed a club ambassador.

Sports.title: Arsenal dealt huge transfer blow as Malick Fofana agrees to join Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Arsenal dealt huge transfer blow as Malick Fofana agrees to join Premier League rivals

Arsenal had been eyeing a deadline day move for Malick Fofana but Sunderland have leaped to the head of the queue and secured a deal for the Lyon star

View 2 Images Malick Fofana is set for a move to Sunderland on deadline day

Sunderland have secured an agreement to sign Lyon winger Malick Fofana - who was also on Arsenal's radar on deadline day.

‌



The Gunners had identified the Belgian as someone they could go after late in the window as Mikel Arteta sought even more quality in the final third, but Fofana is now on his way to Sunderland. The 21-year-old has been granted permission to travel to undergo a medical ahead of signing a five-year deal at the Stadium of Light.

‌



Fofana had gone as far as to speak to Arteta, reports the Athletic, but Sunderland have stolen a march and will bolster their squad. Regis le Bris is having to prepare for a season in Europe, which will place more demand on their resources.

‌



Fofana has recorded two goals in six appearances for Lyon already this season - one of those coming in the second leg of the Champions League play-off defeat to Fenerbahce. Overall he has scored 19 goals in 83 appearances for the French side.

Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Fofana has long been linked with a move to England - Chelsea made a verbal enquiry for him and Everton held talks over a possible move last summer.

Sunderland have been in the market for more attacking talent and had eyed taking Jack Grealish on loan with his days at Manchester City seemingly numbered. Grealish himself wasn't keen on the move and will instead head back to Everton, where he spent last season.

Arsenal's interest in Fofana comes despite the wealth of attacking depth, which has been added to this summer with the signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. He has started both of the Premier League games so far with Bukayo Saka on the other flank.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta had been keen on adding the Belgian

That has left Arteta with the likes of Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke and Max Dowman as options he can call upon from the bench. The array of attacking talent has left some individual on the outer however and Ethan Nwaneri is poised to move to Borussia Dortmund on loan.

Gabriel Martinelli, who was integral when Arsenal first became a force under Arteta, has missed out on matchday squads this season and is poised for a record departure as he heads to Saudi Arabia. Gabriel Jesus, one of only two recognised strikers at Arsenal, is also due to leave.

Sports.title: Can GB and Ireland cause big Walker Cup upset and shock United States?
Sports.content:
Great Britain and Ireland look to end the United States’ Walker Cup dominance and claim a famous victory on home soil this week, live on Sky Sports.

A sell-out crowd is expected at Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland this weekend, where the hosts look to reclaim the prestigious trophy for the first time since 2015.

The two-day in event sees many of the world's best amateur stars compete, with Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy all past participants before going onto Grand Slam-winning careers.

Image: Rory McIlroy featured in the 2007 Walker Cup for Great Britain and Ireland

Which other big names have featured in the Walker Cup? Who is playing in this year's contest? Will Great Britain and Ireland manage a famous win? Here's everything you need to know ahead of the 2026 edition…

What is the Walker Cup?

The Walker Cup is a match play event held biennially, where the leading amateur golfers from the United States play against Great Britain and Ireland.

This year's edition from September 5-6 is the 51st in the event's history since launching in 1922, with two 10-man teams competing across 26 matches over the two days.

Who plays for Great Britain and Ireland?

Jack Whaley makes his Walker Cup debut after becoming just the third Englishman in history to win the US Amateur last month, while Luke Poulter - son of Ryder Cup legend Ian Poulter - returns for a second time.

Captain Dean Robertson has six members of the team that featured last year, including Amateur Champion Stuart Grehan, with Connor Graham, Poulter, Eliot Baker, Niall Sheils Donegan and world No 2 amateur Tyler Weaver the others to return.

Ben Bolton, Sam Easterbrook, Josh Hill and Whaley are the four rookies included.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Whaley chipped in on the opening hole of his US Amateur final victory

How strong are the United States?

The McCormack Medal winner Preston Stout headlines a stacked United States team, featuring seven of the world's top nine in the amateur game.

Miles Russell - who qualified for the US Open earlier this year with Tiger Woods' son Charlie as caddie - was among the automatic qualifiers, with last year's Amateur Championship winner Ethan Fang also included.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 17-year-old amateur Miles Russell got his dad to caddie for him on the final hole of the US Open at Shinnecock Hills

William Jennings, Josiah Gilbert, Ryder Cowan, Kihei Akina, Jay Leng, Stewart Hagestad and Tyler Watts are the others to feature in Nathan Smith's 10-man roster.

Where does the Walker Cup take place?

The 2026 edition takes place on a renowned links venue on the west coast of Ireland, with Lahinch Golf Club hosting the match for the first time.

The iconic venue has been dubbed the "St Andrews of Ireland" and previously hosted the 2019 Irish Open, won by Jon Rahm, as well as the 2024 Arnold Palmer Cup.

Seminole Golf Club (2021), the Old Course at St Andrews (2023) and Cypress Point (2025) have all been recent Walker Cup venues, while Bandon Dunes Golf Resort in Oregon (2028) and Prince's Golf Club in Kent (2030) will host the next two editions.

What is the format and how does scoring work?

There are two sessions of foursomes, each offering four points, before an eight-match session of singles on the Saturday and all 20 players featuring in singles on the final day.

Foursomes matches see two golfers from Great Britain and Ireland compete against a pair from the United States, with team members alternating between shots and each team using one ball.

Each match is worth one point, with 13.5 points across the weekend required for victory and 13 points needed for the United States to retain the trophy.

Why are the United States favourites?

The United States have dominated Great Britain and Ireland through the event's history, winning 40 of the 50 previous matches, with the visitors chasing a sixth consecutive victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the 2023 Walker Cup at St Andrews, where the United States claimed victory

Great Britain and Ireland last won the 2015 contest at Royal Lytham & St Annes, claiming a 16.5-9.5 victory over an American side containing Bryson DeChambeau. They have won nine Walker Cups, while the 1965 edition was tied.

Who has played in past Walker Cups?

The last Great Britain and Ireland team to win on away soil in 2001 contained current Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald, former US Open champion Graeme McDowell and Sky Sports Golf presenter Nick Dougherty.

The United States' 2007 line-up had Webb Simpson, Billy Horschel, Rickie Fowler and Dustin Johnson, where they faced a Great Britain and Ireland side featuring McIlroy and 2016 Masters winner Danny Willett.

Three-time major winner Padraig Harrington and Sky Sports' David Howell were part of the 1995 GB&Ire side that beat Woods and the United States, while Phil Mickelson played in the 1991 edition.

Justin Thomas and Max Homa both featured in 2013 against Matt Fitzpatrick with Scottie Scheffler, Collin Morikawa and Will Zalatoris all part of the record-breaking 19-7 win in 2017. Will some of this week's line-ups go on and enjoy future PGA Tour success?

Image: Matt Fitzpatrick watched his brother Alex Fitzpatrick play in the 2019 Walker Cup

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Jessica chases first success at Wolverhampton
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Tuesday with Flat action from Brighton, Lingfield, Ripon and Wolverhampton, live on Sky Sports Racing...

5.12 Wolverhampton - Jessica seeks first win

Pierre Bonnard's half-sister Jessica will look for her first win on her third start in the second race at Wolverhampton, the Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes.

The €200,000 yearling shares the same dam as the Ballydoyle Group One winner, as well as also being a half-sister to the Group Two-placed Crepe Suzette. Of the two Amo Racing runners, it is interesting David Egan is on her as she comes here off the back of a second-placed finish at Newmarket last month which reads well as the winner, Beguiled, is entered in the Fillies' Mile.

Phalanx Nation represents Archie Watson and is entered in the Redcar Two-Year-Old Trophy in October. This filly arrives here after finishing third on both starts and the form reads very well, but she has been off since May and will need to overcome that break if she is to make it third-time lucky.

Iris Olivia took a good step forward for her first run and looks potentially progressive with Rossa Ryan in the saddle.

2.50 Lingfield - Storm Force takes on three rivals

James Doyle travels to Lingfield to take the ride on Wathnan Racing's Storm Force who takes on three rivals in the Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes.

Richard and Peter Fahey send just their third runner in five years to Lingfield as Storm Force arrives off the back of a success at Southwell. The son of Starspangledbanner travelled like a dream in the hands of Doyle and was able to come home as he pleased. Another bold show is expected under the penalty.

Best of the rest is likely to be Gold Star Gazing who is chasing a first win on his fifth start. He has a rating of 77 but could need a bit extra to beat the Fahey horse.

Blazing Gaden has raced seven times over hurdles but was behind Storm Force on his Flat debut last time out, a first attempt over six furlongs. He should know more now.

3.10 Ripon - Lexington Boom and Roman Crystal feature

The third contest on a seven-race card at Ripon sees two previous winners Lexington Boom and Roman Crystal lock horns in the 21 Engineer Regiment Sapper Nursery Handicap.

Lexington Boom drops into nursery company for the first time on his fourth career start after winning well at Beverley last month and has gone up four pounds for that success, but there is scope for plenty more to come.

Last-time-out-winner Roman Crystal has seen the track five times, scoring just the once, but there is some substance to his form, having been behind Gimcrack winner Arapaho Gold on his second start at Thirsk. He led from pillar to post last time out at Ayr, knuckling down to win nicely in the end and another bold bid is expected.

Lady Dublin comes here top-rated, having won two of her last three starts, but after a below-par performance at Newmarket, she will need to resume her progress if she is to have a say here.

Sports.title: Pakistan's wholesale changes 'most shocking ever', says Afridi
Sports.content:
Former Pakistan captain Shahid Afridi has called the selectors' decision to make sweeping changes to the squad and remove head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed ahead of the third and final Test against England as the "most shocking ever".

Selectors have axed seven players, including wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, batter Imam-ul-Haq and spinner Ali Usman, after the tourists' 194-run defeat at Lord's left them 2-0 down with just one match to play, at Edgbaston from September 9.

Of the seven players to have been drafted in, five are uncapped at Test level, in Arafat Minhas, Mohammed Imran Jr, Said Baig, Mohammad Imran and Razaullah.

White-ball coach Mike Hesson will take charge following Sarfaraz's axing, while Ashley Noffke is now assistant coach after Umar Gul was also relieved of his duties.

Writing on social media platform X, Afridi said: "Not sure what is the logic or reasoning behind this decision!"

"Even the replacements make no sense - T20 players have been included for a Test match in England?

"What is this thinking and approach? Why has the coach been axed after five Test matches?

"This is the most shocking decision ever by a selection committee which includes so many experienced selectors."

Pakistan squad for third Test vs England at Edgbaston Babar Azam (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Abdullah Shafique, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ali, Muhammad Imran, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori (wicket-keeper), Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicket-keeper) Saim Ayub, Sajid Khan, Saud Shakeel, Shan Masood and Ubaid Shah

Cricinfo has reported that Misbah-ul-Haq has offered to resign from the selection committee, but the Pakistan Cricket Board has yet to accept his resignation

Pakistan, who have now lost 15 of their last 20 Test matches, have been bowled out for less than 200 in all four of their innings in the series so far, skittled for 171 and 135 in Leeds and then for 110 and 194 at Lord's.

Sports.title: Kone? Camara? Chelsea working hard to bring in Fernandez replacement
Sports.content:
Chelsea are working hard to line up a replacement for Enzo Fernandez before the transfer deadline.

On top of Monaco's Lamine Camara and Roma's Manu Kone, they are also looking at midfield options in the Premier League.

Chelsea's plan is to bring in one midfielder if Enzo Fernandez, who has made it clear that he wants to make the move to Manchester City, leaves.

Talks are ongoing over City's move for the Argentina international, but Chelsea will only do business on a replacement if they feel it improves their squad.

Chelsea close to agreeing deal for Roma's Kone

Image: Chelsea have agreed a deal with Roma to sign midfielder Manu Kone

Chelsea are close to an agreement to sign France midfielder Kone, but Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini is trying to keep hold of the player according to Sky in Italy.

A deal worth £52m was understood to have been discussed, with talks also advancing to see winger Jamie Gittens head in the other direction on loan.

Chelsea's negotiations continue for both Kone and Gittens, but Gasperini's reluctance to let Kone go is an obstacle to overcome.

Gapserini pushed for Kone to stay when he arrived as head coach and was instrumental in securing the France midfielder's immediate future there.

Roma are working on either AC Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana or Marseille's Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg to replace Kone.

Chelsea have bid rejected for Camara

Image: Senegal midfielder Lamine Camara

Meanwhile, Monaco have rejected a £38.5m (€45m) bid from Chelsea for Camara.

Chelsea are working hard to line up a replacement for Fernandez before the deadline.

On top of Camara and Kone, they are also looking at midfield options in the Premier League.

Chelsea's plan is to bring in one midfielder if Fernandez leaves.

Could Kone fill Fernandez shoes?

Analysis by Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

Kone has pedigree as a 19-cap France international who, at 25, and with his peak years still ahead of him, has already impressed in Italy, Germany and his homeland, demonstrating a capacity to adapt which could serve him well in the Premier League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink explains what Chelsea could expect from Manu Kone

The former Borussia Monchengladbach midfielder has good athleticism and technical quality. Like the player he is in line to replace at Chelsea, he can operate at both No 6 and No 8, although it is at the base of midfield that he is most comfortable.

That may suit Alonso given his favoured, three-at-the-back system leaves little room for the No 8 role in which Fernandez previously excelled for the club. It may also suit Kone, who can defend, pass and carry but doesn't offer the same level of attacking threat.

Fernandez thrived in that sense at Chelsea. The Argentina international contributed an impressive total of 16 goals and 11 assists in the last two Premier League seasons.

Chelsea might need to find those goals and assists elsewhere in his squad if he goes, with Kone, a player who has different strengths, having provided only two and five respectively in league games for Roma in the same timeframe.

now 10.59 EDT Righto, that’s it from me. Here’s Luke McLaughlin to chill with you through the next bit; peace out. Share

I’m expecting him to be deadly on the counter, but I’m not totally convinced he’ll be as effective against low blocks, and he also needs to improve his finishing. I’m a little surprised Andoni Iraola has signed someone to go in front of Rio Ngumoha, though I suppose this felt like too good an opportunity to pass up. Share

7m ago 10.51 EDT David Affengruber, Elche’s Austrian centre-back, is apparently on his way to join Fulham. He’ll have a lot of work to do, because his teammates have looked weak in that area thus far. Share

10m ago 10.48 EDT On Sky, they’re talking about Arsenal’s failure to sign an attacker, which is, I agree a problem – they lack elite quality in that area. They have, though, made one crucial acquisition: the Premier League trophy. The confidence finally winning it will give them will have a colossal impact on how they perform, and they’ve the added bonus of Liverpool and Man City in flux, while Chelsea and United probably aren’t quite ready. 18m ago 10.40 EDT Just get a load of this: Share

20m ago 10.38 EDT “The Premier League is absolutely bonkers transfer-wise,” reckons Terry from Newcastle. “It’s become an almost meaningless industry on its own. Fans crow about ‘winning’ windows but most don’t have a clue about the players their side is recruiting. Pardo from Lille, no idea. Gabriel Jesus must have some agent as well. On another note, please, could you mention this lovely project to keep the Joy, Hope and Positivity Kevin Keegan brought to Newcastle alive if you like?” As John Motson had it on Match of the Day” the eighties, “the little man was, quite simply, a big hero.” Share

29m ago 10.29 EDT “I don’t disagree with your comments on why Utd struggle to sell players,” says Mark Gillespie, “but I think the big factor you missed is that they were throwing over inflated contracts at players for most of the last 10 years. Players are under no obligation to take a pay cut, but buying clubs are under no obligation to pay over the odds in wages, so they look elsewhere. Even reducing transfer fees doesn’t totally fix that problem for Utd, because overpaying on wages can upset the wage structure for the buying club even if they make it add up on the one transfer by getting them for a lower fee.” Yes, agreed – there are hardly any clubs in the world able to afford Marcus Rashford, for example, which is the main reason he’s not been flogged to allow more incomings. View image in fullscreen Femi Azeez of Millwall who was recently named in the PFA Championship Team of the Year for last season. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock Share Updated at 10.49 EDT

The 20-year-old forward, who joined in January 2024 from River Plate, has made three City appearances and had previous temporary spells at Bayer Leverkusen and Girona, one of City’s sister clubs. Share

38m ago 10.20 EDT Or, put another way, it’s important not to be partisan about these things. If you don’t earn it, you shouldn’t be able to spend it, and even if you do earn it, there should be limits to what you can spend in favour of sporting fairness and integrity. Part of me is happy for fans of West Ham, Villa and Palace, who’ve got to see their clubs win European trophies, and part of me is saying well of course they have, almost how could they not – the second best side in last seasons’s Europa were Forest, who almost went down. Share

44m ago 10.15 EDT “There are aspects of what Villa has done that I’m not keen on,” writes Josef Crowther “the endless deals with Chelsea particularly… but do people like you think that Villa should just be happy to sell all their star players and not then spend the money they’ve received for those players? While also massively reducing the wage bill that we’ve received so much sanction for (not saying this was unjustified entirely). Do fans of teams like yours just think we should just know our place and going back to being a happy little mid-table team? Were you decrying the inequities of the Europa League when your team got to the final despite finishing 15th in the league that season?



Typical that these comments come from somebody who supports a club that has every possible advantage and privilege imaginable in the game but still seem to think that isn’t enough.” I think there’s a difference between a club spending money it generates itself, and spending money given to it by a billionaire owner. I’m surprised that’s controversial. On United, they got to the final of the Europa league by winning through the rounds – as far as I’m aware, that’s how these things work, and cup competitions are not impacted by league status. I also think United have paid out over £1bn in interest repayments, which does not, in my book count as “privilege” but, seeing as you semi-ask, I’m in favour of limits on spending and signings for all clubs, squad sizes too. Genuine question,” offers Ross Howarth. “Sure, something else is happening in the past few seasons which requires a different explanation, but in general the trend has been going on for 10+ years. Can’t sell players or get poor fees. Significantly less cash generated from youth sales. Missed out on Russian, Chinese, and now Saudi money. We know the club has been run incompetently ... but haven’t others too? Did Fergie completely destroy agent relations? What is going on? Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester United and Liverpool eye Kroupi? Vardy to Wrexham?
Sports.content:
The final day of the men’s transfer window is here, but there is still time for some rumourmongering, before a Supermarket Sweep-style trolley dash for 11th-hour signings.

Going wild in the aisles? Manchester United’s interest in a new left-back has been known all summer long, yet here they stand without one on the final day of the window. While many are claiming United’s business could be done, RB Leipzig’s David Raum, Fulham stalwart Antonee Robinson and Fenerbahce’s English left-back Archie Brown have all been mentioned as possible last-minute acquisitions. Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander has been tracked by United throughout the window and some are reporting that deal could be done today for €16m (£13.7m). Burnley are keen on United’s own youngster Harry Amass, but his departure may depend on a left-back coming in.

Speaking of United, remember Jadon Sancho? Well, the one-time £74m Old Trafford signing is still a free agent after his contract expired, with his former club Borussia Dortmund ready to take a chance on him providing he signs a heavily incentivised contract.

United and Liverpool are also credited with an interest in Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, though they may not have much time to press on with the transfer. Arsenal have also glanced admiringly in the direction of 20-year-old Frenchman, who is one of the jewels in the Cherries’ crown.

It appears Liverpool knocked back an audacious approach by Nottingham Forest for their young midfielder Trey Nyoni. The 19-year-old is rated highly by Andoni Iraola, and not even a £30m Forest bid tempted the Reds to sell.

Which midfielder will Chelsea sign if and when Manchester City’s pursuit of Enzo Fernández finally bears fruit? Alex Scott, Lamine Camara and Manu Koné have all been identified as targets for the Blues, but only one of those deals can feasibly be achieved on deadline day. Alternatively, is Eduardo Camavinga still attainable for Chelsea or someone else? Noises are coming out of Madrid suggesting Real could listen to offers of around £60m today.

Let’s move on to Everton, who look to have missed out on Richarlison and Stuttgart’s Jamie Leweling but should be able to bring Jack Grealish back on loan, as well as Kenny Tete from Fulham. Tim Iroegbunam is off to Hull and Iliman Ndiaye looks destined for Manchester City after their deal for Cody Gakpo hit the rocks.

The Championship is often where the juiciest deadline-day activity takes place, and Derby are battling Blackburn to re-sign Brighton defender Eiran Cashin on loan. Meanwhile, Wrexham, who were accused by Sheffield United’s Chris Wilder of “blanket bombing” in their bid to sign his player Callum O’Hare, are also considering Portsmouth’s Adrian Segecic and Bristol City’s Scott Twine, while an eye-catching free transfer for Jamie Vardy remains a possibility.

Sports.title: Barcelona breeze past Rayo but all eyes in Spain remain on Julián Álvarez
Sports.content:
If Raphinha has any misgivings about playing as a makeshift No 9 for Barcelona, he is doing a good job of hiding it. Julián Álvarez would have been proud of the Brazilian’s two neat finishes that inspired the Spanish champions to a 5-2 victory against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night, 24 hours before the transfer deadline. Lamine Yamal scored two wonderful goals of his own in a performance that reassured everyone he is back to his best. Add Anthony Gordon to the mix – impressive again in his link-up play – and you have a fluid, fearsome front three.

Yet after the departures of Ferran Torres, Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford this summer, there is no doubt Barcelona not only still want a centre-forward but require one – at least one. Hansi Flick was very happy to see Gabriel Jesus, an £8.6m arrival from Arsenal, in the stands. “He’s a top striker,” the coach said. But Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez is the ultimate prize.

While Mikel Arteta has apparently attempted to speed up a possible deal with a phone call to Álvarez, the Barcelona president, Joan Laporta, has conducted his interest largely in public. He stirred the pot again last Wednesday after Arsenal’s interest was firmed up. “This whole situation has created a lot of noise,” said Laporta, who specialises in creating a lot of noise, in a video on Barça’s social channels. “Atlético told us they were not selling [Alvarez]. However, it looks like, from what we hear now, they are trying to reach agreements with other clubs.”

Laporta left little to the imagination: “We are very interested in buying Julián Álvarez. We would like our offer to be accepted.” Atlético are not playing ball – and who can blame them? Barcelona’s courting of Antoine Griezmann, who announced he was staying at Atlético in a TV documentary in 2018 only to move to the Camp Nou in 2019, still leaves a sour taste. Again they have shown disapproval at Barcelona’s behaviour in their pursuit of Álvarez. “This situation isn’t about money, it’s about dignity,” an embattled Atlético said in a statement the day after Laporta’s video message.

After the hostile reception he received from Atlético’s fans at the Metropolitano when coming on as a substitute against Villarreal the previous weekend, Álvarez missed some training sessions and Saturday’s 3-1 win at Sevilla. Atlético said the striker was unwell. He returned to training on Sunday, with Arsenal appearing his only route out by the end of Tuesday – “there is zero consideration of an Álvarez transfer to Barcelona,” Atlético said.

Álvarez’s absence was felt keenly at the Camp Nou on Monday – for about 20 minutes. After some sloppy Barcelona finishing and an emphatic strike from Rayo’s Sergio Camello, a striker who came through Atlético’s academy, the headlines were obvious. But the narrative did not come to the rescue of the Rayo centre-back Pathé Ciss, who ended up on his backside after Raphinha skipped past him and slotted in the equaliser.

View image in fullscreen Gabriel Jesus gestures upon arrival at the airport in Barcelona on Monday. Photograph: Enric Fontcuberta/EPA

On an evening when Argentina’s footballers were writing Instagram posts about international retiree Lionel Messi, Barcelona’s current No 10 paid tribute in his own way. Lamine Yamal cut inside and whipped a shot past the flying Dani Cárdenas, high at his near post, to establish a lead that was never surrendered. After rumours about the 19-year-old’s fitness and wellbeing circulated after his sluggish start to the season, Flick reminded everyone that the kid had only three weeks’ holiday since beating Messi and Argentina in the World Cup final. Lamine Yamal was reaching his “top level” in training, Flick insisted, and it was hard to argue with him.

It was also hard to argue with Florian Lejeune when the Rayo defender said in a half-time interview that Barcelona “are very good”. Six minutes after the restart, he turned the ball into his own net. Gordon, the most expensive outlay at the Camp Nou this summer except perhaps for the new roof that is still under construction, provided the cross for that own goal and a great deal more from the left wing. The England forward’s selfless passing and running has quickly endeared him to supporters and there were chants of “Gordon, Gordon, Gordon” from behind the goal. His backheel set up Raphinha’s second and Barça’s fourth to make it three assists in three games.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha (right) celebrates scoring Barcelona’s fourth goal with Lamine Yamal. Photograph: Lluís Gené/AFP/Getty Images

After an hour of chasing after Pedri, Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal, Rayo’s midfield had to contend with Rodri off the bench. The marquee arrival from Manchester City did not have the chance to parade the World Cup he had won as Spain’s captain before his Barcelona debut in last Thursday’s win over Athletic . Barça snubbed the trophy presentation following a row over the arrest of one of their supporters who was carrying an Estelada flag – a symbol of the Catalan independence movement – outside the stadium before their season opener at Elche. Athletic’s Spain players had faced whistles from some Basque fans when they presented the trophy in Bilbao. Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella and Real Sociedad’s Mikel Oyarzabal were given a warm reception at the Bernabéu last week.

Lamine Yamal’s second against Rayo, another Messi-esque finish from the edge of the box, put the result beyond doubt. Barcelona and Real Madrid – the only teams with 100% records after three games – are yet to blink as the title race begins, but all eyes on transfer deadline day, you expect, will be on the exit door at Atlético’s training ground.

Talking points

While Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé were on the scoresheet in Real Madrid’s 4-0 home win against Málaga, it was the performance of Trent Alexander-Arnold that was perhaps most striking. The former Liverpool right-back was a creative force, setting up Madrid’s third for Mbappé, in his first start under José Mourinho. Mbappé, tipped for the Ballon d’Or by Mourinho last week, topped the scoring charts for a day or so after his sweeping finish from Alexander-Arnold’s low cross.

Thank you for your feedback.

Aside from Mbappé the most in-form striker in La Liga might be Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. The 37-year-old scored for the third game in a row as Deportivo beat Valencia 3-1 at Riazor for their first top-flight victory since 2018. Aubameyang could not suppress a giggle at the mention of Adama Traoré in a post-match chat with the media – his former Barcelona teammate has just signed from West Ham: “I’ve told him: ‘We are waiting for you.’”

View image in fullscreen Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang finds the net again for Deportivo. Photograph: Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images

Despite competition from Deportivo’s Bright Ede, who crossed the ball into his own box for Valencia to score, defensive mishap of the weekend goes to Matías Dituro. The 39-year-old Elche goalkeeper tried to juggle the ball into his own penalty area to pick it up but was beaten to it by Levante’s Yassir Zabiri, who poked in the first of a hat-trick in Racing Santander’s first win in primera since 2012. “Matías is a very daring goalkeeper. We had spoken to Yassir: I thought he could win the ball off him – and look how it turned out,” said Racing’s prophetic head coach, José Alberto.

Sports.title: ‘I was scared to tell my old teammates’: Victoria Pelova on making leap from Arsenal to Spurs
Sports.content:
There is not the same intensity to club rivalries between women’s teams as there is between their men’s counterparts, but as the game grows that is changing. Increasingly, there is animosity from fans if a player leaves for a rival side.

Victoria Pelova’s move from Arsenal to Tottenham firmly bucks the trend, though. Despite arguably having her best years ahead of her, the 27-year-old departed with a lot of well-wishes and love.

“I was really scared to tell my old teammates that I was going here,” says Pelova. “My close friends knew about it, obviously, but everyone responded so well. Everyone tells me that it reflects on the person I am. So, I’m actually really glad about that.”

Pelova has been an Arsenal fan favourite despite limited minutes in her three years at the club, during which she was hampered by an anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained on international duty in June 2024. Why is she so liked? She comes across as fun and is loved by her teammates, with a wicked and dry sense of humour.

Pelova was not worried what people would make of her move to Spurs, but the Netherlands midfielder did think about it. Ultimately, it was “an easy decision” to join Martin Ho’s squad.

“The way Martin approached me, what he said about how he sees me as a player, the videos he showed me and how he wants me to be, I’ve actually never had a coach talking like that about me,” she says. “So, for me, it was a good decision. I talked a lot with my mum about it and she immediately said yes. That was actually the most important thing for me, what my mum thought.”

At the start of June, Pelova shared online that her mum had died. A carousel of moving photos of the pair through the years was captioned: “Your biggest fear was leaving me behind. My biggest fear was losing you. Rest now, Mum.”

Pelova is not ready to talk about the loss, but it sits in the background of the interview. Not having to move home as a result of her leaving Arsenal was important. “It does really help me that I have friends and family around me that take care of me,” she says.

View image in fullscreen Pelova slides in on Chelsea’s Alyssa Thompson during Arsenal’s 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge in January. Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

Reflecting on her spell at Arsenal, with her ACL injury coming at a time when it was believed she would start to get more playing time, she says: “There was a private situation going on, my mum was ill, and I didn’t get minutes. So, it was a really tough time and people didn’t know what I was going through.”

The goal now? “To be happy again, in football and outside football, and just day by day see how it goes.”

She clarifies: “It sounds like I have not been happy, but I have been happy in the last year and in being with my friends. But when you’re not playing as regularly as you want to it’s inevitable that you’re not going to be totally happy, and when I’m the happiest person, I will be the best footballer I can be.”

The fresh start at Tottenham has been rejuvenating. “It’s nice to have no one know you. For me, that’s the way to go. I don’t know if I can explain it, but I feel like when everyone knows you, they focus on the things they know.”

Ho made an instant impression on Pelova. “All the coaches I’ve met are always like: ‘Oh, you can play there and there and there.’ Martin was like: ‘You’re this for me.’ He knew exactly where he wanted me and what he wanted from me. That, right away, set the tone for me and it was where and how I see myself as well. What I’ve seen so far is that he’s so detailed. He just wants to make you better. He’s very strict, but he wants to make you a better player and that’s why I’m here.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ho has “a lot” of confidence in her, and that is hugely freeing. “That’s the part I don’t have to worry about … and I can focus on other things.”

Pelova’s experience of Tottenham had been playing against them, and the more difficult that got, the more it contributed to her decision to join.

““Defending was so hard,” she says of facing Spurs last season. “So, I already liked the style Martin had the team playing. I also already know Caitlin Dijkstra; I’ve known her for eight years and we lived together in Amsterdam so we know each other so well. She’s like my sister. I know Lize Kop, they’re also one of my closest friends. So, that has made the transition easy because I can always rely on them.

“I’m quite social so I’ve been trying to get to know everyone, the youngsters. It’s quite a hard job in the beginning, it’s intense, but I like it. On the pitch, you’re building relationships, pre-season is always heavy, you just need to grind, but it has been good.”

Pelova has belief in herself and her body too. “We train really hard,” she says. “That’s different to what I’m used to. So, obviously it goes up and down, but I’m confident that in a few weeks everything as a team will have progressed so much. Always with new players, it needs time. I’ve been in football a really long time so I know how it goes.”

Asked about Tottenham’s chances of disrupting things at the top, she flips the question, then says she relishes being outsiders. “You need to put us on as underdogs. The underdog position is the place to be,” she says.

Now, Pelova is ready for the intensity of pre-season to end and for the games to begin at home against West Ham on Sunday. One, in particular, stands out, and it comes on 25 October at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. “Please, stop pre-season,” she says with a laugh. “I just want to start. I can’t wait to play against all the teams. I can’t wait to play against Arsenal.”

Sports.title: Janine Sonis: ‘63,000 fans in Denver proves a women’s team was way overdue’
Sports.content:
In the 13th minute of a 6-1 win against Chicago, Janine Sonis ran into the penalty area and stealthily positioned herself behind a line of defenders, before striking a crisp shot into the right corner. It was her ninth goal of the season, the most of any player Denver Summit player, and joint-seventh in the NWSL.

Now playing for her hometown team in its debut season, the NWSL and Canada veteran feels her happiness is translating on to the field. “I think it’s been a season that I’ve enjoyed myself more than any other season in my career, and I think that that’s showing in the way that I’m playing,” she said.

With family nearby, driving the same roads as when being driven to practice as a child, and captaining Colorado’s first women’s professional soccer team, Sonis said “it’s been, to be a little bit cliched, a dream come true to play here”, adding: “I didn’t think that Denver would get a professional women’s team while I was still playing. But it’s the 63,000 [fans at the team’s home opener at Mile Stadium], the fans that continue to show up for us every week, [it] proves the point that it’s way overdue.”

The versatile 32-year-old, currently playing at left-back, has had a profound influence on their smooth transition into the league, adding a positivity to her play and a decisive impact on and off the ball in a season when many of the scorelines have been narrow. Having experienced some of the league’s growing pains, she acknowledges the progress made since its inception, leading to a moment where debutante teams such as Denver have smoother introductions.

“I think we’ve hit a point where the expectation in every environment around the NWSL is so high, especially with the CBA [collective bargaining agreement] and what the CBA requires. And so I think it’s been just really cool for me to see the evolution of the league, and then to join an expansion team and see where the floor is. I mean, with a brand new facility, building a stadium, like where teams are coming into now is just so significantly different than when I first started out.”

View image in fullscreen Janine Sonis of Denver Summit: ‘I’ve enjoyed myself more than any other season in my career.’ Photograph: Andrew Wevers/NWSL/Getty Images

Denver have spent the season looking up at the playoff positions, slowly moving up the table with a consistency of effort leading to seven wins, six draws and eight defeats, with only two losses by more than one goal. After this weekend (when Sonis also marked her 10,000th regular-season minute in the competition), the Summit are sitting just below the playoffs in ninth, with nine regular season matches remaining.

On how to measure success for a league debutante, Sonis mentions the target of the playoffs, while noting myriad successes already achieved on and off the pitch: “It’s interesting because I think there’s two different answers. As a competitor, success to me is nothing less than making playoffs … We’re putting ourselves in incredible positions in games, we’re creating tons of opportunities, and we’re either drawing games or losing games by really small margins.” She added: “I think that we have already found success in a lot of ways, and we’ve built a really clear identity and clear playing style, and have built a a solid culture in the locker room with people that are very clear about the fact that they want to be here and compete for this club.”

On what it will take to break into the playoff positions, and stay there, in an infamously chaotic and tightly packed table, Sonis said: “Our attacking relationships and the way that we create opportunities, continuing to build those partnerships in the front line. I know as a full-back, a big part of our game is getting our full-backs into the attack, so putting in quality service and helping create for those attacking players. And I think we need to be very clear that it’s one game at a time. Right now, we’re looking at it as a kind of a five-game season, and doing the most that we can in those five games to put ourselves in the best position.”

Having the Champions League winner and fellow Coloradan Lindsey Heaps on hand after she returned from playing in Europe this summer is also a boost: “I don’t think that anyone can deny when someone with that résumé and presence comes into an environment that they wouldn’t have an immediate impact on the field, but even just the culture in the locker room, her professionalism, the way that she takes care of herself, the way that she speaks, is just so influential to not just our younger players, but for myself as well.”

What is Sonis’s favourite contribution of her own this season? A 94th-minute set-piece goal against the Utah Royals to secure a 2-1 win on 9 August. Of the well-rehearsed strike around the defensive wall, she said: “The free-kick was definitely special for me, just because I spend a lot of time working on them.” Defensively, she emphasized the difficulty of defending some of the league’s elite attackers, such as Sophia Wilson: “I think my favourite thing has just been learning and getting better, and and similarly seeing the fruit of my labor and studying how to be a better defender and the art of it … I’ve been really proud of the evolution of our backline across the season, and we’ve put in so much intentional work, and it’s been really nice to see that come to life.”

Other favourite moments include games at the Colorado Rapids Stadium, where she played her state championships in high school, and, of course, setting the NWSL attendance record with 63,004 fans at Mile High Stadium. Sonis: “I think there’s parts of it that felt like a fever dream.”
