Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 11: Manchester City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 1st (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st

Prospects

Champions again at last, after a 10-year wait, Manchester City now face an even tougher task: defending their title. They appear to have a good chance of succeeding, especially after keeping their star striker, Khadija “Bunny” Shaw. The WSL’s top scorer and best player of 2025-26 performed a dramatic U-turn by signing a new four-year contract in May rather than leaving on a free transfer, and that may prove crucial in continuing City’s positive momentum.

Their squad looks to be of a similar strength to last season. The Brazil forward Kerolin left for Barcelona but Beth Mead arriving from Arsenal in essence replaces her. Similarly, the exit of left-back Leila Ouahabi will be compensated for by the acquisition of Niamh Charles from Chelsea. Perhaps the only minor question is whether there is sufficient depth to sustain a challenge in the Women’s Champions League as well as domestically, but the core of regulars looks as formidable as any club in Europe.

The team scored plenty last term and had great success down the flanks, with the right-back Kerstin Casparij providing the joint-most assists in the division. Defensively they look solid. The most intriguing challenge could be psychological, as they switch from hunters to hunted, becoming the team that everybody wants to beat. They start at home to one of the promoted sides, Birmingham City, and first meet a fellow title hopeful – Arsenal – at the start of October, when they will aim to lay down a marker in the title race.

Off-field picture

Owned by City Football Group and led off the pitch by the managing director, Charlotte O’Neill, and director of football, Therese Sjögren, City enter the season with a new women’s team building at the training centre. The £10m building offers everything from underwater treadmills to a barista-style coffee machine in the canteen, with every element tailored towards maximising performance for female athletes. Previously the women’s team sometimes had to share a gym with City’s boys’ academy.

The manager

Andrée Jeglertz’s first season could scarcely have gone better, as he oversaw a league and cup double. He arrived in Manchester after a relatively uninspiring spell in charge of Denmark women but his CV is full of extensive high-level experience, including a 2004 European title with the Swedish club Umeå. The 54-year-old is a calm presence on the touchline, unwavering in his belief that his team will “find a way to win”, and has avoided controversy in press conferences, which he handles assuredly.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead joins the champions from rivals Arsenal. Photograph: Kate Green/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

Mead was the headline signing on a free transfer after nine years at Arsenal. City are hoping that the England forward – the Golden Boot winner and player of the tournament at the 2022 European Championship – is not past her best, at 31, and can flourish across a three-year contract. She is the all-time leading assist provider in the WSL. Mead also has 81 caps and will want to be part of any Lionesses squad at next summer’s World Cup.

Stat attack

If teams want to defend more effectively against the champions, they could start by focusing on free-kicks and corners. City scored at least twice as many set-piece goals as anyone else in 2025-26. As strong as they were elsewhere, this was their superpower.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

The 18-year-old full-back Sacha Lewis signed her first professional contract with City in August, having been with the club since under-14 level. The younger sister of the club’s men’s first-team full-back Rico Lewis, she has been a regular for England Under-19s and has been named in the England Under-20 squad that will go to Poland for September’s Women’s Under-20 World Cup. She was the player of the season for Manchester City’s “Next Gen” team last term and, with City juggling European and domestic football, may get a chance in the first team.

What they say

“Our biggest challenge this year is to continue winning and, at the same, compete in other competitions and also want to win those. Winning in one year is one thing, but being able to win in the next year, that is even tougher. Of course we can do that [compete on multiple fronts] and we have good enough players to be able to play with one starting XI on Saturday and do a couple of changes on Wednesday and still win. That was our biggest challenge last year – we had too many good players that were not playing enough games, so this year we will have the possibility to explore the whole squad. Each player will be more important than they’ve ever been for the club” – Jeglertz speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live.

Where are they playing their home games?

The Joie Stadium is the women’s team’s usual home, across the road from the Etihad Stadium, where they will play two home league fixtures. Those will be against Arsenal on 4 October and against Manchester United on 14 February. The 7,000-capacity Joie Stadium, that hosted matches at Euro 2022, has been the women’s team’s home for more than a decade and they were unbeaten at home in the league last season. They haven’t lost a home WSL game at the Joie Stadiumsince a 4-3 thriller against Arsenal in February 2025.

Sports.title: Saka settles gruelling battle with Aston Villa to extend Arsenal’s winning start
Sports.content:
The smile on Declan Rice’s face with six minutes of normal time remaining said it all. He had just shut down Ian Maatsen as the Aston Villa full-back zoomed into the box. Arsenal, for whom Bukayo Saka scored the only goal, were authoritative and seemingly took great satisfaction in keeping Villa at arm’s length.

Unai Emery’s work‑in‑progress side struggled to test the champions, David Raya untroubled. The records will show Villa have lost their first two league matches of a season without scoring for the first time since 2002 but, despite successive defeats, this time there was no capitulation.

For Villa, this was a marked improvement on defeat at Brighton in their opener. After 31 minutes in their previous game, they trailed 4-0 and after 40 were down to 10 men.

Here they could take plenty of encouragement from a promising if not fruitless performance, the debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson impressing, having taken the No 1 and No 11 shirts vacated by Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins respectively. Suzuki and Jackson were the only changes to Villa’s starting XI but they appeared far more cohesive. Suzuki’s eye for a pass was particularly noticeable, pinging 50-yard passes to George Hemmings, the 19-year-old who kept his place, and John McGinn within a few minutes of each other.

Emi Buendía smacked the crossbar after Boubacar Kamara overawed Christos Tzolis – Martin Ødegaard subsequently asked questions of the referee, Jarred Gillett – but Jackson otherwise created Villa’s best opening. The Senegal forward, who worked under Emery at Villarreal, pinched possession from Gabriel Magalhães a few yards into the Villa half and galloped into the other before sending a near-perfect cross in from the right. Hemmings burst into the six-yard box but was unable to convert. Villa are just the second team to fail to register a shot on target in their first two Premier League matches in a season since 2003-04, along with Swansea City in 2017-18.

This fixture last season ended in despair for Arsenal, their players splayed across the turf after Buendía’s 95th-minute winner with the last kick of the game. Arteta said that defeat still haunts him and reminded his players as much before this game. “That was still in my tummy and I spoke to my players about it, the image of the players on the floor, totally gutted,” the Arsenal manager said. “We used that [as inspiration].”

View image in fullscreen Zion Suzuki, Aston Villa’s new goalkeeper, applauds the home fans after the final whistle. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

In that game last season Eberechi Eze was at fault for Matty Cash’s opener and was subsequently hooked at half-time. Here it was a case of role‑reversal, Eze shining after coming on for the second half in place of Christos Tzolis, who was booked after a foul on Cash and muted.

“I think he learnt a lesson,” Arteta said of Eze, who was involved in Arsenal seizing the lead approaching the hour. Arsenal slowed things down and then punished Villa for switching off. Cristhian Mosquera pushed a pass to Eze, who was afforded space by Cash, Villa’s defender concerned about an unmarked Riccardo Calafiori. Eze promptly spied Calafiori’s underlapping run and the Italian steered the ball across the six-yard box where Saka beat Maatsen to the punch and scrambled the cross into the net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This is a new-look Villa, on and off the pitch. A handful of staff in hard hats were positioned in the closed North Stand moonlighting as ball boys; the corner of rubble between the remaining skeleton and the Trinity Road Stand remains akin to an excavation site. Ibrahim Mbaye, whose £47m move from Paris Saint‑Germain is to be announced on Tuesday, was in the directors’ box. Taylor Harwood-Bellis is also poised to sign in a £25m deal from Southampton. Six of Villa’s starting XI from their Europa League triumph may have departed but Emery has made no complaints and has relayed his no-excuses mantra to his squad. “We do not look backwards,” he said.

Villa’s frustrations were palpable. McGinn, in a hurry to get Villa level, was booked for wiping out Merino. Aaron Wan-Bissaka replaced Cash for his Villa debut and his first job was to stretch his legs to muffle an advancing Eze. Alejandro Garnacho entered in place of Ross Barkley. Arteta introduced Ezri Konsa for his debut, adding further steel.

Villa could not find a way through and Arsenal’s winning habit already appears ominous. “It is painful to lose,” Emery said. “But we can feel optimistic with how we competed.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi’s international retirement serves as a reminder: watch him while you still can
Sports.content:
It was among the defining moments of the 2026 World Cup: Lionel Messi standing arms akimbo, looking up towards Argentina’s fervent supporters after losing the final. Tears streamed down his face after his team’s embarrassing loss to Spain in what we now know was Messi’s final match wearing that famous Argentina kit.

It was not the first time he’d cried at the tournament. There had been tears of joy in Argentina’s opening match, when Messi rolled back the clock to his glory days with a trio of spectacular goals against Algeria. There had been more when his brace against Austria pushed Argentina through to the knockout round as group winners, and even more when his equalizer against Egypt threw la Albiceleste a much-needed lifeline. Later, the world found out that Messi had been struggling all the while with the health struggles of his father, Jorge, a fact that clearly weighed heavily on him as Argentina made a dramatic return to the final in a bid to defend their 2022 title.

There were tears in the weeks that followed the tournament as well, when Jorge passed away. It led Messi – among the most private, reserved megastars in the world, football or otherwise – to provide a rare moment of public vulnerability as he mourned the loss of his father on social media. But buried in that remembrance was something that caught many football fans off guard.

“All I did was play football,” Messi wrote, “and now I have serious doubts that I’ll do it for much longer.”

Messi announced his retirement from international football this week at age 39, a move that was somewhat expected given his age and the sheer emotional exhaustion that had clearly accompanied his final tournament. He finishes his Argentina career with the most men’s World Cup appearances of all time – 34 spread across six tournaments, the joint-most tournaments played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and Guillermo Ochoa. He scored or assisted 185 times in his 207 caps, a record 35 of which came at a major tournament. And of course, he was the leading figure in that legendary run that saw Argentina win the 2021 Copa América, the 2022 World Cup, and then defend their Copa América title in 2024. Internationally, there was little left for him to accomplish.

Yet Monday’s announcement still came as a bit of a surprise to many, largely because Messi’s brilliance is still so readily apparent. Few, if any players, have assembled the run of major tournament performances that Messi just put together, regardless of age.

View image in fullscreen Messi won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, his crowning international honor. Photograph: Friedemann Vogel/EPA

He remains the best player in Major League Soccer as well. Just this past weekend, the Argentinian scored four goals and provided an assist against Montreal, pushing him into the lead for the league’s golden boot.

He remains under a guaranteed contract at Miami through 2028, but Messi’s international exit has now cast understandable doubt on whether he will play that deal out. Messi essentially runs the show at Miami, a club that signs and discards players and coaches at his whim. Guaranteed contracts mean little to the club’s megastars. Just last year, Jordi Alba walked away from a three-year contract after just a few months, choosing retirement and making the MLS Cup final his last professional game. Messi is an idol at the club and would seemingly face little resistance if he chose to bring his career to a close at the end of this season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Lionel Messi scored four goals for Inter Miami over the weekend. Photograph: Chandan Khanna/AFP/Getty Images

All of which is to say: If you’re in North America, or if you can make it there, go see Lionel Messi now, while you still have a chance.

Three years after his arrival, those of us who live and breathe soccer in Canada and the US have grown almost accustomed to Messi’s presence and all of the magic that accompanies it because it has become so routine. Miami’s traveling bazaar of Messi and aging European megastars was a genuine sensation at first but has since retreated into the shadows at times along with the rest of MLS. His four-goal effort against Montreal would have made international headlines in 2023 but now does little to move the needle. If anything, it’s to be expected. Even in Miami, where Messi was embraced readily, Messi’s presence no longer guarantees the hysteria it once did.

Yet Messi’s level, in MLS at least, has not declined. He remains a must-see player and Miami remain a must-watch team. MLS has a sometimes deserved reputation for being a “retirement league,” yet that same reputation provides fans in North America with an opportunity few of them would have otherwise: to witness global greatness in person, and for a relative bargain.

For other players – Thierry Henry, David Beckham and the like – those moments of greatness were sometimes sporadic in MLS. Messi, though, seems to provide those moments at each and every turn.

His star no longer shines as brightly as it did years ago at Barcelona or even months ago, in an Argentina shirt. Yet even the slightly dimmed, more fleeting light Messi produces in Miami is worth watching. His first, presumably permanent, exit from the global stage is a good reminder that soon enough it will be gone for ever.

Sports.title: Ainsley Maitland-Niles set for surprise Premier League return three years after Arsenal exit
Sports.content:
Ainsley Maitland-Niles set for surprise Premier League return three years after Arsenal exit

Everton have agreed to sign former Arsenal man Ainsley Maitland-Niles from Lyon on deadline day, talkSPORT understands.

The deal is understood to be worth around £4.2million.

2 Maitland-Niles is due to sign for Everton ahead of the deadline Credit: Getty



Maitland-Niles is in the final year of his deal at French outfit Lyon.

The right-back will arrive at Hill Dickinson Stadium as competition for Merlin Rohl.

Meanwhile, Nathan Patterson is set to leave Everton for Torino ahead of the transfer deadline.

Maitland-Niles has not played in the Premier League since May 2023.

The 29-year-old spent 20 years on the books at Arsenal, having joined at the age of six.



He went on to make 72 senior appearances and win the FA Cup at the north Londoners.

Maitland-Niles spent the 2022/23 season, his last as an Arsenal player, on loan at Southampton.



With 119 matches played, he earned plenty more minutes with Lyon.

Everton's deadline day plans

talkSPORT understands that Jack Grealish is set to return to Everton from Manchester City on a season-long loan.

The 30-year-old joined the Toffees for the 2025/26 season and was a huge hit before injury brought an early end to his campaign.



2 Maitland-Niles will return to the Premier League three years on from his Arsenal exit Credit: Getty

Richarlison had been linked with a return to Everton, although he has all but confirmed that a switch won't take place.

He would have arrived from Tottenham Hotspur, whose move for Iliman Ndiaye has been hijacked by City in a £60m deal.

Everton have also eyed VfB Stuttgart forward Jamie Leweling ahead of the 11pm deadline.



However, their bid worth up to £36.8m has reportedly been rejected.

Elsewhere, Tim Iroegbunam is heading to Hull City for an initial £13m after two seasons at Everton.

Sports.title: New Chelsea signing has two transfer announcements as Blues find clever way to get around Premier League rules
Sports.content:
New Chelsea signing has two transfer announcements as Blues find clever way to get around Premier League rules

It's been quite the day for Honest Ahanor.

The defender has joined Crystal Palace on a season-long loan from Atalanta.

3 The 18-year-old has made just 41 senior appearances in his career Credit: Getty

Ahanor will then become a Chelsea player next summer as the Blues struck a £40million deal with Atalanta for the teenager.

The transfer chaos has meant Ahanor conducted two different photo shoots on deadline day, posing with Chelsea and Crystal Palace kits.

How could Honest Ahanor sign for both Chelsea and Crystal Palace on the same day?

Given the complexity of the deals along with the Premier League's transfer rules, some may be left questioning how it all works.

Per the Premier League's handbook, a club cannot sign more than one player from the same club.

Palace have already signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea for the season, meaning they could not sign Ahanor had he gone to the Blues right away.

Additionally, Premier League clubs are not permitted to loan a player to another Premier League club if they acquired the player in the same window.

Again, that would have ruled out Ahanor joining Palace if he completed a move to Chelsea this summer rather than in 2027.

But because the Blues struck an agreement with Atalanta to complete the deal next summer, Ahanor is free to get a full season of Premier League action under his belt.

Why did Crystal Palace push to sign a new centre-back?

Palace were in the market for additional help at centre-back after Chadi Riad sustained an ACL injury in their season opener against Everton.

The south London outfit swooped for Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez and had agreed a deal to sign him on loan with an obligation to buy.

3 Ahanor will get a taste of life in the Premier League with Palace before moving to Chelsea Credit: Getty

However, Palace withdrew over fears about Ordonez's recovery time from a broken metatarsal.

They have now landed Ahanor who, at just 18 years of age, has proved he can handle the big occasions.

Ahanor made 35 appearances across all competitions for Atalanta last term, including nine in the Champions League.

His impressive displays at club level earned him a call-up to the Italy squad last June, where he won two caps.

Ahanor will now be tasked with helping Palace, who are involved in this season's Europa League.

Steve Parish reacts to Crystal Palace signing Honest Ahanor

For Eagles chairman Steve Parish, the addition of Ahanor represents a major coup, especially so late in the window.

3 Palace boss Pierre Sage has brought in five new defensive players this summer Credit: Getty

"Honest is an exciting young talent whose arrival offers further competition for places ahead of another European campaign at Selhurst Park," Parish said.

"We are pleased to have him with us in South London."

Ahanor could make his Palace debut on Saturday when Pierre Sage's side take on Fulham at Craven Cottage, with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea starlet predicted to score bundles for EFL promotion challengers after bargain transfer
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea starlet predicted to score bundles for EFL promotion challengers after bargain transfer

Former Chelsea starlet Jimmy-Jay Morgan has been backed to score bundles this season after a fine start to life at West Bromwich Albion.

The 20-year-old has hit the ground running at the Baggies with four goals and two assists in his first five appearances for the club.



3 Morgan scored four times in the first month of the season Credit: Getty

The England Under-20 youth international joined the Chelsea academy at the age of eight before leaving for Southampton.

He was lured back to Cobham over the Saints in February 2023 but failed to make a single senior appearance with the Blues.

Jimmy-Jay Morgan stats

Morgan spent last season on loan at Peterborough, where he scored 12 goals in 34 League One matches before making the step up a division this summer.



Having joined Championship side West Brom on a four-year deal, the attacker has netted in two of his first three second-tier appearances.

The most recent of which came in Saturday's 3-1 defeat to Middlesbrough, which caught the attention of Adrian Clarke.



The former Arsenal midfielder told the EFL All Access panel that Morgan could prove to be a bargain for West Brom this campaign.

Reacting to West Brom's loss to Boro, Hugh Woozencroft said: "They looked great at times during this game - James Morrison's side.



"Isaac Price, and Jimmy-Jay Morgan linking up for the goal. Really well taken goal."

3 Morgan played for Chelsea's under-21s side but did not manage to break into the first team Credit: Getty

Jimmy-Jay Morgan's going under the radar

"I think Jimmy-Jay Morgan's going a little bit under the radar as well," Woozencroft added on the EFL All Access podcast.

"Coming from Chelsea, four goals, two assists for him.

"Now, obviously, they would have preferred the win, but they look a much more dynamic team than they did last season.



"And he did say after the game, James Morrison, he wants to add a couple more.

"They've added Toby Collyer, obviously, from Manchester United; if they can add a couple of quality players, they could be a team to really worry about."

3 West Brom currently sit in a playoff spot after winning two of their first three games Credit: Getty

Adrian Clarke, who tipped Morgan as among his standout Championship transfers last month, said of West Brom: "I like the midfield with [Ousmane] Diakité and [Jayson] Molumby.



"They're getting younger players, aren't they? And these are young, hungry players with a point to prove.

"Isaac Price, he's got his whole career ahead of him. He wants to make it to the very top. Same with Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

"He's got his move from Chelsea. Could be a bargain.

"I think it's £4million, which felt a lot because he wasn't amazing on loan at Peterborough last season.

"But Sam Parkin, our friend here at talkSPORT, he told me he watched Rotherham play against West Brom in the Carabao Cup.



"He said, Jimmy-Jay Morgan is going to score bundles this season. So he's seen something in him."

Sports.title: Premier League clubs questioned for snubbing midfielder Rio Ferdinand wanted at Man United
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs have been urged to shoot their shot to sign one of Europe's brightest young midfielders.

The midfield market has exploded for English top-flight clubs this summer, and is still set to be a major talking point on deadline day.



3 Kees Smit hasn't made a summer transfer despite being tracked by huge clubs Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that Manchester City have seen a bid in excess of £120million for Enzo Fernandez rejected by Chelsea.

Enzo Maresca's side have already invested heavily in recruiting in the middle of the park, with Ayyoub Bouaddi becoming the most expensive teenager in Premier League history, after Elliot Anderson was bought for £116m.

Their city rivals Man United have also transformed their midfield, with Youri Tielemans arriving from Aston Villa for £35m, Andrey Santos joining from Chelsea in a £50m transfer and a package worth an initial £70m deal signed off for Carlos Baleba.



Ahead of that summer spree, Rio Ferdinand told talkSPORT in May that he didn't want his old club to miss out on Kees Smit.

Kees Smit transfer latest

The 20-year-old, who was named as one of the stars to watch in Europe at the start of last season, looked destined to be on the move this transfer window.



talkSPORT previously revealed that Newcastle and Crystal Palace were competing with Real Madrid to sign the Netherlands international.

However, despite the affordable price tag, with AZ seeking over £22m and the raft of Premier League clubs overhauling their midfield, Smit has stayed put.



European football expert Andy Brassell told talkSPORT.com: "I'm really surprised that he hasn't gone anywhere already this summer.

"A 20-year-old midfielder who can dictate already. AZ have had a great start to the season. He's been part of it."

3 Smit was a surprise omission from the Netherlands' World Cup squad after his impressive season Credit: Getty

Kees Smit next club

Brassell continued to talkSPORT: "Now, Newcastle were interested in him for a long time, and they went a bit cold because they felt that someone really big was going to get him.



"Like, really big. Like Real Madrid kind of big. So, I do wonder when you get closer to the deadline if there's a club that could make that kind of move.

"I think that would be really, really interesting. Obviously, a big deal to piece together in the last day.

"I don't know what more he could prove this season in the Eredivisie. Unless, like, AZ win the title and go the whole season unbeaten.

"What really could he do to prove any more?

3 Smit has already registered two assists in four Eredivisie games this season Credit: Getty



"People out there know he's a really good player, and he could get to that top level.

"But maybe, if that opportunity is not out there for him, maybe he does have to look to go to a less esteemed club in a bigger league.

"I mean, look, if you're anyone else in one of those big leagues, just shoot your shot already. You can only say no."

Sports.title: What is a deal sheet and how can Premier League clubs sign players after deadline?
Sports.content:
What is a deal sheet and how can Premier League clubs sign players after deadline?

The summer transfer window will dramatically draw to a close at 11pm on Tuesday night and Premier League clubs are ready for some last-minute action.

Clubs across Europe will conclude deadline day at various times depending on the specific league or competition.



3 Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea as their club-record signing Credit: Getty

This year's edition has seen the record fee for a British player broken twice - with Elliot Anderson's £116m move to Manchester City, closely followed by the signature of Morgan Rogers at Chelsea for £117m.

The Premier League champions Arsenal acquired Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle and Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa, with the transfers sparking debate over Premier League financial rules.

Tottenham have spent around £320m throughout the window and are expected not to stop there with a potential frantic final few hours.



What times do the transfer window close?

The summer transfer window closes on Tuesday, September 1 at 11pm BST for Premier League and EFL clubs.

After opening on June 15, Fifa rules state that the window cannot be open for more than 16 weeks at a time.



Last year, the final day of the window finished at 7pm in the UK; however, it has now changed back to its original time.

However, the rest of Europe do not follow the same rules:

Ligue 1: Tuesday, 1 September - 18:59 BST

Serie A: Tuesday, 1 September - 19:00 BST

Bundesliga: Tuesday, 1 September - 19:00 BST

La Liga: Tuesday, 1 September - 22:59 BST

Scottish Premiership: Thursday, 3 September - 17:00 BST

Women's Super League: Thursday, 3 September - 23:00 BST

Despite the strict deadline, there remains a way for clubs to complete late moves beyond the cutoff point.



What is a deal sheet?

It allows a club to confirm an agreement has been reached and also give themselves more time to submit the remaining documentation.

3 What a deal sheet looks like Credit: Premier League

A deal sheet must be completed by Premier League clubs in the last two hours of a transfer window.

For an 11pm deadline, the form cannot be used before 9pm and needs to arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes at 11pm.



Once the sheet arrives, clubs have another two hours to submit the full paperwork (1am).

How do clubs register a player?

The full paperwork includes the contract, the transfer agreement between the clubs involved in the deal, permission to work in the UK (if required), and international clearance if transferring from abroad.

The Premier League's Football Operations and Regulatory departments are staffed late into the night on deadline day.

Once the legal part is finished, it is cleared through the Premier League and Football Association rules. In some cases, the transfer needs to also comply with FIFA regulations.



3 Isak's move to Liverpool capped off a blockbuster transfer window for the Reds last summer Credit: Getty

Previous deadline day signings

Last summer, Alexander Isak departed St James' Park for Liverpool in a blockbusting deadline day switch that shattered the British transfer record.

Sports.title: Everton see ‘deadline day bid rejected’ for Premier League-ready winger
Sports.content:
Everton have reportedly submitted an official proposal for Stuttgart forward Jamie Leweling.

According to Sky Germany's Patrick Berger, the Toffees' bid was worth up to £36.8million.



3 Leweling has won six caps for Germany since 2024 Credit: Getty

However, Berger adds Leweling has already rejected Everton's advances and wishes to remain at Stuttgart.

Everton's interest in Leweling came after the 25-year-old registered 11 goals and 12 assists for Stuttgart last term.

Nine of Leweling's assists came in the Bundesliga, with only four players contributing more.



Although Leweling may not want to pursue a move to English shores yet, European football expert Andy Brassell believes he'd perfectly fit the rough and tumble of the Premier League.

Andy Brassell's verdict on Jamie Leweling

"Leweling feels a bit more Prem-ready," Brassell exclusively told talkSPORT.com.



"I think because he's quite a physical type of wide player.

"He's someone who's very direct. He's not someone who's slight and speedy and will-o'-the-wisp.

"He's someone who really engages with defenders, who tries to cut inside and scores goals. He's got a feeling that he's in a rush. He likes to do everything quickly. He's adaptable as well.



"I think he can play in a few different forward positions. He's come on so much since he was at Stuttgart, where he's been coached really well by Sebastian Hoeneß. Of course, there's the possibility that he goes to Roma as well. They've been looking for a wide player, particularly a wide left player, for a while now.

"But in terms of him adapting to the Premier League, look, there's been Premier League interest in him for well over a year. See him play a couple of times and you'll totally understand why."

3 Moyes has looked to revamp his attack this season Credit: Getty

Which players are set to join Everton late in the window?

Everton have also agreed a £40m deal to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco.

Balogun, who came through Arsenal's academy, will replace Beto, who is bound for Fiorentina.



Another fresh face set to join is Ainsley Maitland-Niles, who is expected to move in a £4.2m deal from Lyon.

3 Grealish is in the last year of his contract with City, meaning he's effectively played his last game for the club Credit: Getty

The flurry of activity in Merseyside comes as star attacker Iliman Ndiaye prepares to leave.

Ndiaye is headed for City in a £60m deal, with £5m in add-ons.

It initially appeared that Ndiaye was bound for Tottenham, but City swooped and completed the hijack.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay to undergo heart surgery as Napoli return date set
Sports.content:
Napoli have announced that Scott McTominay is set to have surgery on a heart issue.

McTominay has been diagnosed with mild benign arrhythmia, which is an irregular heartbeat.



2 McTominay will undergo surgery on a heart issue Credit: AFP

The midfielder is now set for a spell on the sidelines as he recovers.

"Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days," Napoli said.

"He will be available again after the international break."

What is cardiac arrhythmia ablation?

Cardiac arrhythmia ablation is a short procedure that, according to the British Heart Foundation, can last as little as just 15 minutes.



During surgery, a small cut is made on the patient's groin or wrist, with catheters are then placed inside and moved up to the heart.

The area inside the heart that has caused the arrhythmia is then destroyed by either radiofrequency energy or cryoablation.



This step of the procedure helps to block abnormal electrical signals in the heart.

McTominay has played in both of Napoli's Serie A fixtures this season and was brought off in the 2-1 weekend defeat to Como.



The former Manchester United star's upcoming surgery means he is unlikely to play for Scotland during the international break.

Scotland have four fixtures scheduled for the newly-extended break, which begins on September 21.

2 McTominay looks set to miss the international break with Scotland Credit: Getty

Slovenia, Switzerland and North Macedonia are their Nations League opponents as they begin their Group B1 campaign.



Sebastien Pocognoli will take charge of the side for the first time since being announced as the replacement for Steve Clarke.

The former Belgium and Premier League defender was previously with the Belgian U18s, Royale Union Saint-Gilloise and AS Monaco.

Pocognoli has joined a Scotland team that had a miserable World Cup campaign during the summer.

They scored one goal across their three group matches and missed out on the knockout stages.

Sports.title: Liverpool’s stance on signing a new attacker as Cody Gakpo stays and Ismaila Sarr update
Sports.content:
Liverpool’s stance on signing a new attacker as Cody Gakpo stays and Ismaila Sarr update

Liverpool will not be bringing in any more players before the transfer window shuts, talkSPORT understands.

The Reds' stance comes after they rejected Manchester City's £80million bid for Cody Gakpo, who was also of interest to Tottenham.

3 Gakpo has been with the Reds since January 2023 Credit: Getty

Liverpool had made plans for Gakpo's potential exit earlier in the window by unsuccessfully pursuing Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh.

An approach for Crystal Palace flyer Ismaila Sarr also fell short as the Eagles were not willing to entertain a sale so late in the window.

Alex Crook explains Liverpool's deadline day transfer stance

But now that Gakpo will remain, coupled with the £106million arrival of Bradley Barcola, the Reds are content with their options in the final third.

Liverpool's stance was confirmed on talkSPORT's White and Jordan by chief football correspondent Alex Crook, who felt some Reds fans 'might be a bit disappointed' that a direct replacement for Mohamed Salah, who left at the end of last season, has not been sourced.

"Interestingly, I've been speaking to people at Liverpool this morning and they tell me their business is done in terms of incomings in this window," Crook said.

"I think Liverpool fans on deadline day might be a bit disappointed with the lack of numbers they've recruited this summer.

"They haven't replaced Mohamed Salah on that right-hand side."

How will Liverpool replace Mohamed Salah on the right wing?

As outlined by Crook, the void left by Salah has not been directly filled.

Although capable of playing anywhere across the front three, Barcola is predominantly a left-winger.

That could force Gakpo, who is also a left-winger by trade but capable of playing up top, to the right wing.

3 Barcola is expected to take Liverpool's attack to a whole new level Credit: Getty

Gakpo played on the right side of Liverpool's attack in their 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday, but he is unlikely to be a long-term solution.

Summer recruit Victor Munoz can play on the right but operates more on the left while teenage sensation Rio Ngumoha almost exclusively features on the left wing.

The lack of out-and-out options at right wing adds another unwanted headache for Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, who is yet to pick up his first league win in charge.

That's not the only area of concern for Iraola, as his side have conceded four goals in two games.

It continued an alarming trend for the Reds, who have kept just five clean sheets in their last 22 league fixtures.

Martin Keown's verdict on Liverpool's immediate title hopes

Unfortunately, Arsenal legend Martin Keown believes Liverpool's leaky defence could scupper their ambitions of challenging for the Premier League.

3 Iraola has overseen two draws in as many league games to start the season Credit: Getty

When asked if Liverpool have got enough to contest for the title, Keown replied: "Not quite at the moment.

"I think the full-backs look a little weak defensively.

"Iraola took nine games at Bournemouth to get his first win and there's a lot of information the players are not taking on board.

"The back line don't seem to shift forward enough to do the press."

Iraola will hope to avoid a third-straight game without a league win when Liverpool return to action on Friday night away to Ipswich Town, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm.

Sports.title: BBC axe ANOTHER sports show: Ski Sunday comes to an end just four months after Football Focus was cancelled
Sports.content:
BBC axe ANOTHER sports show: Ski Sunday comes to an end just four months after Football Focus was cancelled

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

BBC have decided to cancel their Ski Sunday show after nearly 50 years on air.

The programme, which was first aired in 1978, had become a recognisable part of the winter sports calendar, detailing all the latest news across the likes of the Winter Olympics to viewers.

The decision comes just over four months since long-running football show Football Focus was also axed.

And, just like with Football Focus, the reason why was attributed to viewing habits.

Philip Bernie, Head of BBC Sport Events, said following the decision: 'Ski Sunday has been a truly iconic programme and a much-loved part of BBC Sport's output for many years. Generations of viewers have enjoyed its coverage of the best in winter sports.

'We are enormously proud of the role it has played in bringing these moments to audiences across the UK, and extremely grateful to the brilliant people who have delivered them, not least the current outstanding team.

BBC show Ski Sunday has been brought to an end after nearly 50 years on television screens

'These decisions are never easy, but as audience viewing habits evolve and we work to deliver value for licence fee payers, we have to make tough choices. We remain committed to bringing audiences the very best of winter sport, above all at the Winter Olympics, across BBC Sport's platforms.'

BBC Sport chief Alex Kay-Jelski, meanwhile, said upon the cancellation of Football Focus that the decision reflected 'the continued shift in how audiences engage with football and our commitment to evolving how we deliver content to reach fans wherever they are.'

Just like the football show, Ski Sunday formed part of weekend show Sunday Grandstand.

It was presented by David Vine for a number of years, with ex-skier Graham Bell taking the reins alongside former snowboarder Ed Leigh.

Chemmy Alcott, who participated in four Winter Olympics, meanwhile, joined the show alongside Leigh five years ago.

Fans were left divided by the news, with one writing on X: 'That's so sad, I'm not into skiing but as a kid used to watch that with my dad with David Vine on comms.'

Another, alongside three crying emojis, posted: 'What's next? Today at Wimbledon? Today at the Test?'

Some, though, weren't fussed.

'I'm 25 and have never seen this on TV,' one X user wrote. 'I've obviously heard people talk about it (mainly its theme tune) and assumed it had ended in the 80s or 90s.'

Another shared: 'How was skiing a TV show on the BBC for 50 years?'

The BBC will continue to show sports broadcasts such as the men's and women's World Cups, the Olympic Games and Match of the Day.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay set to undergo heart surgery - as Napoli release health update on former Man United star
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay set to undergo heart surgery - as Napoli release health update on former Man United star

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Scott McTominay is set to undergo corrective heart surgery, his club Napoli have confirmed.

The former Manchester United star, 29, has developed a heart condition known as mild, benign arrhythmia.

According to medical experts, this is an irregular heart rhythm that is non life-threatening and something that should be resolved after the corrective procedure.

In a statement, Napoli said: 'Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days.

'He will be available again after the international break.'

The British Heart Foundation say the procedure that McTominay will undertake is when heat or cold energy is used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

Scott McTominay is set to undergo corrective heart surgery, his club Napoli have confirmed

McTominay (pictured with partner Cam Reading) should return to action after a short period out

He is expected to be able to return to full fitness following a short period out.

However, Napoli's revelation that he will miss the international break means that McTominay will be unavailable for new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli's first four games in charge.

The midfielder featured in Napoli's 2-1 defeat by Como in Serie A on Sunday, with the 29-year-old substituted after 56 minutes.

He previously played the full 90 minutes in their 2-0 victory over Genoa on the opening day of the season.

McTominay has been a revelation since joining the Italian side from Manchester United in 2024.

The Scottish star has scored 27 goals and added 10 assists in just 82 appearances, while he played a key role in their Serie A triumph in 2024-25.

Under Antonio Conte, he evolved from a dependable squad player at Old Trafford into one of Europe's most effective box-crashing midfielders, scoring 12 Serie A goals and earning the division's MVP award during that superb campaign.

He also came 18th in the Ballon d'Or rankings in 2025, ahead of players including Jude Bellingham, Erling Haaland and Michael Olise.

McTominay repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

His impact prompted comparisons with Napoli icon Diego Maradona, with the Argentine's son even likening the Scot to Jesus.

Napoli added that McTominay is expected to miss Scotland's upcoming fixtures this month

But it is not only McTominay's exploits on the pitch that have won over supporters.

McTominay has embraced life in Naples with his partner Cam Reading and immersed himself in Neapolitan culture, while also learning to speak Italian.

On the day of his medical, he asked to visit the club's home, the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, to pay his respects to the Argentine legend.

He also went viral in April 2025 after hailing the quality of local tomatoes.

'Oh my goodness, the tomatoes,' he said. 'Bellissimo. I never ate them at home, they are just red water.

'Here, they actually taste like tomatoes. Now I eat them as a snack. I eat all the vegetables, all of the fruits. It is all so fresh. It's incredible.'

Moments like this helped McTominay earn the endearing nickname 'McFratm', with 'Fratm' meaning 'my brother' in local slang.

His face has appeared on murals, flags and even birthday cakes, while supporters erected a shrine to him in Naples city centre after the 2025 title triumph.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres feels the full force of Mikel Arteta's ruthless streak, Christos Tzolis gets a rude awakening - and the psychological battle facing Arsenal's opponents: THINGS WE LEARNED as the Gunners beat Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres feels the full force of Mikel Arteta's ruthless streak, Christos Tzolis gets a rude awakening - and the psychological battle facing Arsenal's opponents: THINGS WE LEARNED as the Gunners beat Aston Villa

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mikel Arteta’s ruthlessness is well-documented.

Just ask Aaron Ramsdale or, most recently, Gabriel Martinelli, the pair having been moved on after losing their starting spots.

The needs of the team supersede feelings or perceived fairness.

Viktor Gyokeres is feeling that wrath right now, having failed to come off the bench once again.

It’s a second consecutive match without appearing, only mustering a run out in the 74th minute of Arsenal’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City.

On paper, Gyokeres’ 21 goals across all competitions last season makes the absence of minutes an unusual case.

It is further emphasised after the display of Kai Havertz on Monday night against Aston Villa, an ineffective showing masked by the Gunners’ victory.

The German consistently reminded viewers just why the north London club have been linked with Alvarez, fans desperate for an attacking addition before the window closes.

It’s a second consecutive match without appearing for Viktor Gyokeres, only mustering a run out in the 74th minute of Arsenal ’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City

Havertz's performance in general lacked the composure of a leading Premier League team’s striker, marked by clunky play and an ineffectiveness around the goal frame

On 14 minutes, having been played through by Martin Odegaard, Havertz struck the ball well wide while in the area.

He ought to have done better — and it got worse. Substitute Bruno Guimaraes set the forward free in the second period, yet he could only strike straight at Zion Suzuki.

His performance in general lacked the composure of a leading Premier League team’s striker, marked by clunky play and an ineffectiveness around the goal frame.

All this emphasised Gyokeres’ failure to come off the bench, falling out of favour so badly to not have been turned to by Arteta.

The decision was a surprise and almost a nudge to the ownership ahead of deadline day.

It will not have done the Swede’s confidence any good, or helped him believe he has a place in the team.

The coming weeks are huge for Gyokeres. A failure to play anytime soon could well be the start of a slippery slope out of Arteta’s plans.

Welcome to the Premier League, Christos Tzolis

The plaudits were loud after impressive displays against Man City in the Community Shield, and Coventry in the Premier League.

He couldn’t put a foot wrong, dancing around players and playing piercing deliveries forward.

Yet, against Villa, he just could not get going in a real crash down to Earth.

The Greek seemed flustered from Matty Cash’s physicality and failed to make an impact on the ball.

He started in a wide position, hugging the touchline, trying to drive inwards.

When he was in possession, Tzolis often gave the ball away or succumbed under the opposition backline’s pressure.

When he was in possession, Tzolis often gave the ball away or succumbed under the opposition backline’s pressure

It was a reversal from the carefree marches in the final third from just a week ago.

To top it off, he received a yellow card for a foul on Cash, before being hooked at half-time after going close to a second bookable offence just before the break.

The performance reflected how Tzolis has been brought in to compete for the left-wing spot, rather than as a certified starter.

He’s only 24, and internally Arsenal view him as a player with a high ceiling for the future.

Plus, the Premier League is arguably the most demanding league in world football.

It’s no coincidence that Arsenal are looking to further bolster their frontline in this window at left wing.

Tzolis is a promising player with a bright future ahead. Yet, putting the burden on him right now at Arsenal would be unwise.

Gunners hold the fort

Arteta’s obsession with a rock-solid defence came into focus once again.

In the 29 matches since the start of last season in which Arsenal scored first, the Gunners have won 26 games, had two draws and lost just once.

Adding to this, the signing of Ezri Konsa has strengthened Arsenal’s most formidable area — and it’s already forming their title defence.

The Gunners weren’t at their attacking best but, as has often been the case in the past year, a sole goal is enough because of their backline.

That is a psychological battle opponents will have to deal with, knowing that even if they don’t concede, scoring a goal will still be extremely hard to come by.

The foundations to further potential trophies are being laid.

Sports.title: Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which Arsenal star was brought crashing down to earth? Who had a night to forget for Villa? And which debutant caught the eye?
Sports.content:
Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which Arsenal star was brought crashing down to earth? Who had a night to forget for Villa? And which debutant caught the eye?

Unlock more of the best of our football coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Premier League champions Arsenal maintained their perfect start to the season, following up their opening-day victory over Coventry with a hard-fought win at Aston Villa.

After a cagey first half in which neither side managed a shot on target, Bukayo Saka broke the deadlock in the 59th minute.

The goal came from a well-worked team move, with Eze sliding the ball through the lines for Riccardo Calafiori, who flung himself towards the byline and managed to pull the ball back across goal for Saka to bundle it over the line from close range.

There was a late injury concern for Arsenal when Cristhian Mosquera went down clutching his hamstring and was unable to continue. He was replaced by Ezri Konsa, who joined from Villa only last week and received a largely warm reception on his return, with applause from the home crowd mixed with a smattering of boos.

Despite a late spell of pressure from Villa, Arsenal saw the game out to collect all three valuable points.

Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE and ISAAN KHAN were in position at Villa Park to run the rule over both sets of players...

After a cagey first half in which neither side managed a shot on target, Bukayo Saka broke the deadlock in the 59th minute

Villa's new goalkeeper Zion Suzuki caught the eye on his debut with his impressive distribution

Aston Villa (4-3-3)

Zion Suzuki - 6

The debutant caught the eye with his range of kicking on either foot, which can become a key weapon. A couple of good saves, a couple of shaky moments.

Matty Cash - 7

Struggles against wingers with extreme pace and luckily for him, neither Christos Tzolis nor Eberechi Eze has it. Tenacious in defence and attacked where he could. Subbed.

Victor Lindelof - 6.5

Very shaky at Brighton last week but did better here, defending his box well and using the ball calmly when he had to.

Pau Torres - 5.5

Lucky not to be punished when he gave the ball away playing out. Better than he was at Brighton but looks nervous without Ezri Konsa beside him.

Ian Maatsen - 4.5

Arsenal tried to isolate him against Bukayo Saka throughout. Made a foolish foul on his man, then lost him for the opener. A night to forget.

Ian Maatsen lost Bukayo Saka for the opener and had a night to forget against the champions

Boubacar Kamara - 7

Villa’s key man had to stay ultra-focused as Arsenal’s full backs stepped inside to create overloads in the middle. Did his job well as usual.

Ross Barkley - 6.5

Played up front last week, now asked to play as one of two holding midfielders, and he handled a difficult challenge well. Passing was not always on point. Subbed.

John McGinn - 6

Never easy to play against, the Villa skipper operated from the right and was furious when Tzolis was not shown a second yellow for a clear drag-back. Booked.

Emi Buendia - 7.5

Fabulous strike that hit the bar early on. The Argentine was typically lively and will rue his poor pass to Jackson when Villa had a four-against-three break.

Emi Buendia was typically lively and will rue his poor pass to Jackson when Villa had a four-against-three break

George Hemmings - 6.5

A prospect. Had a tough assignment both with and without the ball and performed steadily. Should have a Premier League career ahead of him. Subbed.

Nicolas Jackson - 6

This was his debut and, understandably, he is still working to understand his team-mates. For most of the game, Arsenal’s centre backs shackled him pretty well. Subbed.

Substitutes

Tammy Abraham (for Jackson, 71) - 6

Villa have been willing to let him go all window and it was no surprise that Jackson came straight in for his debut.

Alysson (for Hemmings, 71) - 6.5

Ran on the outside of Calafiori and fired across goal for Abraham, who nearly turned it in.

Manager

Unai Emery - 6

Allowed Arsenal to dictate the tempo of the match and hoped to hit them on the break. His team faded after a solid first half.

Emery allowed Arsenal to dictate the tempo of the match and hoped to hit them on the break

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1)

David Raya - 6.5

Had his crossbar rattled by Buendia in the first half. Claimed crosses with confidence. Stayed alert when Villa looked dangerous in attacking areas.

Ben White - 5.5

Kept trying to link up with Bukayo Saka. Passing accuracy was lacking, which was a problem. Needed to be better on the ball.

Cristhian Mosquera - 7

Solid positioning and got stuck into tackles. Good pass in the lead-up to Saka’s goal. Stepped up to the challenge.

Gabriel - 6.5

Took the responsibility of leading the backline. Pressed up the pitch and looked for passes, though Jackson enjoyed dribbling against him.

Riccardo Calafiori - 7.5

His left flank was occasionally exposed due to the Italian’s high positioning. But an excellent run and cross to assist Saka. Such a threat in attack.

Calafiori was a strong threat in attack and made an excellent run and cross to assist Saka

Myles Lewis-Skelly - 7

Smart play in the middle. Shielded the ball well, astute both in attack and in his own box.

Declan Rice - 8.5

Played in a quarterback-style role. Good distribution both short and aerially. Villa's midfield looked worried when Rice was in possession, charging forward.

Bukayo Saka - 7

Lost the ball a few times in the first half but kept going. Good movement to get on the scoresheet. He’s now scored in consecutive league matches.

Martin Odegaard - 6.5

An intricate pass on 14 minutes should’ve been capitalised on by Kai Havertz. Could have been more effective on counter-attacks.

Christos Tzolis - 4.5

A crash down to earth after recent strong displays. Flustered by Matty Cash’s physicality and couldn’t get going. A real lesson for the winger.

New signing Christos Tzolis was sent crashing back down to earth after recent strong displays

Kai Havertz - 5

An underwhelming display. Missed a few chances, including after being played through by Bruno Guimaraes in the second half.

Substitutes

Eberechi Eze (for Christos Tzolis, 46) - 6.5

Mikel Merino (for Martin Odegaard, 71) - 6.5

Bruno Guimaraes (for Myles Lewis-Skelly, 71) - 7

Ezri Konsa (for Cristhian Mosquera, 79) - N/A

Manager

Mikel Arteta - 7

Patient with his tactics as Arsenal gradually ground the opposition down.

Referee - Jarred Gillett - 6.5

Decided to give Tzolis a let-off for his foul on McGinn, keeping the second yellow card in his pocket and playing advantage instead. Otherwise, a steady display.

Sports.title: Arsenal NOT expected to make blockbuster deadline day move for Julian Alvarez - with wantaway Atletico Madrid star set to stay
Sports.content:
Arsenal have turned their attention away from Julian Alvarez with the Atletico Madrid forward expected to stay in Spain.

Daily Mail Sport understands that bar a last-minute change in stance from Alvarez, the Gunners are not hopeful of a move and assessing other options.

The forward had missed three consecutive days of training due to ‘illness’ which intensified Arsenal’s hopes of luring Alvarez to north London.

The Argentine is desperate for a move away from Diego Simeone’s side, with Barcelona his dream destination.

Though Atletico are refusing to entertain any such prospect of a sale to their Spanish rivals.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier in the year, Gunners staff were tasked with gathering data on Alvarez to assess whether he would fit the team’s required profile.

Arsenal have turned their attention away from a move for Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez

That included his injury record, physiological numbers and playing output. The result was emphatic: he fits the requirements of Arsenal’s team, and Arteta wants him.

Alvarez was mercilessly booed before, during and after Atletico’s La Liga game against Villarreal last month.

Simeone clarified after the game that Alvarez was under strict orders to not clap the fans following the clash, as he went straight down the tunnel.

Sports.title: The secrets of Ollie Robinson's glorious summer: Bowling slower, more lacquer and the crucial role of Joe Root
Sports.content:
There may never have been a better moment for Ollie Robinson to have made his return to Test cricket than the summer of 2026. As he sat beside Joe Root at Sunday evening’s post-match press conference at Lord’s, it felt like a symbolic alliance, an official welcoming back into the England fold after more than two-and-a-half years in the wilderness. Even his first Test back, against New Zealand at Lord’s in June, was followed by a mini-hiatus. First a knee injury ruled him out of the second Test at The Oval. Then, with Trent Bridge expected to be flat and temperatures punishing, old doubts resurfaced. Did Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes trust their man to pull through? They did not. Only when Root resumed the captaincy on a full-time basis did the next phase of Robinson’s career properly begin. And to the seven for 77 he took against New Zealand, he has since added eight for 80 against Pakistan at Headingley, and a ridiculous eight for 35 off 27 mainly unplayable overs at Lord’s. He has been player of the match in all three, improving his career-best match figures each time. With the third Test at Edgbaston still to come and England eyeing a whitewash, his summer’s work amounts to 23 wickets at 8.34 – the kind of numbers more normally associated with cricket from the 19th century, when batting techniques were rudimentary and pitches even more of a lottery than Lord’s has been of late. Of the five Tests England have played this summer, they have won the three in which Robinson has appeared, and lost the two in which he has not. The evidence is beginning to suggest it is no coincidence. There may never have been a better moment for Ollie Robinson to have made his return to Test cricket than the summer of 2026 Joe Root has backed Robinson and the rewards have come - he has been player of the match in all three Tests he has played this summer

Your browser does not support iframes.

So where has it all gone right? In essence, several factors have come together at the same time, allowing Robinson to make the best use of his height and accuracy, as well as the wobble-seam tactics that leave bowlers as unsure as batsmen which way the ball will deviate. For a start, Robinson’s three Tests have all taken place in favourable conditions: two at Lord’s, where the sideways movement has been lavish and the bounce variable, and one at Headingley, which on a cloudy day remains the spiritual home of English swing and seam. Then there’s the mediocrity of the Pakistan batting lineup, which is yet to reach 200 in four innings this summer, and has managed only two half-centuries. On and off the pitch, the tourists are a shambles. Finally, this year’s batch of Dukes balls is proving especially helpful. Root suggested after his side’s 194-run win on Sunday that they now have a lacquer on the seam itself, and that its hardness has created dents in the pitch for the bowlers to exploit. By way of evidence, he said bats were being cracked in practice. Dukes deny they have done anything differently, but Root – who keeps getting out lbw – disagrees. For tall, accurate seamers like 6ft 5in Robinson, hammering the ball into the surface time and again and waiting for the deviation has become cricket’s answer to the Chinese water torture. Of his 23 wickets this summer, 11 have been lbw and five bowled. But it would be unfair to ascribe all his success to external factors. After all, in the three Tests Robinson has featured in this summer, his haul of 23 wickets at 192 has outstripped Josh Tongue’s 18 for 250, Gus Atkinson’s eight for 164 and Jofra Archer’s eight for 175. And, of the quartet, only Robinson now boasts a Test average below 20 – the first England bowler with at least 50 wickets to do so since Frank Tyson in the 1950s. Most importantly, perhaps, he now feels comfortable in his own skin. The wisdom in the Bazball era, often made explicit by managing director Rob Key, was that he was no good to man nor beast while operating at 75mph, but among the best in the world at 82mph. Yet Robinson is slower now than when he first played for England, five years ago. His average speed so far in this series is 78.12mph, the least rapid of the ten Test series in which he has played, and more than 4mph slower than his quickest: 82.74mph against South Africa in 2022. For tall, accurate seamers like 6ft 5in Robinson, hammering the ball into the surface time and again and waiting for the deviation has become cricket’s answer to the Chinese water torture His new-ball alliance with his Jofra Archer (left) has proved a mesmerising study in contrasts – Robinson threatening their pads, stumps and outside edges, Archer examining their reflexes Even this summer, he has eased up as he has gone along: an average of 79.50mph against New Zealand, followed by 78.39 against Pakistan at Headingley and 77.82 at Lord’s – closer to what the management previously regarded as the unacceptable end of the spectrum. Thanks to the existence of his 90mph colleagues Archer, Tongue and Atkinson, it is a scenario about which both he and England are intensely relaxed. ‘Being able to be my own bowler and not trying to be too attacking has definitely helped,’ said Robinson after Lord’s. ‘With those guys at the other end, it does allow me just to sit in, be very consistent, be very patient, which is my super strength. I probably wouldn’t have picked up those wickets in this series without those other guys.’ In particular, his new-ball alliance with his Sussex colleague Archer has, for Pakistan, proved a mesmerising study in contrasts – Robinson threatening their pads, stumps and outside edges, Archer examining their reflexes and ticker. Equally, Robinson’s economy-rate this summer of 2.4, meaner than any of his team-mates, has meant that the absence of a frontline spinner able to keep opponents in check has not mattered. Might England have fared better in the Ashes last winter had he been available? We’ll never know, though Robinson himself said he wasn’t match-ready. But he says he has worked harder than ever on his fitness, while Stokes and McCullum, who became so wound up by his attitude during the tour of India in early 2024 that they washed their hands of him, are no longer on the scene. Not that Robinson intends to lapse into the complacency of old. ‘We’ve just got to be careful we don’t get too comfortable in this four-man attack,’ he said. He seems a more perceptive cricketer now, in more ways than one.

Sports.title: 'Fans have been walking away for years - the people asking questions of the WRU are not the problem': Welsh rugby's civil war deepens as critics' leader hits back at claims scrutiny has been 'toxic'
Sports.content:
'Fans have been walking away for years - the people asking questions of the WRU are not the problem': Welsh rugby's civil war deepens as critics' leader hits back at claims scrutiny has been 'toxic'

Unlock more of the best of our rugby coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Hayley Parsons OBE, a leading critic of the Welsh Rugby Union, has hit out at the governing body and claimed Wales’ national game has ‘deteriorated on all fronts’ under the current regime, refuting the views of WRU chief executive Abi Tierney that she has led ‘toxic’ attacks on its leadership.

The WRU have come under intense fire for their plan to cut one of Wales’ four men’s domestic teams by 2028 amid significant sporting and financial challenges.

Parsons, who was a director at Cardiff Rugby until last year and is one of the country's most successful businesspeople having founded GoCompare, has led the criticism, as part of a 'coalition of the willing' alongside former Wales internationals Jonathan Davies and Tom Shanklin.

In an exclusive interview with Daily Mail Sport last week, Tierney hit back at Parsons and Co, accusing them of ‘toxic tactics’ and insisting the consequences would be ‘cataclysmic’ for Welsh rugby if the proposal to move to three sides didn’t happen.

In July, the WRU confirmed that Cardiff – who are owned by the governing body – and the Newport-based Dragons were given first refusal on licences to continue, leaving one spot in West Wales for the Ospreys and Scarlets to fight for.

‘I have a lot of respect for several members of the board and my issue has never been about individuals,’ Parsons told Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s about whether the collective leadership of the WRU is working and if you look at the facts, we’re now three years into the current regime and the landscape has deteriorated on all fronts.

Hayley Parsons (left), leader of the 'coalition of the willing' has hit back at claims from Abi Tierney (right) she is leading a 'toxic' campaign to remove the Welsh Rugby Union hierarchy

It has been a torrid few years for Welsh rugby on and off the pitch, with Parsons insisting 'the landscape has deteriorated on all fronts'

'Criticism and asking for accountability given the current situation are not personal attacks and to suggest those questioning the WRU are responsible for falling ticket sales, sponsorship difficulties or damage to the Welsh rugby brand is quite extraordinary.

‘Sadly, the supporters have been walking away for years and Welsh rugby’s problems were not created by the people now asking questions about them.’

Parsons and Shanklin have both called for the entire WRU board to resign on the basis they believe they are not fit to lead Welsh rugby. But such a scenario is far from simple under complex governance rules.

A vote of no confidence in the WRU would have to come from a minimum of 10 per cent of the WRU’s near 300 member clubs forcing an extraordinary general meeting (EGM). In April, that threshold was met but the clubs then asked for the EGM to be cancelled at the last minute after then WRU chair Richard Collier-Keywood confirmed he would be leaving.

That EGM took place anyway, with the WRU insisting it must do so. Parsons said the ‘coalition of the willing’ will speak to WRU member clubs to see if there is an appetite for a second EGM this year.

The WRU insist there is no other option than to cut a team, but their critics have said the way the situation has been handled has been poor, also citing a lack of evidence for the decision. The WRU have said their decision has not been made easily and has been based on rigorous research.

‘I have never taken a position on whether Wales should have three or four professional teams,’ said Parsons, whose previous criticism of both former WRU chief executive Steve Phillips and Collier-Keywood led to their departures. ‘I have yet to see any full evidence or business case required to make such an enormous decision. My concerns are around the governance, transparency and processes by which we have arrived here.

'The only voice that matters now is the clubs. I think the public argument has now gone far enough. The clubs are the shareholders of Welsh rugby and they must now decide whether they have confidence in the current board and executive leadership to take the game forward. Now is the time to act. We are in a small window of opportunity.

'Do we act now or live with the outcome until a further three years has passed? And where will we be then? Down to two regions and an even more inward-looking landscape?

The Ospreys and Scarlets are now battling against each other to survive, with only one spot remaining for a professional team in West Wales

'Over the coming weeks, we will be engaging privately and respectfully with clubs and asking them a very simple question – do you have confidence in the current leadership of the WRU to lead Welsh rugby for the next three years?

'If over 50 per cent of clubs tell us they do, I will accept that democratic verdict and walk away. However, if 50 per cent or more tell us they do not and are prepared to vote accordingly, then an EGM should follow.

‘I have nothing to gain from this campaign. I’m just using my own platform to speak out where others are afraid to. I desperately want to try and make things better.

‘This isn’t about personalities anymore. It’s about the future of Welsh rugby and creating a future that ultimately belongs to its clubs.’

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
