World.title: Phillips Consulting presents PASGA Report, setting the evidence base for a more capable, future-ready Federal Civil Service
World.content:
Phillips Consulting (pcl.), the Lead Consultant for the Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis (PASGA) project, formally presented the PASGA Report, marking the official closeout of the landmark exercise designed to provide an evidence-based foundation for strengthening the capacity, effectiveness and future-readiness of Nigeria’s Federal Civil Service.

The report presentation represents a significant milestone in an initiative that has brought together personnel verification, workforce analytics and skills assessment to generate a more comprehensive understanding of the people, capabilities and institutional requirements of the Federal Civil Service.

Beyond establishing a clearer picture of the Civil Service workforce, PASGA provides actionable insights to support the next phase of public sector transformation, helping government understand where its workforce stands today, where critical capability gaps exist, and what must be done to build the skills and institutions required for tomorrow.

As Lead Consultant, Phillips Consulting worked alongside 15 cluster consultants, namely Workforce Group, StransformLimited, Pivotage Consulting, MacTay Consulting, TWPC Tech, Knewrow Performance Engineering, Zimedy Services Ltd., Evo & Hogg Limited, GEORGID Consulting, Greenfields Consultancy and Allied Services Ltd., QriosityInternational Limited, 1StepAhead Consulting, Premium-Gold Resources Consulting, Time-Line Consult Limited and Saddat Unique Services Ltd., to deliver the nationwide exercise, bringing together expertise, technology, workforce analytics and project management capabilities to support the successful execution of the assignment across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A key value of the PASGA Report is its ability to move the conversation beyond personnel numbers to workforce intelligence and capability development.

The report presents key findings from the exercise, including outcomes from the personnel verification process and insights from the skills gap analysis conducted across the Federal Civil Service.

Among other areas, the report provides:

Key findings from the PASGA exercise highlight significant insights emerging from the nationwide assessment.

Verification outcomes, providing an evidence-based view of personnel records across participating MDAs.

Skills gap analysis outcomes, identifying the areas in which capability gaps exist and the skills that require greater attention across the Federal Civil Service.

Capability development priorities, highlighting areas where targeted learning, reskilling, upskilling, and workforce development interventions can have the greatest impact.

Personnel profiles for individual MDAs, providing a more granular view of workforce composition and capabilities across Ministries, Departments and Agencies.

Strategic recommendations to support workforce optimisation, capability development, and institutional effectiveness.

For MDAs, the insights provide a basis for more strategic workforce planning, targeted capability development, and improved deployment of talent.

This shift is particularly important as the nature of public service continues to evolve, with digitalisation, emerging technologies, changing citizen expectations and increasingly complex policy and service-delivery demands requiring new and enhanced capabilities.

The PASGA Report is therefore positioned not simply as a record of an audit but as an actionable instrument for transformation.

Its Reform Implementation Roadmap provides a structured direction for translating the findings into action, with recommendations spanning immediate priorities, medium-term interventions, and longer-term reforms.

The roadmap is intended to support stakeholders in progressively strengthening workforce capability, institutional effectiveness, and the overall performance of the Federal Civil Service.

By establishing a common evidence base, PASGA creates an opportunity for government and MDAs to make more informed decisions about people, skills, structures and capability investments.

World.title: Four family members die in Kwara building collapse
World.content:
Four members of the same family have died after a three-storey building collapsed at the Popo Giwa area of Ilorin, Kwara State, on Tuesday morning.

The collapse occurred at about 5 a.m. at No. 41 Popo Giwa Street, beside Gogoro Mosque, trapping eight family members, according to the Kwara State Fire Service and the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA).

The fire service said four people were rescued alive, while four others were recovered dead from the rubble.

The agency’s spokesperson, Hassan Adekunle, who spoke with reporters at the scene, said emergency responders were alerted to the incident at about 5 a.m.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We have recovered four people dead and rescued four people alive,” Mr Adekunle said.

He said the fire service immediately mobilised to the scene and began rescue operations with other emergency agencies.

“This kind of situation is not something the fire service can handle alone,” he said, adding that officials of the Hospitals Management Board, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other agencies joined the operation.

An excavator was deployed to the scene as rescuers worked to gain access to those trapped under the debris.

An eyewitness, Abdulganiy Musa, told PUNCH that the family’s father was a serving soldier, while the mother was a casual worker at the Michael Imoudu National Institute for Labour Studies in Ilorin.

One of the children, identified as Firdaus, was among those rescued alive during the operation.

The SEMA Secretary, Magaji Saadudeen, also confirmed that eight people were trapped in the building.

“The rescued persons are receiving treatment presently,” Mr Saadudeen said.

He added that the bodies of the deceased and the rescued victims were taken to a hospital.

Building structure

The Kwara State Commissioner of Police, Ojo Adekimi, said the collapsed section was the boys’ quarters of the three-storey building.

“It was a three-storey building that collapsed. Our findings showed that the boys’ quarter of the building collapsed. Information gathered revealed that eight people were trapped in the building,” Mr Adekimi said.

He said all occupants had been evacuated from the main building while authorities assessed the remaining structure.

“For now, the situation is under control. We will examine the remaining building and see how people can be secured. But for now, we have evacuated everybody from the main building,” the commissioner said.

He urged residents to pay attention to warning signs such as leakages and other structural defects and to evacuate buildings where they notice signs of possible failure.

Mr Adekunle said the actual cause of the collapse would be determined after a proper assessment of the structure.

“We are only here to ascertain the actual cause of this collapse and rescue the trapped victims. As at when due, we will communicate to the media about our findings,” he said.

He added that relevant authorities would take appropriate action if the assessment showed that the building required demolition.

Government reaction

During a visit to the scene, the Commissioner for Education and Human Capital Development, Lawal Olohungbebe, described the incident as unfortunate and expressed condolences to the victims’ families.

“The rescue mission began immediately after the collapse, and to the grace of God, some were rescued, but unfortunately, we have to take it as this,” he said.

Mr Olohungbebe said the road leading to the building was accessible, helping emergency responders reach the scene quickly.

“One of the things that made it very easy for us to rescue the few people we were able to rescue is the access route,” he said.

He urged residents and developers to comply with building and town-planning regulations, particularly requirements concerning access roads to residential areas.

The commissioner commended the Ministries of Health and Environment, the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria, SEMA, the National Emergency Management Agency, the Fire Service, the Civil Defence, the Red Cross, and other agencies involved in the rescue operation.

The Chairman of Ilorin West Local Government Area, AbdulRahman Ladan, said six to seven ambulances were deployed to evacuate victims from the scene.

Mr Ladan urged residents to report structural defects promptly and leave buildings when they observe signs of possible collapse.

“Whenever you discover something like this, please escalate it. Get to the point of evacuating yourself and your family members from that building. Life is the priority,” he said.

He also advised developers to use high-quality building materials and engage qualified professionals to supervise construction, saying that compliance with building standards was essential to preventing structural failures.

World.title: Diphtheria outbreak kills 15, infects 117 in Plateau
World.content:
An outbreak of diphtheria in parts of Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State has killed 15 people among 117 suspected cases reported, health authorities have said.

The Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO) for Jos North, Baks Bulus, disclosed this on Tuesday during an interaction with journalists in Jos.

Mr Bulus said the deaths were recorded within three days of the outbreak, warning that the number of cases could increase if urgent measures were not taken to contain the disease.

“So far, according to the data we have gathered from the communities, 117 people are suspected to have contracted the disease. Out of this number, we have already recorded 15 deaths,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Among those who died were two siblings aged between 12 and 17 years, according to the official.

Diphtheria is a bacterial infection that can spread from person to person, particularly through close contact with an infected person, Mr Bulus explained.

He said sharing personal items such as utensils and towels could increase the risk of transmission.

According to him, vaccination remains one of the most effective ways of preventing severe complications and deaths from the disease.

“For children who have been vaccinated, the effects may be milder and may not lead to death. But for a child who has not been fully vaccinated or has not completed the required doses, it can be deadly,” he said.

Mr Bulus urged residents of the affected communities to maintain good hygiene, avoid overcrowded places, and seek medical attention promptly if they develop symptoms suspected of being associated with diphtheria.

He also cautioned residents against self-medication or relying solely on patent medicine vendors.

“Most times, people resort to chemists and self-medication, which we do not advise. The best approach is to visit primary healthcare centres where we have the necessary structures and personnel in place,” he said.

The DSNO said health workers had been deployed to affected communities to intensify disease surveillance, sensitise residents and support efforts to prevent further transmission.

He urged parents and guardians to ensure that children receive the recommended doses of diphtheria-containing vaccines.

Meanwhile, efforts to obtain further details from the Plateau State Ministry of Health were unsuccessful.

The State Epidemiologist, Maren Job, did not respond to calls placed to her phone.

World.title: Police arrest 1,334 suspects, rescue 383 kidnap victims
World.content:
The Nigeria Police Force has arrested 1,334 suspects and rescued 383 kidnapped victims nationwide during intelligence-led operations conducted in July and August.

The ​‌‌‍​‌‍⁠⁠‌‍​⁠‍​⁠⁠‌‌​Force Public Relations Officer, Anietie Inedu, a chief superintendent of police, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja at the Joint Security News Briefing by security and law enforcement agencies.

Mr Inedu said the operations also led to the recovery of 175 firearms, more than 3,790 rounds of live ammunition, 93 vehicles and several rustled cattle.

He said 127 notorious criminals were neutralised during decisive engagements with police operatives and other security forces across the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the achievements reflected the force’s deployment of intelligence-led and technology-driven policing, enhanced inter-agency collaboration and tactical operations.

He said police tactical teams also successfully prevented a large-scale attack after engaging a heavily armed group of about 240 bandits, with 17 of the assailants neutralised.

Mr Inedu said joint security operations also rescued 32 kidnapped victims at Maikujera in Rabah Local Government Area of Sokoto State.

He added that another operation at Amla-Cho Forest forced armed bandits to abandon 13 kidnapped victims, who were subsequently rescued unhurt.

The police spokesperson said collaborative operations involving the police, vigilantes and other security actors also resulted in the rescue of 76 victims in separate incidents.

He said police operatives recorded significant successes against kidnapping networks in Kogi, Kaduna, Imo, Nasarawa and other states during the period.

According to him, six victims were rescued after gunmen attacked two vehicles along the Kabba-Ayere Road, while nine others were rescued in a separate incident along the Mameramo-Adomu Road.

Mr Inedu said police operatives also disrupted the activities of an IPOB/ESN network in Imo, neutralising a suspected kingpin and recovering two AK-47 rifles, four empty magazines and a vehicle.

He said police operations further yielded significant results in arms interdiction, including the recovery of 551 rounds of AK-47 ammunition and 10 loaded magazines from a female suspect intercepted along the Doma-Yelwa Road.

The FPRO said a follow-up operation led to the arrest of another suspect linked to the ammunition supply network, while additional investigations exposed a wider criminal network.

He said police also recovered 870 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition from suspected gun-runners in another operation.

Mr Inedu said operatives arrested three suspects linked to the 29 June attack on police officers at Aluu Division, recovering two AK-47 rifles stolen during the incident.

He added that another operation led to the arrest of 18 suspects and recovery of 47 firearms, 12 stolen vehicles and 420 rounds of ammunition.

READ ALSO: Police fire tear gas at pensioners protesting arrears at Lagos House

According to him, police operations also targeted cultism, armed robbery and other violent crimes, with 37 suspected cult members arrested during a disrupted initiation ceremony.

He said anti-kidnapping operatives arrested a native doctor linked to an earlier abduction and murder case, recovering two double-barrel guns and one single-barrel gun.

Mr Inedu said the force would sustain intelligence-led operations, inter-agency cooperation and community engagement to further degrade criminal networks.

“The Nigeria Police Force remains resolute in its commitment to securing the nation,” he said.

He commended police officers for their sacrifices and professionalism, assuring Nigerians of the force’s continued commitment to public safety and the protection of lives and property.

World.title: Nigerian military conducts 7,062 operations, kills 1,487 terrorists
World.content:
The Defence Headquarters (DHQ) has said the military conducted 7,062 security operations across the country in July and August, neutralising 1,487 terrorists and insurgents and rescuing 777 kidnapped victims.

The Director of Defence Information (DDI), Samaila Uba, a Major General, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja at the Joint Security News Briefing by security and law enforcement agencies.

Mr Uba said the operations were conducted through coordinated land, air and maritime efforts targeting terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, arms trafficking, oil theft and other criminal activities.

He said troops also arrested 354 suspects, recovered 91 firearms, 1,331 rounds of ammunition and 44 improvised explosive devices during the operations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the military’s operations are aimed at degrading criminal capabilities, disrupting logistics networks, rescuing victims and protecting communities and critical national infrastructure.

“The Armed Forces of Nigeria remain committed to defeating all forms of criminality threatening national security,” he said.

Mr Uba said the troops sustained offensive operations across all six geopolitical zones in response to emerging threats, including terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, armed robbery and attacks on communities.

He said the operations also focused on countering separatist violence, disrupting crude oil theft and illegal refining, and dismantling criminal networks and their support structures.

He said the military recorded significant gains in the North-east, where troops of Operation HADIN KAI neutralised 309 Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province fighters and arrested several suspected collaborators and logistics facilitators.

The defence spokesperson said troops also rescued hundreds of persons held in terrorist enclaves, while sustained pressure compelled terrorist fighters and their families to surrender in several locations.

He said the military’s operations in other theatres also resulted in the rescue of hundreds of kidnapped victims and the disruption of terrorist and criminal movements.

He said the armed forces also recorded notable successes through intelligence-led operations, targeted raids, clearance operations and coordinated rescue missions.

He said the air component maintained consistent combat support and reconnaissance for ground formations, enhancing the military’s ability to locate and engage hostile elements.

“On the non-kinetic front, nine dialogue and peace-building initiatives were undertaken, alongside 15 stakeholder engagement meetings with traditional and religious leaders,” he said.

Mr Uba added that the military issued 137 press releases during the period and identified and countered 13 instances of misinformation.

He said no major border or transnational security incident, critical infrastructure vandalism, prison break or threat to pipelines, railways and highways was recorded during the reporting period.

The DDI said the operational successes reflected the value of joint military operations, inter-agency cooperation and community support.

He urged Nigerians to remain vigilant and provide timely and actionable intelligence to security agencies to support ongoing operations.

Mr Uba also acknowledged the support and strategic guidance of President Bola Tinubu, the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, in strengthening military capacity and operational effectiveness.

He commended military personnel and other security agencies for their sacrifices, while urging the media to continue to report security matters accurately and responsibly.

World.title: Kwara Assembly Sacks Two APC Members Who Defected to PDP
World.content:
*It is a political persecution, says PDP

Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The Kwara State House of Assembly has sacked two members of the parliament over their recent defection from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to the opposition, Peoples Democratic Party(PDP) in the state.

Consequently, the house has declared the seats of the two affected lawmakers vacant with immediate effect.

The two affected lawmakers Hon. Saba Yisa Gideon of Edu State Constituency and Hon. Olusola Odetundun of Irepodun State Constituency recently dumped the APC for the PDP and later picked the tickets of their respective state constituencies for 2027 elections.

However, at a sitting of the state House of Assembly Tuesday, a letter from the APC State Chairman, Mr. Sunday Fagbemi, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Salihu Yakubu Danladi, was read on the floor of the house on the defection of the two lawmakers.

The letter, however, requested vacation of the seats of the two lawmakers in accordance with Section 109 (1g) (2) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended.

The letter stated that since the two members were elected under the APC and there was no division within the party, they have no constitutional right to abandon the party for another.

Leading the debate on the request, the Leader of the House, Hon. Abdulkadir Oba Magaji, emphasized that the matter is constitutional, as outlined in Section 109 (1g) of the Constitution, which stipulates that a member shall not belong to another party than the one that brought him to power, as long as his tenure has not yet expired.

He noted that the two concerned Hon. members have left the APC for the PDP and are seeking reelection to their seats in the opposition party, a development that contravenes the Constitution.

The Leader supported the request that their seats be declared vacant in accordance with the law.

Other lawmakers who spoke in favour of the vacation included Hon. Abolarin Ganiyu Gabriel of Ekiti Constituency, Hon. Ganiyu Folabi Salahu of Omupo Constituency, and Hon. Oguniyi David Sheun of Ojomu/Balogun Constituency.

The Speaker of the House, Hon. Salihu Yakubu Danladi, therefore declared the seats of the two defecting members vacant in accordance with Section 109 (1) (g) (2) of 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended.

Meanwhile, the opposition, PDP in the state has described the sacking of the two lawmakers that left APC for PDP as illegal and unconstitutional.

A statement issued in Ilorin on Tuesday signed by the Publicity Secretary of the party, Mr. Olusegun Olusola Adewara also described the move as political persecution.

The statement warned that sacking the two affected lawmakers over their political affiliation would deprive their constituents of effective representation.

According to the party, “Our party considers such a move a dangerous descent into political intolerance and an unacceptable attempt to weaponise the legislature against elected representatives whose only apparent offence is the exercise of their political choice”.

The opposition party acknowledged the constitutional powers of the House of Assembly to regulate its internal affairs under Section 101 of the 1999 Constitution, but stressed that such powers must be exercised within the limits of the Constitution and democratic principles.

It warned that any suspension based solely on their defection would amount to using legislative authority to settle partisan political scores while denying the people of the two constituencies their voices on the floor of the Assembly.

World.title: Tinubu: We Must Translate Macroeconomic Stability Into Microeconomic Prosperity
World.content:
• Nigerians must carefully evaluate Atiku’s promise to return fuel subsidy

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has said that his administration must translate macroeconomic stability into microeconomic prosperity in the next phase of Renewed Hope.

He added that the country’s macroeconomic stability must translate to more food, more jobs, lower inflation, affordable credit, reliable power, more manufacturing, greater exports and stronger purchasing power

Tinubu, who was represented by the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, disclosed this at the second edition of the Asiwaju Scorecard Series/Asiwaju Policy Roundtable held on Tuesday in Abuja.

He recalled that when he assumed office on May 29, 2023, Nigeria faced a difficult economic inheritance, especially with fuel subsidy distortions, multiple exchange-rate windows, weak revenue mobilisation, foreign-exchange shortages, rising debt-service pressures and years of inadequate investment in critical infrastructure.

The president said he understood that Nigeria could not continue on that trajectory and therefore took difficult decisions, including the removal of the fuel subsidy and the reform of the foreign-exchange market.

Tinubu added that the evidence increasingly showed that the foundation was strengthening, with Nigeria’s gross external reserves having risen to about $52.7 billion by August 2026.

He emphasised that consolidated non-oil revenue increased from approximately N13.63 trillion in 2023 to N16.4 trillion in the first two quarters of 2026, demonstrating the growing contribution of non-oil sources to government revenue.

Tinubu stated: “Our trade position has also improved dramatically: from a merchandise trade surplus of only about N44.8 billion for the whole of 2023 to approximately N7.54 trillion in the first quarter of 2026 alone.

“Real GDP grew by 4.43 per cent in Q2 2026, while inflation has fallen significantly from its earlier peak to about 15.4 per cent.

“These figures do not mean that our economic challenges have disappeared, but they demonstrate that the direction of travel has changed. And let me emphasise: macroeconomic stability is not the destination; it is the foundation.

“The ultimate test is when stability translates into cheaper food, more jobs, affordable credit, reliable electricity and greater purchasing power for Nigerians.

“Most Nigerians have asked, why the ambitious $1 trillion economy by Mr President? The $1 trillion economy is not merely a number, but a national mission: a Nigeria that produces more, exports more, attracts more investment, creates more jobs and gives its young people a greater stake in the future.

“You cannot build a $1 trillion economy on inadequate infrastructure. That is why the Renewed Hope Agenda places major emphasis on strategic highways, railways, ports, energy infrastructure and digital connectivity. But we must think beyond individual projects.

Tinubu said Nigeria must now take full advantage of its enormous maritime opportunity by developing an integrated five-port maritime and logistics corridor.

According to him, “Our strategic ambition should be to develop and connect five major deep-sea ports at Lagos, Ondo, Ibom, Port Harcourt and Calabar, linking them by modern rail and road infrastructure, with the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Super Highway serving as the principal coastal road spine.”

The president stressed that vision does not stop at the coastline, saying the Western Corridor would connect the maritime gateways to the interior through the Lagos–Abuja–Kaduna–Kano rail corridor, complemented by the Sokoto–Badagry Super Highway, thereby opening a direct trade route from the Atlantic coast to the markets of the North-west and the Sahel.

He explained that the Eastern Corridor would connect the eastern maritime gateways through the Port Harcourt–Abuja–Kaduna–Kano rail corridor, complemented by the proposed Calabar–Maiduguri Trans-Sahara Super Highway, creating a second major east-to-north trade route.

His words: “In this way, Nigeria can create an integrated national transport system in which our five deep-sea ports are connected to one another, connected to our major cities and production centres, and connected ultimately to the landlocked markets of Niger, Chad, Burkina Faso, Sudan and the Central African Republic.

“This is how Nigeria can move beyond being simply a coastal trading nation to becoming the maritime gateway and logistics hub of West and Central Africa, capturing a much larger share of the continent’s trade, logistics, manufacturing and distribution value chain.

“That is more than transportation infrastructure, but a trade architecture. It would generate opportunities in logistics, warehousing, freight forwarding, customs, banking, insurance, manufacturing, distribution and agro-processing.”

The president said it would create jobs, generate foreign exchange and strengthen Nigeria’s position as a regional commercial hub.

Tinubu noted that his administration would develop industrial parks, export-processing zones, logistics parks, agro-processing clusters and manufacturing centres along these corridors.

He said: “Where rail reaches an agricultural region, processing industries should follow. Where it reaches mineral resources, processing and manufacturing should follow.

“Where dry ports are established, logistics and distribution businesses should develop around them. This is how infrastructure becomes an engine of economic growth.

“Our ambition must extend beyond individual ports to a genuinely integrated maritime economy covering port operations, shipping, maritime logistics, ship repair, marine services, maritime finance, insurance, fisheries, aquaculture, offshore energy, coastal tourism and marine technology.”

The president pointed out that a good GDP number does not automatically put food on a family’s table, while stronger reserves do not pay school fees and a stronger stock market does not automatically put money into the pocket of a market woman.

He added: “Therefore, we are in the next phase of Renewed Hope which must translate macroeconomic stability into microeconomic prosperity: more food, more jobs, lower inflation, affordable credit, reliable power, more manufacturing, greater exports and stronger purchasing power.

“As we approach 2027, Nigerians will hear many promises. Some will promise to reverse the reforms; others will promise prosperity without confronting the structural problems that brought us here. The question is whether we go backwards or consolidate and improve the progress we have begun.

“Do we abandon infrastructure investment or accelerate it? Do we discourage investors or make Nigeria one of Africa’s preferred investment destinations? Do we allow our ports to serve primarily our domestic economy or position Nigeria as a maritime gateway to the wider African hinterland?

“For the All Progressives Congress, the answer is clear. We choose progress, productivity, investment, infrastructure, innovation, Nigerian enterprise, exports, human capital, and we choose President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. And we choose the ambition of a $1 trillion Nigerian economy by 2030 by Mr President for our common prosperity.”

Earlier, the Chairman, Board of Trustees (BoT), APC Professional Forum, Dr. Isa Yuguda, said the 2027 presidential election should be about issues, achievements and realistic solutions.

He stressed that one of the most significant reforms of the Tinubu administration was the removal of fuel subsidy.

The former governor of Bauchi State said to understand this decision, Nigerians must appreciate its historical context.

According to him, “As Chairman of the Fuel Subsidy Task Force in 2009, I led a committee that examined the subsidy regime and uncovered serious irregularities, fraudulent practices, and financial leakages that placed a huge burden on the Nigerian economy.”

Yuguda explained that the subsidy system had become inefficient and consumed enormous public resources that could have been invested in education, security, agriculture, healthcare, infrastructure, and other productive sectors.

Its removal, he added, was therefore a difficult but necessary reform intended to redirect national resources towards long-term development.

Yuguda noted that President Tinubu demonstrated the political courage to implement a reform that previous administrations had acknowledged as necessary but could not fully execute.

He said: “The additional fiscal space created by the subsidy reform has strengthened the capacity of the federal, state and local governments to address critical national priorities, with over N15 trillion reportedly saved following the removal of fuel subsidy.

“In the education sector, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) is expanding access to higher education and reducing financial barriers for students. In the security sector, increased funding, improved operational support, and substantial investment in modern equipment are strengthening the capacity of the armed forces and other security agencies to protect lives, property, and strategic national assets.

“Nevertheless, Nigeria continues to confront serious security challenges arising partly from instability in some neighbouring countries, porous borders, and the cross-border movement of armed groups and criminal networks into Nigerian territory.

“These external pressures have complicated the Federal Government’s security efforts and, in some instances, enabled terrorist and criminal elements to infiltrate communities and perpetrate violence.

“The administration must therefore continue strengthening border security, intelligence gathering, regional security cooperation, surveillance capabilities, and the operational capacity of security agencies to consolidate the progress already being recorded.

“As we approach the 2027 elections, Nigerians must carefully evaluate political promises, particularly those relating to the return of fuel subsidy. The proposal by former Vice-President, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, to restore subsidy may appear attractive to citizens seeking immediate relief, but it must be examined against our national experience.

“The old subsidy regime was associated with massive leakages, fraudulent claims, inefficiency, and a significant drain on public finances. Presenting a return to that system without clearly addressing these problems risks misleading Nigerians for short-term political gain and could reverse the fiscal space now supporting critical national investments.

“Every Nigerian has the democratic right to present alternative policies, but economic choices must be guided by facts, experience, sustainability, and the long-term interest of the country.

“Having chaired the 2009 Fuel Subsidy Task Force and witnessed the weaknesses of that system firsthand, I believe Nigerians deserve an honest conversation about what subsidy truly cost the nation and what can now be achieved when those resources are directed towards education, security, agriculture, infrastructure, and other areas that improve citizens’ lives.”

World.title: PDP Chief Dan Orbih is Dead
World.content:
Chief Daniel Osi Orbih, a former Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Edo State and

National Vice-Chairman for the South-South zone, has died.

Orbih passed away on Monday, according to a statement issued on behalf of the Orbih family by Francis Udukhomoi Orbih, Esq.

The family announced his death with “profound sadness and a heavy heart,” while expressing total submission to the will of God.

The deceased was survived by his wife, Mrs. Florence Orbih; his children, Ms. Winifred Anwosiobor Orbih and Dr. Mildred Omonemi Orbih; his brothers and sisters, and other members of his extended family.

Orbih served as Chairman of the Edo State chapter of the PDP from 2008 to 2019, making him one of the longest-serving state party chairmen in Nigeria.

He also served as the PDP National Vice-Chairman for the South-South zone.

The family appealed to relatives, friends and well-wishers to remember them in their prayers as they mourn the loss.

“Further details will be announced in due course,” the statement said.

The family prayed that the deceased’s soul would “rest in perfect peace.”

World.title: Alausa Expands National Tertiary Institutions’ Ranking, Makes Participation Compulsory
World.content:
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has expanded Nigeria’s national tertiary education ranking framework to cover universities, polytechnics and colleges of education.

‎This is contained in a statement issued on Tuesday in Abuja by the Special Adviser to the Minister on Media and Communications, Mr Ikharo Attah.

‎Attah quoted Alausa to have announced the development at a meeting with the Nigerian Universities Ranking Advisory Committee (NURAC), adding that participation was now compulsory for all tertiary institutions.

‎Alausa said the expanded ranking framework was part of President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms under the Renewed Hope Agenda, implemented through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI).

‎According to him, the initiative is aimed at strengthening quality, accountability, institutional performance and global competitiveness across Nigeria’s tertiary education system.

‎“The ranking will provide institutions with clear benchmarks for assessing their performance, identifying areas requiring improvement and measuring progress, while promoting healthy competition and continuous institutional advancement,” he said.

‎Alausa said that the 2026/2027 ranking exercise for universities would commence in September, while the committee would determine the appropriate timeline for extending the exercise to polytechnics and colleges of education.

‎He added that the Federal Government would provide funding for the exercise through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund).

The minister stated that TETFund would develop guidelines to institutionalise the ranking and formally communicate to vice-chancellors and heads of other tertiary institutions that participation was compulsory.

‎He reassured the committee of the ministry’s commitment to providing the policy direction, funding and capacity-building support required to make the ranking credible, sustainable and impactful.

‎“The ministry will work with the committee to facilitate in-service training and institutional capacity-building programmes across tertiary institutions, with the expectation that significantly more Nigerian institutions will achieve greater global recognition in subsequent international ranking exercises,” Alausa said.

‎Alausa reiterated the commitment of the Federal Ministry of Education to ensure that the ranking framework became a credible tool for driving quality, accountability and continuous improvement in Nigeria’s tertiary education sector.

‎On her part, the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad, described the initiative as a significant step towards strengthening accountability and quality across the tertiary education system.

‎Ahmad said healthy competition was essential to encourage institutions to assess their performance, address identified gaps and consistently improve the quality of education they provide.

‎“Ranking should cover both public and private institutions, as this will provide a mechanism for establishing and maintaining minimum standards across the sector,” she said.

‎Ahmad assured the committee of the ministry’s full support, saying the exercise would help institutions understand their strengths and weaknesses and drive measurable improvements as the nation’s tertiary education system continued to expand.

‎Also, the Chairman of NURAC, Emeritus Prof. Peter Okebukola, congratulated President Tinubu on the increasing number of Nigerian universities gaining global recognition.

‎Okebukola, also the former Executive Secretary of the National Universities Commission (NUC), called for greater investment in university education to accelerate the progress.

‎“The committee’s mandate has now been expanded to cover polytechnics and colleges of education, leading to its transformation into the Nigerian Tertiary Education Ranking Advisory Committee,” he said.

‎Okebukola expressed optimism that sustained investment, stronger institutional capacity and the new national ranking framework would enable more Nigerian institutions to make significant progress in international rankings.

‎He said the initiative would also enable Nigerian tertiary institutions to compete more confidently with leading institutions globally. ‎(NAN)

World.title: U.S. Troop ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‌‍​⁠‍‍⁠​‍‌​Drawdown Won’t Weaken Nigeria’s Security Partnership, Says DHQ
World.content:
The Defence Headquarters (DHQ) has said the planned drawdown of more than 200 U.S. personnel from Nigeria will not affect the enduring security partnership between both countries.

Director of Defence Information, Maj.-Gen. Samaila Uba, gave the assurance on Tuesday in Abuja while responding to questions at the Joint Security news briefing.

Uba said the withdrawal should not be interpreted as a breakdown or termination of Nigeria’s security cooperation with the United States.

“The relationship between Nigeria and the United States remains strong, enduring and mutually beneficial,” he said.

He explained that the deployment of U.S. personnel was tied to specific operational and counter-terrorism objectives, making the drawdown part of the evolving nature of the engagement.

According to him, intelligence cooperation, training, information sharing and other areas of professional military cooperation will continue despite the adjustment in U.S. troop presence.

“The responsibility for the defence of Nigeria and the protection of its citizens rests primarily with Nigerian security forces,” Uba said.

He said the partnership with the United States was designed to strengthen Nigeria’s capabilities through intelligence sharing, training and technical assistance.

Uba added that where both countries jointly assessed the need for additional efforts, including joint strikes, such operations would be undertaken.

He said the partnership had continued to produce favourable outcomes against terrorism and other transnational security threats.

The Defence spokesman urged the media and Nigerians not to interpret routine adjustments in foreign military deployments as evidence of a collapse in bilateral security cooperation or Nigeria’s defence capability.

On kinetic and non-kinetic operations, Uba said the military’s primary responsibility remained kinetic operations against terrorists and other armed groups threatening Nigerians.

“Our major job is kinetic operations. As much as possible, we want to take down all the terrorists in Nigeria, or anybody who takes up arms against citizens,” he said.

He, however, said the military would continue supporting non-kinetic interventions under the whole-of-society and whole-of-nation approach to tackling insecurity.

Uba stressed that such support would not compromise the military’s position against dialogue with terrorists or the payment of ransom.

He further clarified that some non-kinetic initiatives were state-led, with the military providing support where required.

He said the distinction was important because the police remained the lead agency for internal security, while the military provided support to the Nigeria Police Force.

He said the Armed Forces remained focused on defeating armed criminal elements while contributing to broader national efforts aimed at addressing the root causes of insecurity. (NAN)

World.title: Olowo Seeks Still Earth Group’s Support for Igogo Festival
World.content:
The Olowo of Owo Kingdom, His Imperial Majesty, Oba Ajibade Gbadegesin Ogunoye III, has sought the support of the Executive Chairman of Still Earth Group, Ms Oyindamola Lami Adeyemi, towards the successful hosting and promotion of the annual Igogo festival.

The monarch requested during a courtesy visit to Adeyemi at her Banana Island residence in Lagos last weekend, as preparations intensify for the centuries-old festival.

Also present during the monarch’s visit was Chief Taiwo Kabir Adeyemi, the father of the host, Ms Adeyemi.

The visit, initiated by the Owo Palace, was aimed at strengthening collaboration with prominent indigenes and other stakeholders towards preserving the cultural significance of the festival while broadening its appeal and visibility.

Adeyemi, a native of Owo, is expected to play a significant role in supporting the festival, which remains one of the most important cultural events in Owo Kingdom and Ondo State.

Speaking during the visit, Oba Ogunoye traced the history of the Igogo festival, explaining that the celebration is rooted in values, including fidelity, forgiveness and the rejection of betrayal.

According to the monarch, one of the festival’s most distinctive traditions is the suspension of conventional drumming during the celebration, with the gong assuming particular significance.

“It was originally a day set aside to do away with the beating of drums, except the gong, and that’s where the festival got its name, ‘Igogo’,” he said.

The Olowo described Adeyemi as a worthy daughter of Owo whose contribution would be valuable to efforts to strengthen the festival and project the cultural heritage of the kingdom to a wider audience.

Responding, Adeyemi expressed appreciation to the monarch and the palace for considering her worthy of the responsibility, saying she was proud of her Owo heritage and delighted to contribute to the preservation and promotion of its traditions.

She pledged the support of Still Earth Group for the festival and indicated that the commitment would extend beyond the current edition.

“At least, for the next three years, we will be on board,” Adeyemi said.

She added that the partnership would seek to enhance the organisation and profile of the festival while respecting the customs and traditions that have sustained it through generations.

The Igogo Festival is one of Owo Kingdom’s most enduring cultural celebrations and attracts indigenes, visitors and culture enthusiasts to the ancient town annually.

World.title: Omoyibo, Rallies Isoko APC for Oborevwori, Joel-Onowakpo
World.content:
Sylvester Idowu in Warri

A prominent Isoko industrialist and philanthropist, Chief Daniel Omoyibo, popularly known as ‘Danmotech’, has rallied the people of Isoko to close ranks and support the All Progressives Congress (APC), the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, and the Senator representing Delta South, Joel-Onowakpo Thomas, ahead of the 2027 elections.

Omoyibo made the call in Oleh last weekend when Senator Joel-Onowakpo paid him a courtesy visit as part of consultations on the unity, political future, and development of Isoko Nation.

He urged his kinsmen, women, and Isoko people at home and in the diaspora to avoid political division and rally behind leaders who, he said, were positioned to attract meaningful development to the area.

“Let us not go into opposition. Let us queue behind the governor and our own son, Senator Joel-Onowakpo Thomas, to consolidate on the good work he has started. That is how Isoko will develop,” Omoyibo said.

He stressed that unity remained the greatest political strength of the Isoko people, and urged political leaders, traditional stakeholders, professionals and youths to work together in advancing the collective interests of the area.

Omoyibo also commended Senator Joel-Onowakpo for his role in the establishment of the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) in Oleh, describing the project as a landmark achievement that would leave a lasting impact on the people of Isoko and the wider Delta South senatorial district.

The senator, he recalled, sponsored the Federal Medical Centre Act (Amendment) Bill 2023 (SB. 197), seeking the establishment of the institution in Oleh. The bill was introduced in the Senate on November 7, 2023, passed second reading on October 22, 2024, and subsequently passed by the National Assembly before it was signed into law by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“The new FMC, which will be the first federal tertiary healthcare institution in Delta South, is expected to expand access to specialised medical services while creating employment opportunities and stimulating economic activities in the region,” he said.

Omoyibo, who has been involved in community development and youth empowerment initiatives across Isoko, said the medical centre would provide affordable healthcare and open new opportunities for medical professionals, youths, and businesses.

Senator Thomas thanked Omoyibo for his philanthropy and sustained commitment to the development of Isoko Nation, assuring the people that he would continue to pursue strategic federal projects, interventions, and legislation capable of transforming the socio-economic fortunes of Isoko.

The meeting ended with a renewed call for political unity and collective action, with Omoyibo and the senator urging the people of Isoko to remain united in their quest for greater development and representation.

World.title: Foundation Supports 3,000 Indigent Residents of Kwara With Medical Outreach
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

A non-governmental organisation in Kwara State,.Arike Hopeful Heart Foundation, has supported over 3,000 indigent residents of the state with various kinds of medical outreach as part of effort to reduce untimely death of the people in the state.

The foundation was formed and launched on Monday by Hajia Zainab Kale Kawu, wife of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate for 2027 election in the state, Mr. Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu.

Speaking in Ilorin on Monday during the launch of the foundation, Hajia Kawu said that the foundation was formed to bring healthcare delivery to the doorsteps of Kwarans without any conditions.

The launch of the foundation coincided with Hajia Zainab Kawu’s birthday celebration.

She said the gesture would go a long way in assisting vulnerable women, children and families who want access to basic healthcare in the state.

The founder said the initiative was also driven by her desire to give back to society by addressing challenges confronting vulnerable members of the community, particularly in accessing healthcare and obtaining timely health information.

“I believe life is measured not only by what we achieve, but by the lives we touch, the burdens we ease and the hope we give,” she said.

Kawu said the foundation would focus on basic healthcare, health awareness, prevention and early detection, with particular attention to conditions such as diabetes and hypertension, which she described as silent health challenges capable of becoming life-threatening when left undetected.

“Our mission is to provide compassionate and practical support, particularly for women and children, while promoting health awareness, prevention and early detection,” she said.

She added that the foundation would also pay attention to post-menopausal health and other healthcare needs, stressing that its intervention would not be limited to material assistance.

“For me, this foundation is about more than assistance. It is about restoring dignity, creating awareness, bringing healthcare closer to people and, most importantly, giving hope,” she said.

According to her, the name Arike Hopeful Hearts reflects the vision of encouraging people to care for one another and respond to the needs of those experiencing hardship.

She noted that seemingly simple interventions, including medical screening, providing health information, caring for a child or supporting a woman, could have a lasting impact on beneficiaries.

“Sometimes, changing a life begins with simply reminding someone that their life matters,” she said.

The founder called on healthcare professionals, development partners, philanthropists, organisations, community leaders and individuals to support the foundation as it begins its humanitarian activities.

She also appreciated her husband and family members for their encouragement and support, promising that the foundation would operate with integrity and remain responsive to the needs of its beneficiaries.

“As we begin this journey, I make this promise: We will listen, we will serve, we will act with integrity and we will continue to give hope,” she added.

Also speaking, Hajia Kawu’s husband, Bolakale Kawu, pledged his support for his wife’s humanitarian initiative, describing her as a woman passionate about improving the lives of people in need.

The PDP governorship candidate said he was confident that the foundation would make meaningful contributions to the wellbeing of vulnerable women, children and other members of the society.

He stressed the importance of supporting initiatives designed to address the challenges confronting ordinary people, assuring his wife of his continued encouragement.

“I am 100 per cent dependent on somebody that thinks she is a fine woman, but we decided to go through this situation with support and support,” Kawu said.

He urged supporters and well-meaning members of the public to encourage the foundation and contribute to its success.

The launch marked the beginning of what the founder described as a long-term commitment to promoting healthier communities and restoring hope and dignity to vulnerable people in Kwara State.

World.title: URC 2026/27: South Africa’s ‘Big 4’ rebuild for new season
World.content:
Siya Kolisi rejoins the Stormers ahead of the URC 2026/26 campaign. Image: www.inpho.ie (Wikimedia Commons), GovernmentZA (Flickr).

Could South Africa shift the balance of power in the new United Rugby Championship (URC) season?

The Stormers, Bulls, Lions and Sharks are rebuilding their rosters with three weeks to go to the new campaign.

Cape Town is at the epicentre, where the Stormers are creating what could be the league’s strongest team.



Kolisi, Kolbe join Western Cape super squad

The Stormers have already set themselves up as the team to watch in the new URC campaign.

No signing demonstrates this more than bringing national icon Siya Kolisi back to Cape Town after his time with the Sharks ended.

Alongside the legendary Springboks forward, speedster Cheslin Kolbe will also return from Japan.



The third big name on the list is monster prop Wilco Louw, who has switched allegiance from the Bulls.

Stormers coach John Dobson has made a point of downplaying talk of signing “marquee players.”

Instead, as reported by SuperSport, he has referenced Kolisi and Kolbe as returning home to help the team win trophies.



The additions to the Stormers’ ranks have been balanced against the loss of Dan du Plessis, Salmaan Moerat and Dylan Maart.

Sharks rebuilding team and squad identity

The departure of Siya Kolisi was a major blow for the Sharks, but the team has not sat back.

Instead, the Durban franchise has brought the mighty Thomas du Toit back from Bath to anchor the front row, while scrumhalf Ivan van Zyl has made a move from Saracens.



He has been brought in to replace Grant Williams, who left the Sharks for Japan’s Kobe Steelers.

Van Zyl will be joined at Hollywoodbets Kings Park by Gianni Lombard and Stephan Lewies.

Meanwhile, top-rated backline player Aphelele Fassi was granted a season-long sabbatical in Japan.



The signings come at an interesting time for the Sharks and head coach JP Pietersen.

With the club having recently rebranded, the team still needs to find a balance between new and existing stars.

Bulls trying to balance incoming and outgoing stars

Rebuilding for the new URC season has come with ups and downs for the Bulls.



On one hand, a set of new names is due to bolster the Pretoria side’s ranks.

These include Thaakir Abrahams, who joins the Bulls from Munster, and Dylan Maart, joining from the Stormers.

The team will also gain the experience of Hanro Liebenberg and Curwin Bosch.



However, the Bulls are also still dealing with the departures of several veteran players.

This includes Wilco Louw, who will turn out in the Stormers’ colours this season. Kurt-Lee Arendse is also gone, having signed for the Sagamihara Dynaboars in Japan.

Centre David Kriel, who is heading to La Rochelle in France, marks the third first-choice loss for the Bulls.



It remains to be seen how the team will stack up heading into the new URC season.

Lions prioritise URC consistency over signings

Compared to their local rivals, the Lions appear to be investing in a stronger core squad over big-name signings.

However, this does not mean the Johannesburg team have not made some major moves.



The club confirmed that prop Boan Venter is set to lace up for them after departing Edinburgh.

He will join Boeta Chamberlain, Asad Moos, and Daniel Kasende in the red and white.



Balancing these signings, the Lions have lost Gianni Lombard and Darrien Landsberg to the Sharks.

Despite this, the team seems to be prioritising player development over breaking the bank for marquee stars.

Whether this strategy will serve the Lions in the long run is the biggest question for now.

World.title: Why you should stop what you’re doing and fill up your vehicle NOW
World.content:
South Africa’s motorists have just hours left to fill up at cheaper prices before a major fuel price increase kicks in at midnight. Image: Engen

South Africa’s motorists have just hours left to fill up at cheaper prices before a major fuel price increase kicks in at midnight.

From Wednesday, 2 September, both grades of petrol will become R1.34 per litre more expensive, while diesel prices will jump by around R3 per litre.

The latest increases have been confirmed by the Central Energy Fund (CEF) and the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources.



For motorists who need to refuel, filling up before midnight on Tuesday, 1 September could mean avoiding the full impact of Wednesday’s increases.

Fuel Increase Petrol 93 R1.34/litre Petrol 95 R1.34/litre Diesel 0.05% R2.93/litre Diesel 0.005% R3.15/litre Illuminating paraffin R2.13/litre

How much can you save?

The difference becomes significant when filling a larger tank.

For example, putting 50 litres of petrol into a vehicle before the increase takes effect will save approximately R67 compared with filling the same tank after midnight.

For diesel motorists, the saving is even greater.

A 50-litre fill of 0.005% sulphur diesel before the increase would save approximately R157.50 compared with the new price.

For a 60-litre tank, the difference rises to about R80.40 for petrol and R188.40 for 0.005% sulphur diesel.



Why are fuel prices increasing?

The latest adjustment follows a sharp increase in international petroleum product prices during the CEF’s review period.

International prices for petrol, diesel and illuminating paraffin rose substantially between 31 July and 27 August.

The stronger rand provided some relief, with the average exchange rate improving from R16.4554 to R16.2139 to the US dollar.

However, the currency gains were not enough to offset the surge in international fuel prices.

Slate levy adds to the pain

Another major factor behind the increase is the slate levy.

The combined cumulative petrol and diesel slate balance stood at a negative R9.519 billion at the end of July.

As a result, the slate levy increases from 61.38 cents to 83.28 cents per litre from Wednesday.

That represents an additional 21.90 cents per litre on both petrol and diesel.

The slate mechanism is used to account for accumulated under-recoveries when the revenue collected through fuel prices does not cover the costs reflected in the Basic Fuel Price.

Petrol margin also rises

Petrol motorists will also face a 4.9-cent-per-litre increase in the retail margin.

The Department said this adjustment accommodates wage increases for service-station employees, including pump attendants, cashiers and administrative staff.

Once all the various components are taken into account, both petrol grades increase by R1.34 per litre.

Diesel motorists face the biggest hit

Diesel users are facing the largest increases.

The price of 0.05% sulphur diesel rises by R2.939 per litre, while 0.005% sulphur diesel increases by R3.149 per litre.

The latter will push the wholesale price of 0.005% sulphur diesel above R30 per litre in Gauteng.

The increase will not only affect diesel vehicle owners but could also have wider consequences for businesses and industries that depend heavily on diesel-powered transport, machinery and equipment.

More increases for paraffin and LPGas

The price pain extends beyond petrol and diesel.

The wholesale price of illuminating paraffin rises by R2.13 per litre, while its Single Maximum National Retail Price increases by R2.84 per litre.

The maximum retail price of LPGas also rises by 69 cents per kilogram.

All of the new prices take effect from Wednesday, 2 September, and will remain in place until the next monthly adjustment.

FUEL PRICE IN SOUTH AFRICA IMPACTED BY TWO MAIN FACTORS:

1. The international price of petroleum products, driven mainly by oil prices.

2. The rand/dollar exchange rate used in the purchase of these products.

Oil price

At the time of publishing the brent crude oil price is $92.59 a barrel.

Exchange rate

At the time of publishing the rand/dollar exchange rate is R16.09/$.

World.title: Woolworths pulls popular product from shelves in South Africa
World.content:
Woolworths has recalled a WBeauty shampoo from stores across South Africa after testing detected a potentially harmful bacterium. Image: V&A Waterfront website

Woolworths has recalled a WBeauty shampoo from stores across South Africa after testing detected a potentially harmful bacterium in a limited batch of the product.

The retailer announced the recall of WBeauty Complete Clarifying Shampoo 250ml with immediate effect as part of its quality assurance processes.

READ | Woolworths opens new ‘dark store’ to boost Woolies Dash offering



The affected product has been removed from shelves, and customers who purchased it are being asked to return it to their nearest Woolworths store for a full refund.

Importantly, proof of purchase is not required.

What caused the recall?

Woolworths said an issue was identified with a batch of the shampoo during its quality assurance processes, prompting additional testing.



Those tests detected the presence of Pluralibacter gergoviae, a bacterium that can occur naturally in environments including water, soil and plants and has also been associated with contamination of personal-care products.

The bacterium is considered an opportunistic pathogen, meaning it generally poses a greater risk to vulnerable people than to healthy individuals.

READ | New Woolworths CEO announces major leadership shake-up



Woolworths said the risk to healthy individuals is considered low.

However, customers with weakened immune systems have been advised to stop using the shampoo to avoid the possibility of bacterial infection.

People with open wounds or broken skin, or those with invasive medical lines, may also be more vulnerable to opportunistic infections.



In some cases, Pluralibacter gergoviae can cause skin and soft-tissue infections, bloodstream infections, respiratory infections and urinary tract infections.

There is no indication from Woolworths that customers should be alarmed if they are otherwise healthy, but anyone with the recalled product should follow the retailer’s advice and discontinue use.

Which product is affected?

The recall applies to the WBeauty Complete Clarifying Shampoo, sold in a single 250ml variant.



The product is marketed as a deep-cleansing, clarifying shampoo designed to remove product build-up and excess oil.

Its ingredients include witch hazel, apple cider vinegar, activated charcoal and rose geranium oil.

The shampoo forms part of Woolworths’ WBeauty haircare range, which is manufactured in accordance with the retailer’s Good Beauty Principles.



These principles cover formulation, ingredient sourcing, testing and manufacturing practices.

Woolworths said its beauty formulas are assessed by qualified independent toxicologists and accredited laboratories, while products are also dermatologically tested for sensitive skin.

The range is formulated without sulphates, parabens and mineral oil and includes locally sourced ingredients, African botanicals and cosmetic ingredients such as hyaluronic acid and peptides.



Woolworths added that its manufacturing practices adhere to vegan-friendly processing standards and are certified by Beauty Without Cruelty.

What should customers do?

Customers who have the affected WBeauty Complete Clarifying Shampoo should stop using it and return it to any Woolworths store.

A full refund will be provided, and customers do not need a receipt or other proof of purchase.



“We pride ourselves on exceptionally high standards, and we go to great lengths to ensure every item we produce is the quality our customers expect,” Woolworths said.

“Product safety is critically important to us, and the well-being of our customers is our first priority.”

World.title: IEC rules out extension for local election candidate nominations
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) says it has not allowed, nor does it intend to allow, any political party or independent candidate an additional opportunity to capture candidate nominations after the close of the nomination period.

This follows reports that the African National Congress (ANC) experienced technical difficulties while submitting some of its candidate nominations for municipalities in its stronghold, the Eastern Cape.

The IEC had urged all political parties and independent candidates to submit their candidate nominations by 17:00 on Friday, 28 August 2026.



ANC SAYS OUTSTANDING ENTRIES BEING FINALISED

On Monday, the ANC said it had successfully lodged the overwhelming majority of its candidates within the IEC deadline.

However, the party said the IEC’s candidate-capture system experienced technical issues on the day of the submission, affecting a number of contesting parties.

“As a result, a small number of the movement’s entries are being finalised together with the Commission. This is a technical and administrative matter, and it is being handled through the Commission’s established processes.

“The ANC has full confidence in the Electoral Commission and in the integrity of the electoral process. We commend the Commission for its constructive engagement with all affected parties, and we are working with it to bring these outstanding matters to a close. We are confident they will be resolved,” ANC spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu said.

IEC RESPONDS TO ANC CLAIMS

In response, the IEC said it had noted the ANC’s statement regarding the submission of its nominated candidates.

The Commission clarified that it had not allowed any political party or independent candidate an additional opportunity to capture nominations beyond the close of candidate nomination on Friday, 28 August 2026 at 17:00.



“All matters pertaining to the intricacies of the candidate nomination process would be discussed in the National Political Liaison Committee constituted by all parties that are represented in the National Assembly,” the IEC said.

The Commission also clarified that its Online Candidate Nomination System remained available to users throughout the nomination period, including on the cut-off date.

While the official candidate nomination period began on Proclamation Day on 7 August 2026, the IEC said it had opened the system earlier, on 21 June 2026, to provide contestants with sufficient time to use the system ahead of the deadline.

The IEC said it would provide a comprehensive briefing on the outcome of the candidate nomination process and the next milestones in the 2026 Local Government Elections on Wednesday, 2 September.

World.title: WATCH | Baby Alert: Chef Onezwa Mbola debuts her growing baby bump
World.content:
Chef extraordinaire and author Onezwa Mbola is one happy and glowing mama-to-be.

Mbola made her pregnancy announcement on social media on Tuesday, first showing us her Spring Day garden blooms and then her bourgeoning baby bump was introduced.

“It is the first of September, the day we all decided to recognise a spring day in the Southern Hemisphere. So here’s everything that I am growing this spring. Lots of beautiful kale in my garden. Gorgeous leeks that made it through the winter. Lots of big, beautiful sweet beetroot. Strawberries are also looking really, really good. I always, always have tomatoes. Carrots, Gorgeous red onion. All those big leafies was charred. I’m still growing some cabbages. I’m also growing a baby,” said the happy Mbola.



We have seen Mbola’s seven-year-old, an adorable boy who sometimes makes a cameo in his mother’s videos.

By all indication – thanks to the pink baby shoes in the video, the new addition to the family is a little girl.



Onezwa Mbola, The Author

Best known for her mouth-watering home grown, organic produce and truely ‘from scratch’ recipes, Mbola recently launched her first recipe book, A Food Love Story, that put all her best dishes in one place for her fans to try.

This comes after years of perfecting her dishes in her kitchen and sharing with the audience that she’s grown over time.

World.title: How much does it cost to: Visit the Two Oceans Aquarium?
World.content:
Planning a day at Cape Town's Two Oceans Aquarium? Here's how much you'll pay for adult, children, students and pensioners tickets. Image: Two Oceans Aquarium website

Planning a family day out at Cape Town’s Two Oceans Aquarium? Visitors can expect to pay R280 for a standard adult ticket, while children, students and pensioners qualify for cheaper rates.

Situated at the V&A Waterfront, the Two Oceans Aquarium showcases marine life from South Africa’s Atlantic and Indian Ocean coastlines and is open 365 days of the year.

Two Oceans Aquarium ticket prices

The current standard admission prices are:



Adults: R280

R280 Children aged 14 to 17: R210

R210 Children aged 4 to 13: R130

R130 Children under four: Free

Free South African students: R210

R210 South African pensioners: R210

Children under 14 must be accompanied by an adult. Students and pensioners need to provide valid identification to qualify for the discounted rate.

Save with the After 3 Special

Visitors looking for a cheaper afternoon outing can take advantage of the Aquarium’s After 3 Special during South African school terms.

Tickets purchased at the on-site ticket office after 15:00 cost:



Adults: R210

R210 Children aged 14 to 17: R158

R158 Children aged 4 to 13: R97

R97 Children under four: Free

The discounted tickets are valid from 15:00 until closing on the day of purchase and cannot be bought online or in advance.

The aquarium is open daily from 09:30 to 18:00.

In addition, the Two Oceans Aquarium’s special birthday offer has been extended to your entire birthday month.



South Africans can now enjoy complimentary admission to the Two Oceans Aquarium on any (one) day throughout their birthday month.

Aquarium membership prices

For visitors who plan to return regularly, an annual membership could offer better value.

Membership provides a year of unlimited access to the Two Oceans Aquarium, as well as additional benefits including exclusive events and bespoke discounts. Memberships are non-refundable.



The current membership prices are:

Membership Price Adult R670 Child aged 14 to 17 R520 Child aged 4 to 13 R330 Child under 4 Free South African student R520 South African pensioner (65+) R520 Au pair R520

South African students must present a valid student card when activating their membership.

Pensioners must be 65 or older, and the aquarium may request identification when the membership is activated.



Au pairs must provide proof of employment when activating their membership, including their employer’s contact details.

For regular visitors, the membership can quickly pay for itself. An adult membership costs R670, meaning it is equivalent to fewer than three standard adult visits.

The Two Oceans Aquarium remains a popular Cape Town attraction, with visitors able to see penguins, sharks, turtles, jellyfish and the iconic kelp forest, among other marine life.

World.title: Meet the Georgian referee to take charge of Springboks-All Blacks clash at FNB Stadium
World.content:
Nika Amashukeli will take charge of the third Test between South Africa and New Zealand at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg on Saturday. Image: World Rugby website

Nika Amashukeli has been handed one of the biggest assignments in his refereeing career after being confirmed as the referee for the third Test between South Africa and New Zealand at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg on Saturday, 5 September.

Kick-off is at 17:10.

RIP | Springbok great dies in church after watching South Africa beat All Blacks



The Georgian official, who will turn 32 later this month, was originally scheduled to referee the second Test in Cape Town on 29 August, but illness ruled him out.

Australian referee Angus Gardner stepped in for that match, which the Springboks won 33-26 to level the four-Test series at 1-1.

World Rugby subsequently confirmed that Amashukeli would take charge of the crucial third Test instead.



Who is Nika Amashukeli?

Born in Tbilisi, Georgia, in 1994, Amashukeli initially played football before taking up rugby at the age of 11 with Georgian club Jiki.

He played primarily at flanker and centre, representing Georgia at age-group level, but a succession of injuries forced him to end his playing career.

He had suffered several concussions, as well as ankle and knee injuries, by his early 20s.



Rather than leaving rugby behind, Amashukeli turned to refereeing.

His rise through the ranks was rapid, eventually taking him onto the international stage.

READ | Airlink Cape Town Stadium flyover now under official review



A history-making referee

Amashukeli made history in 2022 when he became the first referee from outside the traditional Six Nations nations to referee a Six Nations match, taking charge of Ireland against Italy.

He subsequently refereed at the 2023 Rugby World Cup and has built a growing portfolio of elite appointments across international rugby, the Champions Cup, Top 14 and United Rugby Championship.

READ | Cheslin Kolbe boots his way up Springbok points scorers list



A huge assignment in Johannesburg

Now, Amashukeli returns to the centre of the action for a potentially decisive Test.

With the series level at 1-1, the Springboks and All Blacks head to Johannesburg knowing that victory will put them one step closer to claiming the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

Amashukeli will have Angus Gardner and England’s Christophe Ridley as his assistant referees, with France’s Eric Gauzins serving as TMO.



For the 31-year-old Georgian, it represents another major milestone in a remarkable rise from rugby player to one of the game’s most prominent international referees.

DID YOU KNOW | Here’s who’s next in line for Springbok Test centurion

Record refereeing the Springboks

To date, Amashukeli has refereed the Springboks on four occasions.



South Africa have won three of those matches – and perhaps crucially – the only match against the All Blacks.

The Springboks also boast wins over Wales and Argentina when Amashukeli had the whistle, with their only defeat to date coming against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin in November 2022.
