World.title: Impeachment Committee drops Madonsela as evidence leader
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Section 89 Impeachment Committee has rescinded its nomination of Advocate Thandazani Madonsela as evidence leader.

The decision follows President Cyril Ramaphosa’s objection to the appointment, citing potential conflicts of interest.

The committee had been seeking legal advice on the objection and will now have to decide how to proceed with appointing an evidence leader.

World.title: Illegal mining ravages SA's economic hub
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Whole chunks of a once-busy road in Johannesburg have collapsed because of damage caused by the illegal mining rampant across South Africa's economic hub.

Elsewhere along Wemmer Pan Road are cracks and sinkholes from underground blasting by irregular miners digging under the city for gold and other minerals.

The round-the-clock operations are undermining Johannesburg's infrastructure -- from transport and power networks to homes and buildings -- and introducing crime linked to competition between gangs, residents and officials say.

"At first it was the blasting and the tremors from underground, and we would feel our flat shake," 45-year-old Voneen Trompeter told AFP in Roodepoort.

"Now there are shootouts in the area. It is scary."

Illegal mining in South Africa pulls in thousands of impoverished men from countries around the region who can spend days underground at a time.

Known locally as zama zamas, which means "those who try" in Zulu, they are mostly heavily armed and descend deep into shafts abandoned by mining companies, or dig out new ones.

They steal electricity cables, damage water pipes and dig up roads, said Michael Sun, a member of the provincial legislature in Gauteng, which includes Johannesburg.

"Who gets to suffer? The residents get to suffer," he said.

City of Gold

A businessman in Denver, near central Johannesburg, showed AFP a gaping hole around 100 metres from the entrance of his factory from where he said a large number of illegal miners emerged each week.

"We are worried about what is happening beneath our buildings," the 63-year-old said, asking to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation.

He pointed out cracks in the premises that he said were caused by underground blasting.

The city's electricity network said its infrastructure is being wrecked.

"Underground excavations have compromised ground stability, placing substations, transformers, pylons and transmission towers at risk," City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena said.

"In some areas, infrastructure has already begun to sink as illegal mining activity continues to expand beneath the surface," he said.

President Cyril Ramaphosa deployed troops across Gauteng province in March to bolster police operations against crime and illegal mining.

Johannesburg -- reported to be the richest city in Africa -- was born from a gold rush in the 1880s. While regular mining continues in parts, there are also hundreds of abandoned shafts along the main gold reef.

While some are being reworked by zama zamas, many are filled with acidic water that contributes to sinkholes, said mining expert David van Wyk.

"Things are still going to get worse in terms of infrastructure damage," said van Wyk, who estimates that there are more than 34,000 irregular miners in South Africa.

People living in informal settlements built on mine waste dumps are falling ill and more "houses will crack and fall into sinkholes", he said.

'They rule'

In a mining village outside Carletonville, zama zamas have taken over an abandoned school, barring anyone else from coming near.

Outside, men sat in groups, some draped in blankets, while others carrying shovels and wearing mining boots appeared to be returning from nearby shafts. They said they were from Lesotho and Mozambique.

One told AFP he could earn up to R15,000 on a good day and more than R100,000 a month.

"I have been here for four years, and this job feeds my family," said the 27-year-old father of three from Lesotho.

The area had become "chaotic" since the miners took over, said local councillor Moiketsi Ntilane, 44.

"They are the authority," he said. "Families live in fear. They are ruthless, gun-toting and happy to kill."

Outside of Gauteng, in the North West province, the damage and fear brought by illegal mining was stark in the village of Bapong, about 65 kilometres northeast of Johannesburg.

Several homes stood dangerously close to the edge of massive pits dug with excavators by miners seeking access to chrome deposits.

While regular police and military patrols now keep the zama zamas at bay, the community lives with the damage, said 63-year-old resident Sarah Rakgwanhla.

"The holes are dangerous because they have water, and our children pass by them every day on their way to school and to the shops," she said.

"We need help to have these holes sealed."

World.title: Messi legacy will 'live forever', says Beckham
World.content:
MIAMI - David Beckham said Lionel Messi's "legacy will live forever" after the Argentina legend announced his retirement from international football.

Messi on Monday revealed he had called time on his remarkable career with Argentina after 207 caps and 125 goals.

The 39-year-old won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and his last game for his country was Argentina's World Cup final defeat against Spain in July.

Messi's brilliance for Argentina and Barcelona made him one of the world's greatest ever players.

Former England captain Beckham has had a close-up view of Messi's career as an opponent and now as co-owner of the forward's current side Inter Miami.

"This is the moment we get to look back on and realise how grateful we were to witness the greatness of a young kid with a dream," Beckham wrote on Instagram on Tuesday.

"Leo, you have been a credit to yourself, your family, your friends and your country. Leading by example and creating inspiration for millions of children not just in Argentina but around the whole world.

"Leo, you delivered the greatest gift to your country and, for that, your legacy will live forever. Congratulations on all you achieved for Argentina."

World.title: Hawks target more suspects in Tembisa Hospital corruption probe
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - More suspects are being sought in the Tembisa Hospital theft case, says the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, also known as the Hawks.

Spokesperson Katlego Mogale says several investigations are running in parallel, tracing the money to identify the beneficiaries of the systematic looting of R2-billion.

The money was meant for the healthcare facility in Ekurhuleni. Gauteng Department of Health Chief Director of Financial Accounting Babita Deokaran blew the whistle when she discovered the looting under her watch in 2021.

Her murder outside her Johannesburg home blew the lid wide open, exposing the extent of the rot. Businessmen Hangwani Maumela and Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matlala are among those who have been linked to the theft.

World.title: Tsitsipas says Kyrgios's positive cocaine test 'kind of expected'
World.content:
NEW YORK - Stefanos Tsitsipas said that he was not surprised that his old rival Nick Kyrgios tested positive for cocaine and was suspended.

"I kind of expected it, to be honest," the world number 53 from Greece said at the US Open after defeating French 10th seed Arthur Fils in four sets in the opening round.

The former Wimbledon finalist Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended and last month admitted to making "a huge mistake" after failing a test for cocaine.

The 31-year-old Australian, who has hardly played singles tennis in recent years, apologised and said injuries had taken "a huge toll on me both physically and mentally".

After defeating Fils 4-6, 7-6 (7/3), 6-1, 6-4 in New York, Tsitsipas -- who briefly played doubles with Kyrgios but has had a turbulent relationship with him -- was asked about the positive drugs test.

"I'm not going to try and cover up someone that I know the truth for," the 28-year-old replied.

"I'll consider myself a nice person with everyone, but these were behaviours that I personally heard on the tour and heard other people in that same environment saying those sort of things to me.

"Again, when I saw it, I was, like: Well, pretty much expected, to be honest. I am surprised it came so late, though."

Boasting a big serve and booming groundstrokes, Kyrgios has won seven singles titles on the ATP Tour and rose to a high of 13 in the world in 2016.

His finest performance was on the grass at Wimbledon in 2022, when he reached the championship match, losing in four sets to Novak Djokovic.

Despite his natural talents that is as good as it got, with a series of injuries taking their toll.

In January he admitted he would never be the player that he once was.

World.title: Anthropic signs $35B computing deal with startup backed by Nvidia
World.content:
NEW YORK - Anthropic signed a $35 billion deal for access to cloud computing power from a US-based startup backed by Nvidia, adding to a string of such deals clinched by the artificial intelligence (AI) developer amid fierce competition for advanced computing power.

The San Francisco-based AI lab has agreed to a six-year deal with Lambda, a source familiar with the deal told AFP.

Based in San Jose, California, Lambda provides access to AI cloud computing services.

Lambda will secure access to a data centre being built by another company, Hut 8, which mines bitcoins and builds data centres, including one in Texas that Anthropic will tap for computing power, according to media reports.

Nvidia, which has invested in both Anthropic and Lambda, will lease the data centre from Hut 8, and Lambda will then pay Nvidia an unknown amount to get access to the data centre, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

Anthropic also recently signed a similar six-year-long deal worth $45 billion with Nscale, a cloud provider based in London, which will give Anthropic capacity at a facility in West Virginia, a source confirmed to AFP.

Just this year, Anthropic has signed various computing deals worth at least $135 billion.

The company is in a race with AI lab OpenAI to win customers and grow revenue; the rivals are both barreling toward initial public offerings as well.

Demand for chips and advanced computing power has skyrocketed over the past couple of years as leading AI model developers compete with each other for customers and capacity.

Meanwhile, that demand is also crunching global supply chains for chips across sectors, including consumer electronics.

Apple has already increased prices for certain devices, such as Macs and iPads, due to memory and chip costs; the company is expected to increase prices for the newest generation of iPhones which it will unveil at an event in September.

World.title: Drones in Ithaca: Azov's Odyssey turns Ukraine war into modern myth
World.content:
KYIV - In a theatrical adaptation of the Odyssey by Ukraine's Azov military corps, Penelope beats a suitor to death with plastic grocery bags.

An attack drone flies over the stage to chase a soldier, while Odysseus shouts for battlefield updates over a radio.

Men sleep in khaki sleeping bags.

"We are not doing Homer, that's very important. Our Odyssey is about our heroes, though we draw on archaic, mythical, and profoundly significant themes," says Darya Legeyda, who plays Penelope.

The longing for home at the heart of Homer's Odyssey resonates in Ukraine, where Russia's invasion has displaced millions and sent hundreds of thousands to fight, with tens of thousands still missing or held captive.

While the epic has found audiences worldwide with Christopher Nolan's blockbuster, Kyiv has staged its adaptation: a collaboration between the Ivan Franko Theatre and the Azov military corps.

Written and performed by Azov service members, the play is part of the unit's cultural outreach, and ticket funds go to an organisation supporting prisoners of war.

World.title: Naomi Watts to receive lifetime award at top Spain film fest
World.content:
MADRID - Hollywood star actor and producer Naomi Watts will receive a lifetime achievement award at Spain's top film festival next month, organisers announced on Monday.

The San Sebastian Film Festival said the British-born Australian, a two-time Oscar nominee, would take the "Donostia" prize as "one of the most talented and recognised actresses of her generation".

Watts, 57, first made a name for herself in David Lynch's 2001 movie "Mulholland Drive" and has played versatile roles in both auteur cinema and big productions.

She earned Oscar nominations for her performances in "21 Grams" (2003) by Mexican director Alejandro Gonzalez Inarritu and "The Impossible" (2012) under Spain's Juan Antonio Bayona.

Inarritu's "Birdman" (2014), "You Will Meet a Tall Dark Stranger" (2010) by Woody Allen and Michael Haneke's "Funny Games" (1997) feature among her other standout roles.

Watts was nominated for an Emmy Award for her work in Ryan Murphy's mini-series "Feud: Capote vs. The Swans", where she was also an executive producer.

Watts has also stood out in recent times for raising awareness about women's health and menopause.

The prize ceremony will take place on September 19 in the northern coastal city of San Sebastian, where the Spanish-speaking world's most prestigious film festival will run from September 18-26.

A showing of the new film "The Housewife" will follow, where Watts stars as the enigmatic wife of a suspected former Nazi official living in 1960s New York.

German director, scriptwriter, producer and actor Werner Herzog is also due to take home a Donostia award this year.

The illustrious list of previous winners includes Gregory Peck, Bette Davis, Lauren Bacall, Francis Ford Coppola, Woody Allen, Oliver Stone, Agnes Varda, Catherine Deneuve and Pedro Almodovar.

World.title: Japan is using AI, drones and wolf robots to keep bears at bay
World.content:
Bear attacks in Japan have hit a record high, with 13 deaths and more than 220 injuries recorded between April 2025 and March 2026. It is a sharp increase from the same period the previous year, when three people died and 82 were hurt, and as fall approaches, the bears’ peak feeding season, authorities are on high alert.

The rise in human-bear encounters in Japan can be traced back to shrinking rural communities following the World War II when millions of young people began moving to cities. “With the loss of farmland that once buffered settlements from bears, the boundary between towns and forests became more blurred for them,” explained Liam Adcock, a wildlife researcher at the Nagano-based Picchio Wildlife Research Center.

He added that tighter hunting restrictions and a shrinking hunter population have allowed Japan’s two native bear species — the Hokkaido brown bear and the Asiatic black bear — to grow. It is estimated that there are more than 57,000 bears in the country.

Climate change has made the problem worse: vegetables, berries and acorns, which the bears rely on, are growing later in the season and becoming more scarce, Adcock said. “But they know that one food source remains unchanged: human rubbish.”

This has brought hungry bears closer to towns than ever before, with 50,000 recorded bear sightings last year.

In a 2026 environment white paper, the government described the animals as “a serious threat to public safety and peace,” while easing bear hunting rules and introducing a population control roadmap. The plan aims to reduce the bear population to between 62% and 67% of current levels across a number of prefectures by 2030, through culling.

Adcock said that while there is still a general cultural preference for coexistence, the priority has shifted to ensuring immediate public safety and responding efficiently to threats.

The Asiatic black bear population has drastically increased in Japan. Picchio Wildlife Research Center

“Often, fireworks are set off in towns to scare off bears,” said Adcock. “But when it’s not enough, the police or military is deployed, which is often synonymous with euthanizing the bears, especially if it’s during the day and there’s people around.”

“We want to show that coexistence through nonlethal management, including technology, is perfectly achievable,” he added.

High-tech alternatives

Regions prone to bear encounters, such as Gunma, Toyama and Ishikawa, have started equipping forests surrounding residential areas with movement-monitoring cameras that use AI to identify bears and notify local officials. The system, developed by Hokuriku Electric Power Company along with communications systems company Hokutsu, has allowed authorities to issue warnings to locals and take action to drive the bear farther away from town, according to reports.

In Hokkaido, KDDI SmartDrone set up a drone port in the town of Shintotsukawa that can get a drone airborne within 10 minutes of a bear sighting, tracking the animal until help arrives. Nonlethal methods are usually prioritized to drive the bears away.

AI and drones are “very efficient for detection, and quite helpful for deterrence,” Adcock said. The technology has also proven effective elsewhere in the world, such as the US, where a small 2024 study found that drones in Montana successfully hazed bears away from human habitations 91 percent of the time.

But the technology isn’t practical for individuals looking to keep bears off their property. That’s where the solar-powered, animatronic “Monster Wolf” comes in. The $4,000 robot was originally developed to protect agricultural crops from bears by mimicking the howl of the extinct Japanese wolf to scare them away.

Motohiro Miyasaka, the managing director of Wolf Kamui Co., the company marketing the robot, told CNN that its sales have doubled “following the frequent sightings of bears in urban areas in Japan since last year.”

The company is developing a portable 8-inch plush version, for those “who enjoy stream fishing, camping and hiking,” Miyasaka said. “The Monster Wolf Mini will be tested around the end of 2026.”

A family of Asiatic black bears roaming freely Picchio Wildlife Research Center

However, these systems aren’t a silver bullet according to Tokyo-based engineer Danyel Koca. “The use of AI, drones and robots costs a lot,” he told CNN. “They’re not easy to build, to use and to scale nationally.” He added that they are lifesaving in certain cases, but do not provide immediate information for locals and hikers.

In August 2025, a fatal bear attack on a hiker on Mount Rausu in Hokkaido prompted Koca to look into bear incident data across the country. “There was no single, practical place to check the risk,” he said. “Japan already had a lot of bear information, but it was spread across many local sources. Prefectures and municipalities published reports in different formats: PDFs, local maps, Excel files, press notices, and Japanese-only pages. That made it hard to check one route or one destination.”

He decided to make public information usable before people go outdoors, and founded Kumamap, a bear incident tracker. Using local government data, national news, and verified community reports, Koca argues that the app supports coexistence. “If people understand the risk, they can prepare better and avoid surprise encounters,” he said. “Kumamap is helping people make better decisions in bear habitat.” As of early August, the app had nearly 6 million users and has tracked 156,631 public bear incident records, including 821 reviewed community records.

Kumamap is a Japan-wide database aggregating bear sightings. Kumamap

Traditional deterrents

Adcock recognizes the potential of technology for bear conservation but emphasizes that people on the ground are almost always needed to deal with the issue.

That’s why Picchio Wildlife Research Center recommends using Japan’s original “deterrent technology”: bear dogs. “Japan used to (raise) semi-wild dogs (which naturally would) chase bears away from the city,” Adcock said, adding that his organization uses Finnish Karelian bear dogs to reduce human-bear conflicts by tracking, barking at, and chasing bears away from residential towns without harming them.

Karelian bear dogs were originally bred for the purpose of hunting bears in Finland. Now, they are used in Japan to help conserve bear species. Picchio Wildlife Research Center

“Despite bear encounters having almost doubled from last year, the towns we work with had the lowest records of bear encounters in a long time,” he said. “The method works, and we hope more regions and countries will look at it. Generally speaking, the way Japan is efficiently implementing new technology and nonlethal methods like bear dogs is something other countries can learn from.”

World.title: Trump’s theory of global power faces a reckoning in Iran and Canada
World.content:
Donald Trump’s presidency rests on the premise that he and the United States are so powerful that allies and enemies alike must submit to his will.

His break with decades of US foreign policy doctrine is laced through his speeches and national security strategies. It was best explained in January by top aide Stephen Miller, who told CNN’s Jake Tapper that “iron laws” dictate a real world that is “governed by strength, that is governed by force, that is governed by power.”

But the philosophy faces its most serious tests in deepening showdowns with Iran and Canada.

Iran has defied the might of the US military for six months in a war Trump started but has been unable to end.

Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney, who shut down trade talks with Washington, has meanwhile argued more forcefully than any other Western leader that the US under Trump “has changed.” He told his country Saturday that Trump was using “economic integration as a weapon.”

It is a commentary on the extreme disruption of the Trump era that Canada, one of America’s most loyal friends, has found itself in a similar state of economic warfare with the US as Iran, one of Washington’s worst foes.

But the Trump administration left no doubt Monday what it wants as it fights a trade war with Ottawa and a shooting war with Tehran.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced an “economic onslaught” against Iran’s global financial connections, drawing an analogy with the D-Day invasion that turned the tide in World War II.

Trump, meanwhile warned on social media that “The U.S.A. will always be far bigger, richer, and stronger than Canada.” He added: “Someone should get these clowns to ‘fall in line.’”

President Donald Trump speaks during a campaign rally for in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, on August 21. Evan Vucci/Reuters

Will Trump stay the course?

The administration’s rhetoric Monday suggests that Trump is now sending the US economy to war.

Trump hopes to chalk up a lopsided trade deal with Canada and to finally bring about the downfall of Iran’s regime.

But the way forward is uncertain on both fronts because the president often backs down when the economic consequences of his attempts to assert his authority become clear.

Any prolonged US effort to prevail over Canada and Iran — and third-party nations sanctioned in his bid to shut down Tehran’s financial networks — could trigger retaliation that causes energy and food price hikes for US consumers. It could also rattle US markets at a time when some investors fear a bond crisis.

If Monday’s threats are the precursor to more TACOs (“Trump always chickens out”), the president will undermine his own power and the nation’s, and slip closer to lame-duck status as difficult midterm elections loom in November.

What Trump could achieve by strangling Iran’s economy

Bessent’s announcement was the latest US effort to find a new way out of the war with Iran.

But the D-Day analogy seemed tonally off, given the terrible sacrifices made by American soldiers to liberate Europe. And unlike Bessent, allied commander Gen. Dwight Eisenhower didn’t spent days in 1944 previewing a massive attack only to follow through with new threats of sanctions and no timeline.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent points as reporters raise their hands during a news conference at the Treasury Department in Washington, DC, on August 24. Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

Still, administration skeptics often ignore the genuine power that Trump could wield by clever use of economic warfare.

A truly global effort to cut off Iran’s pathways to finance and trade could inflict extreme damage on an already devastated economy.

“It can work if we can get the buy-in of our partners,” Max Meizlish, a former senior Treasury official, said on CNN News Central Monday, specifically referring to Bank Melli, an Iranian commercial bank controlled by the government that operates in France, Germany and elsewhere and is a cog in Iran’s efforts to evade sanctions.

Kenneth Rogoff, a former IMF chief economist who is now a Harvard University chair, told CNN’s Richard Quest: “Fundamentally, sanctions work if you can get most of the world behind you. But if they’re not, it’s very hard.”

Trump might have had more success with such an approach before alienating US allies with a war many regard as unwise and illegal.

And the White House may be misreading its capacity to influence events inside Tehran. Signs of disagreement between pragmatists and hardliners over the economy are encouraging. But Washington has for decades over-read such tea leaves and assumed regime collapse would follow.

Most damagingly, the Trump administration is sending signals that it may not be serious about its own policy.

There was no immediate action against an array of Chinese banks that facilitate Beijing’s trade in cut-price Iranian oil. China has already said it will defend its interests — code for potential retaliatory reaction against the US that could further raise prices and anger US voters. It showed last year in threatening to curtail rare earth mineral exports critical to the US defense and tech industries that it can counter Trump’s power.

And the US leader also has a big date circled on his calendar — the state visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping next month. It’s hard to see him souring the atmosphere before then.

In a revealing moment, Bessent only reinforced doubts about the administration’s staying power. He was asked why he was not immediately imposing secondary sanctions on entities that deal with Iran.

“Well, we are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behavior; why would I want to blow up the global financial system?” he replied.

A worker secures a coil of steel at an ArcelorMittal Dofasco facility in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, on August 24. Cole Burston/AFP/Getty Images

Canada sees a showdown that goes beyond a trade dispute

The administration is less wary of sanctioning the manufacturers of Canadian hockey sticks than Chinese banks.

And cross-border rhetoric is increasingly toxic.

“We have to remember, Canada is a state. Sorry, Freudian slip. That was actually an accident,” Vice President JD Vance said Monday.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford said at a news conference that “I have a lot of real estate on my ass, so (Trump) has a lot of room to kiss my ass.”

Venting can sometimes create political room to relaunch talks.

But Canadians believe they are embroiled in more than a trade dispute.

Drew Dilkens, the mayor of Windsor, Ontario, just across from Detroit, explained the damage inflicted by Trump’s 51st-state claims. “When you say it the first time, perhaps you can laugh it off, but it was the doubling down and certainly continuing to reinforce that,” he told CNN’s Brianna Keilar.

Ottawa said that, among other disputes, Carney ended trade talks after the US sought to water down its constitutional guarantees of bilingualism. Printing packaging for products sold in Canada in French as well as English is an inconvenience for US firms. But it’s a validation of the cultural and linguistic diversity that keeps Canada whole. Carney also implied Washington sought to restrict trade deals that his government could make with third countries.

“We will not allow any nation to dictate our future,” Carney said Saturday.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks at a new conference in Ottawa, Ontario, on August 22, after trade talks with the US collapsed. Dave Chan/AFP/Getty Images

As the smaller economy, Canada would suffer the most harm in a trade war with the US. But it can challenge American power. A long tariff duel could result in the mutually assured destruction of the auto industry on both sides of the border. And the growing impact of Canadian boycotts could weaken Republicans in key contests in border states Michigan and Maine, which could decide who controls the US Senate next year.

And in seeking to impose his dominance, Trump may have revealed another iron law of power that Miller did not mention back in January.

When people see their sovereignty and independence threatened by a hostile greater power, there is almost no price they will not pay.

World.title: Vance casts El-Sayed as ‘evil’ and tells him to ‘keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth’
World.content:
Vice President JD Vance said in Michigan on Monday that “there’s something about Abdul El-Sayed that is very, very, evil,” arguing that the state’s Democratic Senate nominee is symptomatic of a growing trend in America of fighting “for one group at the expense of others.”

His sharp criticism of El-Sayed — which included telling the Democrat to “keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth” — underscored how heated the rhetoric has become in this competitive Senate race, which could be critical in the larger battle for control of the chamber.

Vance cast the choice between El-Sayed and GOP nominee Mike Rogers as about who would fight for all Michiganders — even if they don’t agree 100% with Rogers — while obliquely suggesting that El-Sayed cared more about members of the Muslim community than other voters.

“There’s something about Abdul El-Sayed that is very, very evil and on the rise in the United States of America today, and it’s people who see themselves not as citizens of a common nation, fighting for every single person … but see themselves as fighting for one group at the expense of others,” Vance said at a rally in Sterling Heights hosted by MAGA Inc., a super PAC aligned with President Donald Trump.

“What I see is a man who has sympathy and compassion for people who share his religion, but have nothing for people who don’t. A person who will apologize for a murderer so long as he looks the right way, but will not understand the plight of an innocent child if that person has the wrong faith,” Vance said, calling on voters to “reject it in November” and back Rogers.

El-Sayed on Monday pushed back on Vance’s comments, casting the Trump administration and Republicans as the ones perpetrating evil.

“Evil is ripping healthcare away from working people in exchange for tax breaks for billionaires. Evil is making people pay more for groceries and gas while pushing for trade wars and actual war. Evil is dividing people for your own gain. Evil is selling out your morals for a little bit of power,” he said in a statement.

“Michigan is better than being lectured to by sock puppets from Ohio and Florida. We understand what’s at stake, and Michiganders will show you at the ballot box this November when we send Mike Rogers packing,” he added.

El-Sayed recently apologized for saying after a March attack on a Michigan synagogue that “violence is a cycle” and that “hurt people hurt people.” (The attacker lost family in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon a week before the Michigan attack.) At the time, El-Sayed also condemned the synagogue attack and antisemitism broadly.

Vance’s speech became more personal as he took aim at recent comments from El-Sayed that some viewed as racist. Earlier this month, the Democratic candidate responded to a clip of Vance at a rally referencing his late grandfather, “Papaw,” by mentioning second lady Usha Vance, who is the child of Indian immigrants and was raised Hindu.

“So do we think JD is taking Usha with him back in time to meet Papaw, or no…” El-Sayed wrote on X.

“I’d rather not talk about spouses at all,” El-Sayed told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Monday evening on “The Source,” as he sought to clarify his comment about the vice president’s wife. “The point that I’ve been making about his wife is that he believes in a political philosophy that says that some people are somehow more American than others.”

Vance on Monday said El-Sayed has a “weird habit of talking about my family,” going on to lob a series of misleading claims at the Democrat — a pattern that’s emerged from the GOP since El-Sayed won the Senate nomination in early August, with some Republicans resorting to overtly Islamophobic attacks.

“My message to Abdul El-Sayed is: You can pal around with terrorist sympathizers, and you can say that America deserved 9/11, or you could empathize not with the children who were targeted at Temple Israel, but with the attacker,” Vance said.

He continued: “But whatever you want to talk about, Abdul, keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth, because she’s way out of your league.”

While El-Sayed campaigned during the primary with Hasan Piker — a far-left Twitch streamer who once suggested that the country “deserved” 9/11 — El-Sayed did not say that. Piker has since walked back the remark, saying it was “inappropriate,” and El-Sayed has downplayed his relationship with him.

Still, at a state party convention over the weekend, El-Sayed remained largely dismissive about concerns over his relationship with Piker, a strident critic of Israel, telling reporters, “This is not a campaign that is about a single streamer in California.”

This story has been updated with additional details.

World.title: Rashwan: Accurate, timely information vital to combating rumors
World.content:
Egypt’s Minister of State for Information Diaa Rashwan emphasized the vital importance of coordination among government spokespersons, media advisers, and print, broadcast and television media outlets to ensure the rapid flow of accurate information on state and community affairs.

He said providing official accounts of events, decisions, measures and achievements would help close information gaps and prevent the spread of rumors and false reports aimed at undermining state efforts and social stability.

Speaking at an expanded meeting attended by 35 government spokespersons and media advisers, Rashwan said improving their performance was part of presidential directives to enhance Egyptian media and strengthen its role in raising public awareness and positively influencing public opinion.

This requires government officials to provide information promptly and respond to media requests in order to present the facts and the views of state institutions, he added.

Rashwan also pointed to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s repeated calls for opening up the public sphere and allowing space for different opinions on issues and topics within the framework of the Constitution, the law and national interests.

Participants highlighted several challenges, including the spread of inaccurate information and fabricated reports on social media, as well as the reliance of some media outlets on social media as a source of information.

They also raised concerns that some newspapers and websites do not give sufficient attention to information provided by official sources.

The participants called for a clear definition of the roles and responsibilities of government spokespersons and media advisers, greater access to information within their institutions, and advanced training programs for spokespersons, media advisers, journalists and media professionals covering ministries and government institutions.

Rashwan said developing the performance of government spokespersons and media advisers was among the ministry’s main priorities and that training programs for various segments of the media sector were currently being prepared.

He added that the ministry would coordinate with government bodies and media organizations to establish clear mechanisms for continued cooperation and ensure the timely and adequate flow of information.

He also said the ministry would establish a framework for sustained coordination among government spokespersons and media advisers to prevent contradictions in the state’s media messaging.

He noted that several ministries and state bodies were working to regulate social media use and limit risks such as privacy violations.

Rashwan concluded by saying that efforts were underway to accelerate the issuance of a freedom of information law that would require government bodies to provide information to citizens, the public and the media, and regulate the ways in which such information is transmitted and shared.

World.title: Local Development Minister discusses development of nature reserves
World.content:
Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad discussed on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, a number of projects and proposals for developing nature reserves in a manner that ensures the sustainable use of natural resources and supports ecotourism.

She also stressed the need for regular follow-up of investment projects in nature reserves to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and standards, along with establishing a continuous environmental monitoring plan.

The remarks came during the 76th meeting of the board of directors of the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) which discussed a number of issues related to developing the environmental work system, supporting environmental projects and investment, maximizing the sustainable utilization of natural resources and following up on the implementation of decisions and recommendations issued at previous board meetings. These efforts aim to enhance institutional performance and support the state’s efforts to protect the environment and improve citizens’ quality of life.

The meeting was attended by CEO of the EEAA Sherif Abdel Rahim as well as representatives of the ministries of defense, industry, foreign affairs and international cooperation, planning and economic development, water resources and irrigation, health and higher education and scientific research in addition to a number of environmental experts and officials from the ministry of local development and environment.

At the beginning of the meeting, Awad affirmed the ministry’s commitment to continuing to develop the environmental work system and improve performance, as well as supporting projects that contribute to environmental protection and the preservation of natural resources.

She stressed the importance of coordination and integration among all relevant authorities and accelerating the implementation of environmental policies and programs to ensure that plans are translated into tangible results on the ground.

She explained that the board began its session by approving the minutes of meeting No. 74 and reviewing the implementation status of the decisions and recommendations issued by it, as well as the implementation status of the decisions of meeting No. 75.

This reflects the ministry’s commitment to continuously monitoring implementation rates and enhancing institutional efficiency.

Awad also pointed out that, as part of the state’s drive to promote environmental investment and encourage the private sector to participate in developing natural destinations, the board discussed several projects and proposals for developing nature reserves in a manner that ensures the sustainable use of natural resources and supports ecotourism.

The board reviewed the technical and financial assessments, permit durations and technical and financial proposals concerning several applications submitted by companies seeking to invest in nature reserves, while preserving their geological and environmental characteristics.

Awad further stressed the need for regular monitoring of investment projects in nature reserves to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and standards.

She called for a continuous environmental monitoring plan, environmental awareness programs and measures to encourage visitors to adopt sustainable practices, while ensuring that environmental impact assessment studies are conducted and coordination is maintained with the EEAA and relevant authorities to safeguard biodiversity and ensure the sustainability of reserve resources.

Awad directed that new environmental projects should focus on generating tangible benefits for citizens and visitors by improving the quality of services provided in nature reserves, developing infrastructure and facilities and enhancing the visitor experience. This would increase the attractiveness of environmental destinations and support ecotourism while ensuring full protection of nature, biodiversity and natural resources.

Awad also directed efforts to create a favorable environment for the private sector to expand environmental investments and encourage projects that generate economic returns and provide job opportunities for members of local communities, while ensuring compliance with environmental requirements and standards. This would strike a balance between supporting investment and maximizing the benefits of natural resources while protecting and sustaining them.

World.title: PM discusses with Fujairah officials steps to complete implementation of “Fujairah-Alamein” oil, gas company project
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, the attention that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi is giving to the establishment of Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company, describing it as a promising strategic project whose agreement was recently signed.

He noted that completing the procedures for establishing Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company and holding its inaugural general assembly meeting at the Al-Hamra Petroleum Port, affiliated with the Western Desert Petroleum Company (WEPCO) in New Alamein, comes within the framework of the firmly rooted strategic relations between Egypt and the UAE.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting at the government headquarters in the New Capital with Director of the Fujairah Amiri Diwan Mohammed Saeed al Dhanhani to follow up the procedures and steps required to complete implementation of the project following the establishment of Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company.

The meeting was attended by Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister Karim Badawi.

Madbouly stressed the vital importance and the project’s multiple developmental dimensions in the energy sector.

He also emphasized the importance of accelerating efforts and intensifying joint work to expedite the establishment of a special free zone under the name “Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company” in New Alamein City. The company will engage in the storage and trading of petroleum products and crude oil and enter actual operational phases, in a manner that serves the mutual interests of both sides and reflects the depth of the firmly rooted strategic relations between Egypt and the UAE.

For his part, Dhanhani thanked Madbouly and his government for their efforts on this matter and particularly to the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources for its support for the establishment of the company.

Dhanhani expressed the keenness of Sheikh Hamad bin Mohammed Al Sharqi, Member of the UAE Supreme Council and Ruler of Fujairah, to strengthen ties of cooperation with the Egyptian side.

He affirmed the commitment to expediting implementation of the project.

The meeting reviewed the project’s implementation steps, which come within the framework of supporting and enhancing Egypt’s role as a regional hub for energy trading and handling.

The project aims to develop Al-Hamra Port through cooperation and integration with the Fujairah Oil and Gas Corporation. It also includes the transfer of expertise and the application of the latest systems and technologies in use, thereby enhancing the port’s efficiency and bringing it up to international standards.

The project will also involve storing crude oil using the storage facilities at Al-Hamra Petroleum Port in New Alamein, maximizing the economic benefits and returns from Egypt’s infrastructure and capitalizing on the port’s unique location and advanced infrastructure to make it a strategic hub for crude oil storage and transportation.

For his part, Badawi stressed the importance of the project and the substantial government support provided by both the Egyptian and the UAE sides to ensure the success of this project on Egypt’s Mediterranean coast and to replicate the successful experience of the existing project in the Emirate of Fujairah.

Badawi explained that ensuring the success of this major project is a top priority.

He affirmed that joint teams from both sides are working in full and continuous coordination to achieve this objective, complete the procedures and steps necessary for implementation and establish a specific timetable for the various stages of execution.

He stressed that the ministry would provide all necessary support and overcome any challenges that might arise during implementation.

World.title: President al-Sisi: Together for more prosperous future for Egyptian, Chinese peoples, humanity
World.content:
This year we celebrate the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Arab Republic of Egypt and the People’s Republic of China. Egypt was the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with China in 1956, as an extension of the civilizational and historical ties between two nations whose roots extend deep into history.

As we mark this special anniversary between our two friendly countries, we also celebrate the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to Egypt as an honored and cherished guest.

Throughout history, Egypt and China have been united by enduring bonds of friendship and a shared legacy of civilizational achievement, embodied by the Nile River, the birthplace of Egyptian civilization and the lifeline of its people, and the mighty Yangtze River, the cradle of Chinese civilization and a timeless source of Chinese wisdom, culture, and philosophy.

Through the knowledge, sciences, and innovations they cultivated, these two ancient civilizations made profound contributions to human progress, creating an enduring arc of achievement stretching from the Pyramids of Egypt to the Great Wall of China.

Egyptian civilization made seminal contributions to fields such as medicine, engineering, and astronomy, while Chinese civilization pioneered transformative innovations that were remarkably advanced for their time.

The knowledge and discoveries generated by these civilizations were transmitted, developed, and built upon by successive generations of scholars and scientists, helping to lay foundations for the Industrial and Technological Revolutions and the unprecedented advances that followed.

Without this cumulative intellectual and scientific heritage, humanity could not have attained its present level of development across such a broad range of fields.

This shared legacy reinforces the legitimate aspiration of Egypt and China to participate fully and equitably in contemporary technological progress and to benefit from its advances, which will advance comprehensive and sustainable development for the peoples of both countries and other nations, and enable Egypt and China to continue their historic contribution to the advancement of human civilization.

The two countries were connected by a historic trade route that contributed to the movement of people and goods and extended from the Chinese Silk Road to the Red Sea and the Egyptian Suez Canal, the lifeline of global trade.

Along this route, missions and trade caravans journeyed from the coasts of China and Asia to Egyptian ports on the Red Sea and the Mediterranean, which continue to serve today as an indispensable link between East and West.

For centuries, Egyptian ports served as major commercial hubs for the exchange of goods among Asia, Europe, and Africa.

These vital routes also enabled the exchange of cultures, knowledge, and ideas between the two peoples, further strengthening the historic bonds between Egypt and China and laying the foundations for centuries of extensive people-to-people, commercial, and cultural interaction.

This long history of engagement ultimately culminated in the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries seven decades ago—a landmark moment that opened a new chapter in bilateral relations and paved the way for their continued development and flourishing.

Egypt was the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with the People’s Republic of China, at a pivotal moment when Egypt affirmed its support for the right of peoples to freely choose their own political and economic systems.

Egypt thereby paved the way for Arab and African relations with China, which have expanded and flourished over the decades, culminating in the establishment of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

Egypt has consistently adhered to the One-China principle and rejected interference in China’s internal affairs. It supported the restoration of China’s permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, while China supported Arab rights and the right of the Palestinian people to establish their independent state.

These historic positions remain deeply engraved in the collective memory of both nations as enduring milestones in their relationship.

As the Egyptian and Chinese peoples commemorate this cherished anniversary, they recall this shared history not only with pride, but also as a lasting foundation for solidarity and a source of renewed momentum for deeper cooperation, mutual support, and partnership in the years ahead.

Over the past seven decades, Egypt-China relations have witnessed remarkable development, culminating in the establishment of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries in 2014, during my first official visit to the People’s Republic of China.

At that pivotal juncture, Egypt was determined to broaden and deepen its relations with countries across the world, diversify its foreign policy, and reach out to its friends and partners to forge stronger and more comprehensive partnerships founded on mutual respect, solidarity, and mutual benefit.

Egypt also exerted efforts to advance joint development in infrastructure, investment, trade, manufacturing, and technology transfer. China was among the first countries to demonstrate its keenness to consolidate relations with Egypt on the basis of these firmly established principles, which constituted the solid foundation for enduring and longstanding relations that have succeeded in achieving benefits for the two peoples and safeguarding the interests of the two countries.

Accordingly, the comprehensive strategic partnership established by the two countries has brought about a major transformation in bilateral relations. China has become a major trade and economic partner for Egypt, and Chinese direct investments have increased, including in the Suez Canal Economic Zone SCZONE, which has provided tremendous opportunities for Chinese investors to generate returns and benefit from the significant advantages available to foreign investors in the zone.

The SCZONE contains industrial areas hosting numerous factories of international companies from various countries seeking to benefit from these opportunities, as well as from Egypt’s geographical location at the heart of the world, as an essential link between East and West.

Chinese companies have also contributed to numerous major national projects, such as the construction of the Central Business District in the New Capital, the launch of the electric railway to the Tenth of Ramadan City, the construction of renewable energy power plants, the development of ports, and other projects that formed part of the Egyptian state’s national plans to overhaul its infrastructure, which Egypt undertook with the cooperation with a number of different countries, including China.

This has contributed to Egypt’s globally advanced position in the field of infrastructure, which is pivotal to laying the foundations for an advanced and integrated industrial base, and transforming Egypt into a global logistics hub for industry, trade, and services.

This significant progress in strengthening and modernizing Egypt’s infrastructure has reinforced its position as an attractive destination for major industrial investments from around the world. China has been among the leading countries keen to expand its industrial presence in Egypt and capitalize on the country’s strategic location, advanced infrastructure, and the significant investment opportunities and competitive advantages it offers.

Egypt and China share a common commitment to harnessing the synergies between Egypt’s strategy for industrial localization and China’s strategy for high-quality development, with a view to attracting greater Chinese industrial investment to Egypt. Priority sectors include electric vehicles, energy-storage batteries, renewable energy, electronics, components for seawater desalination plants, shipbuilding, and other advanced industries.

This cooperation also extends to promoting technology transfer in telecommunications, artificial intelligence, and space sciences, which represent key priorities for economic and technological development and promising avenues for expanding Egypt-China cooperation in the next phase of our strategic partnership.

China’s development and its ability to achieve remarkable economic progress and eradicate extreme poverty have been an inspiration to developing countries seeking to realize their aspirations for modernization and advancement.

Egypt views this development positively, while at the same time believing that developing countries have a tremendous opportunity to achieve economic advancement in accordance with a development model suited to their respective circumstances and compatible with their historical and cultural contexts.

In this vein, it is important to underscore the need to create an appropriate international environment that enables these countries to achieve this desired objective.

From this standpoint, Egypt has played its constructive regional and international role over the past decades and adhered to the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and the rules-based international order. Egypt has worked to contribute to supporting international organizations in carrying out their essential role in safeguarding international peace and security.

It has made tangible contributions to peacekeeping and peacebuilding operations and participated, alongside all parties of the international community, in efforts to enhance the role of international economic organizations in achieving global sustainable development and advancing the United Nations development goals.

Egypt has firmly maintained its position in support of strengthening the voice of the Global South and promoting its representation in international institutions, in a manner that respects the right of these countries to express their will and takes their concerns into consideration.

Egypt has joined a number of emerging institutions and joined BRICS in 2024, as well as the New Development Bank affiliated with it and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

It also joined the Shanghai Cooperation Organization as a dialogue partner, out of its keenness to strengthen South-South dialogue and openness to broad and diverse partnerships with all countries of the world.

I therefore take this opportunity to congratulate China on assuming the BRICS presidency next year, and wish to express that Egypt looks forward to continued coordination and consultation with China in this regard.

Egypt has also adhered to a policy of strategic balance as a guiding principle of Egyptian foreign policy at a time when waves of polarization and competition are intensifying, emphasizing its independent foreign policy and calling for the international community to coordinate its efforts to overcome the global challenges that have come to threaten the entire world.

Egypt and China have become partners contributing together to enhancing the role of the Global South in the international system, in a manner that achieves greater justice and fairness for developing countries.

From the same viewpoint, Egypt has undertaken intensive diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the situation in the Middle East and prevent the escalation and expansion of the conflict, as the region undergoes a dangerous phase of conflicts that threaten regional security and stability and, indeed, threaten international peace and security.

In this context, Egypt and China agree on the necessity of resolving conflicts through peaceful means, taking into consideration the security concerns of all parties, and respecting the sovereignty of states as a basis for the peaceful settlement of conflicts. It is not in the interest of any regional or international party to widen the conflict or exacerbate armed hostilities.

In the same vein, the Nile River has been the foundation of Egyptian civilization and a vital source of its prosperity throughout history. Egypt and its fellow Nile Basin brothers have benefited from the Nile for thousands of years, with its waters serving as a shared resource and a basis for life, development and human well-being.

Throughout its history, Egypt has remained committed to supporting the development of the countries of the Nile Basin, particularly in the areas of water resources development and dam construction, including in the Sudan and Uganda, and, most recently, through its contribution to the mega-project of the Julius Nyerere Hydropower Project in Tanzania.

Egypt will remain steadfast in advocating for transboundary cooperation in accordance with the principles and rules of international law, rather than unilateral approaches that result in harm to downstream States.

Egypt firmly believes that the sustainable management of shared water resources can only be achieved through prior notification, consultations and consensus among riparian States.

In this regard, Egypt highly values China’s position that has affirmed its recognition of the vital importance of the Nile River to Egypt as its principal lifeline, and reiterates the importance of refraining from unilateral measures and strengthening collaboration in good faith to achieve Win-Win cooperation and mutually beneficial outcomes.

Just as Egypt and China have, over the years, written remarkable chapters in the history of cooperation and friendship between our two countries, we look forward to writing together a new chapter in this enduring relationship, whose roots stretch back thousands of years. We aspire to many more decades of progress and prosperity for our two friendly peoples, and to a future in which the world enjoys greater stability, security, peace, and development.

World.title: Sunu Assurances Liberia Opens New Office In Sinkor
World.content:
MONROVIA – SUNU Assurances Liberia Limited has officially opened its new office at 13th Street, Sinkor, Monrovia, marking another significant milestone in the company’s continued growth and commitment to delivering accessible, professional, and quality insurance services in Liberia.

The opening ceremony, held as an Open House event, brought together distinguished representatives from the public and private sectors, including the Central Bank of Liberia, Liberia Insurance Association, insurance brokers, clients, shareholders, business partners, stakeholders, and other friends and well-wishers of SUNU Assurances Liberia Limited.

The occasion provided an opportunity for the company to formally welcome its clients, partners, and stakeholders to its new premises and showcase an improved environment designed to enhance customer experience and service delivery.

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr. Habib Dia, Managing Director/CEO of SUNU Assurances Liberia, said the relocation represents more than a change of address, describing it as an important step in the company’s ongoing commitment to becoming closer, more accessible, and more responsive to its customers.

Mr. Dia reaffirmed SUNU Assurances Liberia’s commitment to providing reliable, innovative, and quality insurance solutions designed to protect individuals, businesses, properties, and wealth.

He also expressed appreciation to the company’s clients, regulators, brokers, partners, shareholders, and the wider community for their continued confidence and support, noting that these relationships remain fundamental to SUNU Assurances Liberia’s growth and success.

As part of the SUNU Group, Mr. Dia emphasized the company’s commitment to growing alongside Liberia, delivering excellence in customer service, managing risks with professionalism, and providing the protection and peace of mind that customers deserve.

The new office is strategically located in Sinkor, providing greater accessibility to clients and strengthening the company’s ability to serve individuals, businesses, and organizations.

SUNU Assurances Liberia extends its sincere appreciation to all distinguished guests, clients, partners, regulators, brokers, shareholders, stakeholders, and well-wishers who joined the company in celebrating this important milestone.

The company is pleased to announce that it is fully open for business at its new location at 13th Street, Sinkor, Monrovia, and looks forward to welcoming both existing and prospective clients.

With its new location, SUNU Assurances Liberia continues to position itself for sustained growth while strengthening its commitment to delivering dependable insurance solutions and building lasting relationships with its customers and partners.

World.title: Liberian Statesman Intensifies Call for Police Inspector General to Recuse Himself From US$317M Cocaine Investigation
World.content:
Monrovia – United States-based Liberian statesman and Pleasantville City Council member, James D. Barclay, has intensified his call for Liberia’s Inspector General of Police, Colonel Gregory O. W. Coleman, to recuse himself from the ongoing investigation into the reported seizure of cocaine valued at approximately US$3.17 million.

Barclay, who has been vocal on matters of national security, the rule of law and Liberia’s fight against illicit drugs, is urging the Government of Liberia (GoL) to ensure that the investigation is conducted independently, transparently and in a manner capable of commanding public confidence.

According to Barclay, the Inspector General’s decision to recuse himself would send a strong signal that the Liberian Government is committed to combating illicit drugs, money laundering and other forms of transnational organized crime.

He argued that the reported cocaine case, given its financial value and potential international implications, requires an investigation free from any perception of conflict of interest, undue influence or interference.

“Recusal would demonstrate that the Government of Liberia is serious about its fight against illicit drugs and other transnational crimes,” Barclay said, emphasizing that maintaining public confidence in the investigation is critical.

Engagement with U.S. Officials

The Liberian statesman also disclosed that he has begun engaging U.S. political figures regarding the matter, including a meeting with U.S. Congressman Jeff Van Drew.

Barclay said that during his meeting with Van Drew, he requested assistance in connection with the ongoing investigation.

He further said he was surprised when the Congressman appeared to have prior knowledge of information he was preparing to discuss concerning the case.

Barclay did not provide additional details about the information discussed or explain how the Congressman may have obtained such knowledge.

He said his engagement with U.S. political figures is intended to draw greater international attention to the case and encourage the Liberian Government to ensure that the investigation meets appropriate standards of transparency, accountability and due process.

Barclay said he intends to continue engaging relevant stakeholders in the United States to keep Liberia’s international partners informed of developments surrounding the reported cocaine investigation.

Calls for Institutional Independence

Barclay maintained that Liberia’s efforts to combat illicit drugs cannot be effective if questions arise about the impartiality or independence of officials directly involved in investigating major narcotics cases.

He called on President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s Administration and the relevant security institutions to take all necessary steps to protect the integrity of the investigation and ensure that anyone found culpable is prosecuted in accordance with Liberian law.

The reported seizure of cocaine valued at approximately US$3.17 million has generated significant public interest, with the case raising broader questions about Liberia’s efforts to combat narcotics trafficking, money laundering and other forms of transnational organized crime.

Barclay said Liberia must demonstrate that its institutions are capable of investigating major criminal cases without fear or favor, regardless of the individuals, organizations or interests that may become involved.

He also encouraged Liberia’s international partners to continue supporting the country’s law-enforcement institutions while promoting greater transparency and accountability in investigations involving narcotics trafficking and other serious transnational crimes.

No Presumption of Guilt

Barclay emphasized that his call for the Inspector General’s recusal should not be interpreted as a determination of guilt or wrongdoing against any individual connected to the case.

Rather, he said, his objective is to ensure that the investigation is conducted under circumstances that eliminate reasonable doubts about its credibility and independence.

As calls for greater transparency continue, attention is expected to remain focused on how the Liberian Government and the leadership of the Liberia National Police respond to concerns surrounding the investigation.

Barclay said the credibility of the process will ultimately depend on whether the investigation is seen by the Liberian public and international partners as impartial, transparent and capable of producing an outcome based on evidence and the rule of law.

World.title: ‘Desist From Political Solidarities In The Fight Against Crimes Suspects Are Not Convicts Until Proven Guilty’ Liberian Law Student Cooper Warns
World.content:
Liberian Law School Student Keah Cooper

A law student at the Liberia School of Law, Keah Cooper, has commended the Government of Liberia for its fight against not only corruption, but also against the abuse of drugs in the country and warned citizens to desist from all forms of political solidarities in favor of crime suspects no matter their status in society.

Cooper said political solidarities for suspects of criminal offenses pose a serious threat to the country’s justice system and are virtually undermining the credibility of the judicial system, or may prejudice judicial outcomes, if measures are not taken.

In a statement issued over the weekend, Cooper pointed out that all crimes, especially drug abuse, are serious national security threats, and if Liberians do not pay keen attention and work together, they could damage the future of the nation.

Cooper argued that the drugs law, which was signed into law in 2022, a first-degree felonious offense, is aimed to regulate, restrict, control, limit, or eradicate the illegal export and importation as well as the flagrant use, abuse, and proliferation of narcotic substances within the bailiwick of the Republic of Liberia and is not in any way designed to target any group of specific lawful persons.

“The drugs law should not be misconstrued and politicized as a witch-hunt or selective justice,’’ he stated.

However, the Liberian Law School student called on the government to remain within the confines of the rule of law in the fight against the deadly practices.

He added that the constitutional rights of all defendants are not negotiable and must be fully protected without any justification.

“As much as we all appreciate the government’s political will to fight drugs, or crimes in general, we are also keen to remind them to remain lawful, especially law enforcement officers, so that they themselves will not be the violators of law they are protecting or will not abuse others’ constitutional rights,’’ he said.

Cooper warned that “suspects are not convicts, and therefore should be treated as innocent until proven guilty, especially as regards their rights to due process, right to life, right to fair trial, right to a speedy and public trial, which are fundamental rights that must be protected at all times regardless of the persons before the law. ‘’

In an African legal system, “Taytay-mo-taytay” (the law is the law), Cooper intimated that all persons are equal before the law and must be treated equally, regardless of their status and capacity in society.

He encouraged Liberians to continue their advocacy for fair justice and respect for the rules of law.

‘‘Liberia deserves to be a crime-free society, and Liberians deserve to live a better life,’’ Cooper said.

“Drugs affect all citizens regardless of which party, religion, or community you are part of. Therefore, we call all well-meaning Liberians to support the Government of Liberia’s efforts in the fight against drugs, and desist from challenging law enforcement officers,’’ he added.

World.title: Liberia: Kogar’s MDR Expulsion Puts Koung, Unity Party’s Nimba Base Under Scrutiny
World.content:
MONROVIA — The expulsion last week of Senator Samuel Gongben Kogar from the Movement for Reconstruction and Democracy (MDR) may have been decided inside a party meeting room, but its political implications could extend far beyond the walls of the party’s headquarters in Monrovia.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

For the MDR, the decision represents the enforcement of party discipline and a reaffirmation of its alliance with President Joseph Boakai and the governing Unity Party. For Kogar, however, the expulsion creates a new political reality for a senator who has built an electoral identity that predates his most recent association with the party.

For Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung, the development could prove even more delicate.

Koung’s political strength has long been closely associated with Nimba County, while the Unity Party’s historic victory in the county in the 2023 presidential election was one of the strongest pillars of the Boakai-Koung ticket’s national success.

The question now emerging is whether the political disagreement between Kogar and the MDR can remain confined to the party or whether it will eventually begin to alter the political calculations surrounding Nimba ahead of the 2029 presidential election.

The MDR Executive Committee voted to expel Kogar after a disciplinary process that Chairman Cooper Kruah said was triggered by a complaint alleging violations of the party’s constitution and bylaws.

Kruah has insisted that Kogar was given an opportunity to defend himself and that the expulsion followed established party procedures rather than being an arbitrary political decision.

“Anybody who contravenes the Constitution and bylaws of the party, that person will be dealt with in keeping with what the law says,” Kruah said.

According to the MDR chairman, Kogar received a copy of the complaint and initially participated in the process but subsequently failed to appear for a further hearing.

“He was provided with a copy of the complaint, and he submitted himself to the investigation, but continued to ask for excuses, one excuse after the other,” Kruah said.

Kruah added that when the matter was scheduled for further hearing, neither Kogar nor his lawyer appeared, which he characterized as a waiver of their right to be heard.

The committee subsequently recommended Kogar’s expulsion and instructed that anything belonging to the MDR that remained in his possession be returned to the party.

“That means, for today, he is no longer a member of the party,” Kruah declared.

But the chairman’s explanation went beyond the disciplinary process and directly entered the broader political relationship between the MDR and the Unity Party.

Kruah accused Kogar of taking positions that were inconsistent with the governing coalition and argued that a politician cannot simultaneously participate in government while presenting himself as an opposition voice against that same government.

“This party is in collaboration with the Unity Party. We are part of the government. You cannot be part of the government and sit and play opposition in the same government that you are a part of,” he said.

Kruah was equally emphatic about the MDR’s continuing allegiance to President Boakai.

“This party stands with the Unity Party and stands with this president,” he said, adding that the party supported Boakai in the past, supports him presently and intends to support him in the future.

That position makes Kogar’s expulsion politically significant beyond the question of party membership.

The MDR is not simply another political organization in the Liberian landscape. It is the party founded by the late Senator Prince Y. Johnson, whose political influence transformed Nimba into one of the most closely watched electoral battlegrounds in the country.

And the response from Johnson’s family indicates that the dispute may increasingly become entangled with the unresolved question of who carries the political legacy of the late senator.

Amy Johnson, daughter of the late Prince Johnson, publicly came to Kogar’s defense following the expulsion. Her statement was sharply critical of individuals she accused of having betrayed her father while expressing sympathy and support for Kogar.

She argued that the senator’s expulsion was not necessarily an unexpected political development and warned him to be cautious, drawing comparisons with what she described as the treatment her late father received from people within his own political circle.

Her intervention was also framed around the history of the MDR and her father’s political legacy. She questioned why individuals who had previously left or opposed the party had returned following Prince Johnson’s death, while recalling earlier internal battles involving her father and Kogar.

At the heart of her message was a declaration of solidarity with the senator: “Da My Pa Party: We Will Stand By Kogar.”

The statement does not automatically translate into an electoral bloc for Kogar, but its political symbolism should not be underestimated. Prince Johnson spent decades constructing a political organization whose influence was particularly powerful in Nimba, and the question of what remains of that influence after his death is likely to become increasingly important as the 2029 election approaches.

That is where the history of Nimba becomes particularly relevant.

The county has repeatedly demonstrated that it can produce powerful political movements around individual leaders, but its electoral history also shows that no politician has been able to permanently command every voter.

In the first round of the 2017 presidential election, Prince Johnson demonstrated the scale of his political influence when he received 107,430 votes in Nimba, equivalent to 53.50% of the county’s presidential vote. Joseph Boakai received 39,964 votes, representing 19.90%, while George Weah secured 16,002 votes, or 7.97%, and Alexander Cummings received 12,548 votes, representing 6.25%.

The political importance of PYJ’s influence became even more evident in the runoff. Following his decision to support George Weah, Weah’s Nimba vote rose to 73,434, representing 57.14%, while Boakai received 55,083 votes, or 42.86%.

That election created a powerful precedent in Liberian politics: a dominant Nimba political actor could potentially move a substantial portion of the county’s electorate behind a national presidential candidate.

But subsequent elections have complicated the idea that Nimba’s vote belongs permanently to any one political leader.

When Koung contested the 2020 senatorial election on the MDR ticket, he won with 37,899 votes, representing 36.12% of the vote. Edith Gongloe-Weh received 34,153 votes, or 32.55%, while Garrison Yealue secured 15,607 votes, representing 14.87%.

Koung therefore became senator with considerably less than half of the countywide vote, demonstrating that even a strong political figure backed by an influential political machine could not automatically consolidate the entire Nimba electorate.

The political landscape changed dramatically in 2023 when Koung moved from the Senate to the national stage as Boakai’s running mate.

The Boakai-Koung ticket received 138,070 votes in Nimba in the first round of the presidential election, representing 59.53% of the county’s vote. George Weah received 50,427 votes, or 21.74%, while Tiawan Gongloe secured 17,024 votes, representing 7.34%.

In the runoff, the Boakai-Koung ticket increased its dominance, receiving 144,646 votes, or 74.14%, compared with Weah’s 50,453 votes, or 25.86%.

Those numbers established Koung as an exceptionally important electoral figure in Nimba and gave the Unity Party a political advantage that would be difficult for any rival to ignore.

But there is another way to read the same numbers.

Even when Nimba had a son of the county on the national ticket, approximately one-quarter of voters in the runoff still supported the opposing candidate.

That is perhaps one of the most important lessons for the Unity Party as it considers 2029. Nimba can strongly support a political ticket without becoming politically unanimous.

That distinction becomes even more important when examining what happened after Prince Johnson’s death.

The late senator died in November 2024, leaving behind not only a vacant Senate seat but also a political structure whose future was suddenly uncertain.

The April 2025 senatorial by-election therefore became an early test of the post-PYJ political order.

Kogar emerged as the MDR candidate and won decisively, receiving 62,136 votes, representing 52.08% of the countywide vote. Edith Gongloe-Weh received 40,506 votes, or 33.95%, while Mack Gblinwon secured 7,489 votes, representing 6.28%.

The significance of Kogar’s victory extends beyond the percentage. He crossed the 50% mark in a countywide election and accumulated more than 62,000 votes at a time when Nimba was still adjusting to the death of one of its most influential political figures.

Whether those votes represented Kogar personally, the MDR machinery, the continuing influence of the PYJ political network, support from Koung, or some combination of all four is difficult to establish with mathematical certainty.

But the result nevertheless demonstrated that Kogar possessed a substantial electoral constituency. That makes his expulsion from the MDR a political experiment of sorts.

The next question is whether Kogar’s support is attached primarily to the party, to the political establishment that backed him, to his own personality, or to a combination of those factors.
