World.title: Officer: Ukraine downs 80% of Russian weapons in record attacks
World.content:
Russia has been carrying out record‑breaking combined air attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding areas of the Ukrainian capital in recent nights and days. According to Liias, the Ukrainians have held up surprisingly well despite the extensive attacks.

"About 80 percent of all the attacking weapons have been shot down. Considering that Russia has combined several different types of attack weapons – conventional drones, jet‑powered drones, ballistic missiles and anti‑ship missiles – this has put Ukraine's entire air defense capability and the whole spectrum, from machine guns to Patriot missiles and fighter jets, to the test," Liias told "Ukraina stuudio".

Since 80 percent of the attacking weapons have been shot down, it is also not entirely clear what Russia was attempting to strike, Liias noted.

"Based on what has been hit, it can be said that they are still trying to affect or destroy Ukraine's heating plants, power plants and water infrastructure. Logistics companies and retail have now been added, and there is also no escaping Russia's brutality – schools and hospitals have been targeted as well," he said.

Russia's jet‑propelled drones are causing problems for the Ukrainians, however. "At the moment, the Geran‑4 and 5 are still in use, and the newest is the Banderol S8000, which is no longer classified as a drone but as a drone missile. They move considerably faster, about three times as fast, at speeds of up to 600 kilometers per hour. They fly at high altitude and can reach even 700 kilometers per hour when descending," Liias said.

This means that Ukraine's mobile air defense teams are unable to shoot down these drone missiles with machine guns and anti‑aircraft guns.

"And therefore Ukraine has to use air defense missiles to shoot them down or hope that when they dive, there is that brief window during which air defense teams can hit them with cheaper means – guns and machine guns," Liias continued.

However, this does not mean that the Ukrainians are incapable of finding a solution to the problem, he added. "If we look at the course of the fighting and the development of the war, technology turns things on their head about once a year – every measure has a countermeasure. I simply do not know at the moment what countermeasure the Ukrainians could use. Right now, air defense missiles and fighter jets are what are mostly being used to shoot them [drone missiles] down," Liias said.

What is important is that Ukraine is now once again able to use U.S.-made Patriot surface-to-air missiles. The Ukrainians naturally do not disclose how many they have. "However their addition is extremely important, because this is one of the few, almost the only means Ukraine has that can intercept a ballistic missile. A [Russian ballistic missile] Iskander races into the upper atmosphere and then dives straight down from there, practically falling vertically, and disrupting it with electronic warfare does not produce the same result. Therefore, it is extremely important that the United States continue supplying Patriot missiles," Liias said.

The situation remains fluid, but Ukraine's ability to intercept the vast majority of Russian attacks suggests its air defense systems are holding.

World.title: Supreme Court rejects EKRE challenge to Ülle Madise's presidential candidacy
World.content:
The Supreme Court of Estonia has rejected a challenge to Ülle Madise's presidential candidacy, ruling she did not have to resign as justice chancellor before being nominated.

On August 24, 75 MPs nominated Madise for the first round of the presidential election in the Riigikogu, set for September 2. The National Electoral Committee (VVK) registered her as a candidate the following day.

Three days later, on August 27, nine members of the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) parliamentary group challenged the decision, arguing Madise should have stepped down as chancellor of justice first because her candidacy conflicted with the separation of powers and the independence required of the justice chancellor's office.

The Supreme Court upheld Madise's candidacy, but affirmed the MPs' right to challenge the registration even though the President of the Republic Election Act does not explicitly provide for such appeals.

The court noted that only candidates who meet constitutional and legal requirements and are lawfully nominated should be eligible for election, and that any fundamental questions or concerns should be resolved as quickly as possible before the election takes place.

Independence rules protect justice chancellor

The Supreme Court ruled Madise's registration as presidential candidate last week was constitutional because the law does not require a chancellor of justice to resign before running for president.

The justice chancellor must, however, remain independent in their work and public statements while campaigning, and the court found no indication Madise had violated that requirement.

Under current law, the terms of elected and appointed officials end when they are sworn in as president. Any additional restrictions on officials seeking the presidency, the court said, must be clearly established by law.

The top court likewise noted the Constitution's requirement that the chancellor of justice remain independent is meant to protect the office's ability to carry out its duties, not impose unnecessary restrictions on the officeholder.

Court warns against political statements

The Supreme Court noted that Estonia's president primarily serves as a unifying figure that helps ensure the stability of the executive power and balance the country's constitutional institutions.

Although the president has some policymaking powers, including the power to veto legislation, appoint certain officials and represent Estonia abroad, the role is not directly comparable to the political role of the Riigikogu or local government councils.

Madise would assume those powers only upon election and after taking the presidential oath of office, not while she is still chancellor of justice.

The court noted Madise must avoid political statements during her candidacy that could undermine her position as justice chancellor, but had found no evidence that she had made statements that could call her independence into question.

The Riigikogu will convene Wednesday, September 2, to elect Estonia's next president. Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise is the only candidate.

World.title: Estonian racing cyclist hits dog at 60 km/h in Turkey, escapes injury
World.content:
Cyclist Rein Taaramäe hit a dog that ran into the peloton during the third and final stage of the Tour of Samsun in Turkey, but escaped without injury.

The incident happened on the third and final stage of the UCI 2.2-level race, on Turkey's north coast, when a stray dog suddenly darted into the group. Taaramäe, who rides for the Kinan Racing Team, had no time to react.

"I accidentally hit a dog that suddenly ran into the group. I was pulling at the front at the time and had just looked at the speed, which was exactly 60 km/h. I had no time to brake or react. But I'm fine," Taaramäe said.

Despite the incident, Taaramäe finished 83rd in the 146.3-kilometer stage after a bunch sprint finish, just over five minutes behind stage and overall winner Ramazan Yilmaz in his home race. He placed 51st overall.

Dogs wandering onto major cycle races and sometimes joining the peloton is a fairly common occurrence. However, there was no immediate word on the condition of the dog in this case.

World.title: Cabinet to review accounting lapses in defense sector
World.content:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform Party) announced that he has convened a government cabinet meeting for early Thursday morning, where he will ask the Auditor General to provide an overview of unclear accounting practices in the defense sector.

"From Minister of Defense Hanno Pevkur, Commander of the Defense Forces Andrus Merilo, head of the Center for Defense Investment (RKIK) Elmar Vaher, and Ministry of Defense Secretary General Kaimo Kuusk, I expect a concrete action plan at Thursday's meeting to resolve the problems quickly," Michal wrote.

"People in Estonia need assurance that every euro invested in the defense sector goes toward defending Estonia," he said.

In an audit of the state's consolidated annual financial report published last week, the National Audit Office found numerous serious problems in the activities of institutions under the Ministry of Defense, which in its assessment increase the risk of misuse of state funds and assets.

According to the audit, defense‑related inventories are incorrectly recorded in the state's consolidated annual report.

The National Audit Office issued a remark regarding the accuracy of inventory balances in the Ministry of Defense's area of governance amounting to €1.2 billion, because due to significant shortcomings in the Defense Forces' inventory accounting, it is unclear which inventories, in what quantities, and at what value are reflected in the balance sheet — and which have been unjustifiably left out.

Last Friday, Minister of Defense Hanno Pevkur (Reform Party) said that the National Audit Office's recommendation to temporarily transfer the management of Defense Forces assets to the Ministry of Defense is correct, and the ministry will do so.

World.title: Eesti 200 MP: Remote gambling tax cut not to blame for revenue drop
World.content:
A shortfall in projected tax revenues since the break came into effect at the end of last year is not solely due to that break, Tein said.

Tein's comments come after Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu said the tax break would cost the state €31 million in lost revenues, while Cultural Endowment (Kultuurikapital) head Margus Allikmaa called the tax cut an "unjustifiable" move which had left the culture sector with less funding.

The tax cut, introduced last December, was aimed at attracting more online casinos to register in Estonia, with the rate set to drop from six percent to four percent over two years. While gambling tax revenue fell by 9.7 percent in the first seven months of 2026, Tein said the decline was not caused by the remote gambling tax cut alone.

"A 9.7 percent decline in total gambling tax receipts is not the 'loss' caused by the remote gambling tax cut. The legislative amendment changed the remote gambling tax rate. But total gambling tax also includes [state lottery] Eesti Loto and traditional gambling, whose tax rates were not reduced by this reform," Tein said.

He pointed to the two‑month legislative error at the start of the year and noted that the Cultural Endowment's shortfall from remote gambling stood at around €956,000 — a fraction of the total gap.

Tein also rejected Reinsalu's €31 million figure, calling it a forecast and not a guaranteed loss, and warned that hiking the rate from 5 percent to 7 percent would translate into a 40 percent higher tax burden on businesses.

"The €31 million mentioned in today's report is also a forecast. Reinsalu himself told ERR that, according to the Finance Ministry's forecast, this is a figure calculated through 2029 compared with the previous assumption. That calculation assumes, among other things, how the tax base will behave in the future. It is precisely this assumption for which I want to see an impact assessment," Tein said.

The MP also noted that six companies that had not previously operated in Estonia have received operating permits in 2026 — already more than in all of 2025. "It would be equally mistaken to claim that the eight new operators that entered the market in 2024 came because the tax was raised from 5 percent to 6 percent," he said, adding that there is a long lag between a company's decision, obtaining a licence, and actual tax revenue.

Tein said the 2026 tax year is also a transitional period, with operators moving to stricter security and anti‑money laundering requirements. He warned that raising the tax rate now could undermine the long‑term goal of attracting larger international operators.

"The Cultural Endowment's interest should not be to have the highest possible tax rate. It should be to have the largest possible sustainable amount of actual tax revenue reaching culture and sport," Tein said.

"My position is therefore simple: let's give the agreed strategy time. If someone wants to reverse it now, I would first like to see an impact assessment showing that a higher tax rate will provide Estonia and the Cultural Endowment with more tax revenue that is actually collected three or five years from now," he concluded.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) has said the government will hold a debate on the issue in the coming weeks, adding that culture must not lose out and that if the tax cut does not bring additional revenue, there will be no further reduction.

World.title: Summer favorite Saaremaa drew more tourists this season
World.content:
While the tourism sector still has room for improvement, Saaremaa businesses and officials say the Western Estonian island has seen more visitors this summer.

Ferry statistics confirm what local islanders already noticed this summer: a marked increase in tourists on bike, arriving from both Estonia and abroad.

Eva and Thomas, two Polish cyclists, began their trek in Tallinn two days ago.

"Yesterday we were in Hiiumaa, and we're going to Latvia and Lithuania," said Eva. "And we are going to finish in Suwalki."

Veiko, an Estonian who also traveled from Tallinn, said he takes a similar cycling trip each summer, typically riding more than 100 kilometers in both Hiiumaa and Saaremaa.

"I rode 30 yesterday, today will be 60, and we'll see from there," he said.

Visit Saaremaa director Anu Lomp said new direct flights from Helsinki to Kuressaare have also boosted visitor numbers, with tourism businesses reporting a significant increase in Finnish guests.

"The Finnair route has also made a difference this tourist season," she said.

Room for improvement

Even so, local officials and businesses say the municipality has room to do more to attract visitors and come up with something new.

"People are always looking for something new and exciting, and that's what the tourism sector really needs — something new and exciting," Lomp explained.

Local businessman and politician Mart Maastik likewise said the local government could be doing more to support business, including tourism, on the island.

"You need to create things with a bit of a twist, because they're what draw people in," Maastik said.

Meanwhile, for the first time ever, Kuressaare's Söstar Kitchen & Bar even saw lines for its outdoor seating area. Owner Kristi Kuuse said their busy season kicked off earlier than usual this year.

"We were already seeing a nice flow of people at the beginning of May," Kuuse recalled. "This season has been very different from the previous two — it started early and there have been a lot of foreign tourists."

World.title: Kersti Kaljulaid: In a good school, children learn the art of being human
World.content:
In a good school, our children learn how to be human — empathy, searching for and finding shared interests, understanding and acknowledging different opinions, and also recognizing the boundaries where it is time to stop arguing and accept differing worldviews, writes Kersti Kaljulaid.

When I began school exactly half a century ago, we were starting from a much more equal position than today's schoolchildren. A child's knowledge was mostly a simple function of their age. Humanity's level of knowledge seemed such that in 12 school years one could give everyone an overview of the best of world literature, the cultural development of Estonians from the national awakening to flourishing socialism, the natural sciences through the centuries up to modern astronomy and genetics.

There was time to learn all 14 grammatical cases and to write at a level certainly higher than what journalism's utilitarian texts now offer. There was no "wide" and "narrow" math, no state exams except for literature. Yes, imagine — teachers were allowed to decide themselves what grade to give a child on an exam, and even those awarding medals trusted that result.

Meanwhile, humanity has created an enormous amount of new knowledge in the sciences. The idea of what constitutes a graspable amount of good literature that everyone should read has changed drastically. Access to knowledge is nearly absolute for anyone who knows how to use the internet. A classroom of children will never again have such uniform knowledge as half a century ago.

School, however, has not changed much. Children sit in classrooms sorted by age, lessons follow a predetermined program, and knowledge checks focus on proving that the program has been completed. Teachers' attitudes toward students have certainly changed. In my time, the teacher was always right — at least in my school — whereas today teachers feel they have no room for asserting themselves.

"Social skills still mature through interaction with other people, but the surrounding environment offers few opportunities to validate school acquired knowledge."

School struggles with a rapidly changing world because the human growth cycle remains the same. Social skills still mature through interaction with other people, but the surrounding environment offers few opportunities to validate school‑acquired knowledge — or rather, it shows that outside the prescribed path lie far better ways to cope than those found by diligently following it.

This is neither good nor bad — it simply creates different tensions in the school system, and it is inevitable. Among humanity's vast knowledge, it is increasingly difficult to choose what is absolutely necessary for everyone.

Children's greater autonomy makes classroom management different. Communication skills are more important than knowledge. Curiosity allows one to acquire a unique worldview instead of formal education and turn it into a profession. Some of these professions rely on scientific understanding, but even a fantasy world without any truth can turn out to be lucrative.

At the same time, there is a body of essential knowledge humanity must not lose — otherwise we would no longer know how to treat people, build houses, or create text that is clearly understood across languages.

School must still fulfill the same ultimate goal: to send out young adults who can function acceptably as members of society, achieve their goals without harming others, value others' contributions, and know how to take them into account. These young people must also be equipped with enough classical knowledge to study medicine, engineering, IT, or become creative artists.

So what should we do? Probably accept where humanity is headed and adapt. What does that mean? I suspect it means accepting the imperfection of education.

There are few things we can be certain will benefit the children starting school this week in their future working lives.

But something does remain. And that is the ability to function in human society. I do not use the word "values," because it immediately makes people want to enter a culture war. But something must remain: we must be able to live alongside each other. Even more — we must be able to defend ourselves together, grow the economy, care for the elderly, treat the sick, and distribute society's benefits in a way that results in the greatest number of satisfied people.

Life no longer requires acquiring these basic societal skills in order to grow up. Previously, a young person eventually had to ride the bus alone, buy milk and bread from the store, or agree with a neighbor on how to complete shared tasks.

"School must still fulfill the same ultimate goal: to send out young adults who can function acceptably as members of society."

Society now allows people to avoid human interaction both in stores and when using services. Our natural, life‑acquired ability to be one member of society declines — the ability to understand others' feelings, read body language, or talk through difficult situations. Half a century ago, it was common that there weren't enough balls or bicycles for everyone, and children had to learn to share. And if you didn't want to play alone, you had to make room for both your own and others' interests in the group.

Call these values or emotional intelligence — I call it the art of being human. And this is a person's true competitive advantage over any smart machine, no matter how well the latter pretends to be human.

Compassion. Sensing that something is wrong with someone even if they insist everything is fine. Understanding that a hug helps against sadness even if it doesn't remove the cause. Knowing that you must not hurt others. Knowing that evil must be confronted with lawful force — but not before all other options are exhausted. Understanding that those other options lie in cooperation between people with shared interests, such as neighboring nations who value free choice. Recognizing the necessity of rules and being able to follow them even when short‑term self‑interest suggests otherwise.

Call these things general competencies or values or whatever you prefer — but keep culture wars out of this discussion.

In a good school, our children learn how to be human — empathy, searching for shared interests, understanding and acknowledging different opinions, and also recognizing the boundaries where it is time to stop arguing and accept differing worldviews.

These skills can emerge only in a school environment that values meaningful discussion, and such an environment must be consciously shaped. If it were up to me, I would leave more room for independent decision‑making to every school leader and teacher. I would not impose so much oversight and control — I would let schools prepare children for life as they see best, and let universities measure knowledge at admission according to the needs of each field.

World.title: Narva-Jõesuu eyes €10 million revival for historic resort hall
World.content:
Narva-Jõesuu is buying back its historic resort hall from private owners, with plans to redevelop it with EU support as a mixed-use cultural and community hub.

Completed in 1912, the Art Nouveau-style resort hall, or kuursaal, is listed in Estonia's National Registry of Cultural Monuments. Much of the building was damaged during World War II.

More than two decades ago, a company linked to businessman Tiit Vähi bought the property with plans for a hotel and restaurant, but the project never materialized.

Mayor Maksim Iljin said those plans had once been realistic, but became unfeasible after the global financial crisis, Russia's annexation of Crimea and the ongoing war in Ukraine.

"And that's one of the reasons we've reached the point where we're buying the property back for the city," he said.

Events as soon as next year

Narva-Jõesuu City Council has agreed to pay €375,000 for the resort hall and nearly 3 hectares of adjoining properties, with the aim of seeking EU funding for the redevelopment.

The total investment could reach €10 million, Iljin said, noting that the city has already set aside up to €20,000 this year for basic safety work and plans to begin improving the surrounding grounds.

The Narva-Jõesuu resort hall (kuursaal) during Estonia's first independence era. 1925. Source: Osvald Haidak/Eesti Ajaloomuuseumi kogu/Muis.ee

The city hopes to start holding events in the park behind the hall next year.

The redevelopment could also include a new concert hall, addressing a longstanding shortage of year-round venues in town big enough to host major events.

"Our plan is not only to restore the existing resort hall but also build a concert hall, because outside the summer season, we pretty much have no options for hosting large events," the mayor explained.

High hopes for EU funds

The city plans to finance preliminary work, including surveys, expert assessments and design work, from its own budget.

For the rest, the goal is to secure EU funding when the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) begins, with three specific funding measures already under consideration.

The completed complex is envisioned as a year-round hub and destination, combining conference and event facilities with a restaurant, youth center and tourist information center.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports through Hormuz hit 2.2 million bpd in August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said that the country’s crude oil exports through its southern marine outlets, which link to the Strait of Hormuz, fluctuated between two million and 2.2 million barrels per day in August.

The ministry stressed that these outlets are the major conduit for Iraqi oil exports and a vital part of the national export system.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, indicated that southern outlets represent one of Iraq’s important export channels, citing the critical role that crude oil profits play in supporting the national economy.

As part of its attempts to increase the flexibility of the oil export system and minimize dependency on a single route, al-Rikabi stated that the ministry is supporting and developing various alternative export outlets through northern and western Iraq.

Al-Rikabi emphasized that Iraqi oil flows to the Turkish port of Ceyhan are continuing with volumes ranging between 150,000 and 180,000 barrels per day.

Advanced steps are being taken to explore the possibility of increasing oil exports through the Syrian port of Baniyas. This initiative would offer Iraq an additional outlet to the Mediterranean Sea, as stated by al-Rikabi.

The Iraqi official emphasized that these channels enhance the resilience of the export system and offer reliable alternatives when necessary. They also ensure the stability of Iraqi oil shipments to global markets.

In terms of transporting Iraqi crude oil through Jordan’s port of Aqaba, al-Rikabi stated that the project is still being studied technically and economically, with some critical issues yet to be completed.

The assessments include determining the total project cost and the targeted export capacity before any final decisions are made, according to al-Rikabi.

These Iraqi initiatives to develop alternative export channels arise as Baghdad aims to enhance the flexibility of its oil exports and diversify its export routes.

The attempts are part of Baghdad’s efforts to mitigate the risks associated with reliance on a single route while increasing the oil sector’s capacity to respond to regional and geopolitical developments.

World.title: US authorizes $800 million combat helicopter sale to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US State Department authorized on Monday the potential $800 million foreign military sale to supply Iraq with new aircraft and tactical systems.

The step aims to modernize the country’s aging military fleet and transition to a long-term bilateral defense relationship.

The US State Department said in a statement that the proposed sale aims to strengthen both the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by enhancing the security of an important strategic partner.

The Iraqi government has requested to buy Bell 412EPX helicopters, Bell 407M helicopters, and other related military equipment, according to the statement.

The proposed sale will improve Iraq’s capability to meet current and future threats by improving its rotary wing transport, reconnaissance, and air-to-surface targeting capabilities, according to the statement.

The Iraqi Ministry of Defense announced last October that it received US Bell 505 helicopters as part of a deal in which 15 aircraft arrived in two separate shipments.

In August 2024, Iraq’s Army Aviation Command received the first shipment of Bell 505 helicopters that will be used in training missions.

The new helicopters will prepare qualified pilots who can defend Iraq’s airspace from any attack, as well as drastically and visibly improve the training system using modern aircraft.

According to ambitious, cutting-edge plans in this field, these helicopters are expected to train pilots and improve the capabilities of Iraq’s Army Aviation.

World.title: Iraq weighs oil-backed U.S. bank loan to tackle liquidity shortfall
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi government is preparing to formally engage official U.S. banking institutions to secure an emergency sovereign loan facility backed by future crude oil export revenues, an informed official source disclosed to local news agencies.

The financing initiative is designed as a rapid intervention to bridge expanding state cash-flow deficits and secure public sector payroll obligations without resorting to domestic currency printing.

Financing Structure & Diplomatic Coordination

Inter-Ministerial Formulation: The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs are coordinating the joint terms of engagement to present formal loan requests to designated American banking institutions.

Oil Revenue Collateral: Debt-service installments and loan principal repayments are structured to be settled directly from Iraq’s international crude sales proceeds in global energy markets.

Inflation Prevention Policy: Securing foreign currency credit provides an alternative to unbacked domestic monetary expansion, mitigating risks of dinar devaluation and consumer price inflation.

Emergency Legislative Framework

To implement the credit facility, the executive branch is finalizing specialized fiscal legislation for parliamentary ratification:

Draft Borrowing Law: The proposed Borrowing, Grants, and Subsidies Law serves as a statutory spending bridge to sustain vital state operations in the absence of a comprehensive annual budget framework.

Parliamentary Finance Committee Review: Lawmakers are awaiting the official submission of the cabinet’s draft bill to establish clear spending ceilings, debt sustainability parameters, and compliance with national fiscal targets.

Key Macroeconomic & Monetary Indicators

Indicator Metric / Trend Economic Impact Monetary Base (M0) – May 2026 113.560 Trillion IQD Expanded by 13.761T IQD (+13.8%) since Dec 2025 Primary Cash Outlay Drivers Civil service salaries & core operating expenses Rapid depletion of available treasury cash reserves Target Financing Mechanism Oil-collateralized U.S. credit line Restores liquidity without inflating domestic money supply

The decision to pursue external commercial borrowing underscores Baghdad’s focus on maintaining monetary discipline amid regional geopolitical volatility and oil price fluctuations.

By utilizing structured sovereign credit instead of domestic quantitative easing, the Ministry of Finance aims to preserve liquidity reserves, meet mandatory salary disbursements on schedule, and protect the exchange value of the Iraqi Dinar.

World.title: Iraq ranks 61st globally in PPP minimum wage at $626: Report
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq ranks 61st globally out of 130 countries in monthly minimum wage adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), recording $626 per month, according to an international comparative index published by Visual Capitalist.

The ranking adjusts statutory wage baselines to account for local price levels, subsidized consumer baskets, and relative costs of living across economies, providing an accurate metric of real purchasing capacity rather than nominal dollar conversions.

Global and Regional Comparative Standings

Iraq placed in the upper-middle tier of the 130-nation survey, closely outpacing emerging and regional economies:

Adjacent Global Peers: Iraq ($626/mo) marginally led South Africa (62nd at $620/mo) and Guyana (63rd at $619/mo).

Regional & Major Economy Comparisons: Iraq recorded higher real purchasing capacity at the baseline wage floor than China (73rd at $544/mo) and Tunisia (77th at $513/mo).

Global Leaders:Switzerland led the index with a PPP-adjusted minimum wage of $3,804 per month, followed by Germany, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands, while the United States ranked 25th at $1,257 per month.

Lower-Tier Rankings: Developing economies at the base of the index included Niger (121st at $196/mo), Ghana (127th at $100/mo), and Gambia (130th at $67/mo).

Global Minimum Wage Rankings (PPP-Adjusted Monthly USD)

Rank Country Monthly Minimum Wage (PPP USD) Economic Context 1 Switzerland $3,804 Global highest wage floor — Germany / UK / Netherlands Upper Tier High productivity & social wage floors 25 United States $1,257 Federal baseline minimum wage ($7.25/hr) 61 Iraq $626 Upper-middle tier; leading regional peers 62 South Africa $620 Major emerging market peer 63 Guyana $619 Expanding energy-driven economy 73 China $544 Baseline regional statutory wage average 77 Tunisia $513 North African comparison 121 Niger $196 Sub-Saharan baseline 127 Ghana $100 Lower-tier wage floor 130 Gambia $67 Lowest ranking among 130 surveyed nations

The $626 PPP valuation reflects how local price subsidies, utility price caps, and domestic living costs expand the real-term domestic purchasing capacity of Iraq’s statutory minimum wage (nominally set at 350,000 IQD per month by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs).

While nominal conversion rates place Iraq’s minimum wage near $268 USD, purchasing power adjustments demonstrate that baseline earners retain greater domestic absorption capacity than several larger industrial peers where basic living expenses and utility tariffs are considerably higher.

World.title: Iraq’s Zidane Iqbal signs with Blackburn Rovers from FC Utrecht

World.title: Iraq launches 1M residential plot drive, unlocks $15B in refinery savings
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Chief of Staff of the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office, Ihsan Al-Awadi, announced on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, the official on-the-ground launch of a sovereign initiative to distribute one million serviced residential land plots to Iraqi families who do not own property, under the direct directive of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi.

In a video statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Awadi also revealed that the government has enacted structural economic reforms within the Iraqi Oil Refining Company during its first 100 days, projecting annual federal budget savings of approximately $15 billion.

Core Pillars: Housing Initiative & Fiscal Savings

1,000,000 Serviced Residential Plots: Targeted exclusively at low-income and propertyless citizens across Iraqi governorates to alleviate housing shortages and urban overcrowding.

300,000 Plots Prepared: Over the administration’s initial 100-day window, government teams finalized site surveying, legal allocations, and infrastructural planning for 300,000 residential plots, which are now ready for allocation.

September 1 Ground Launch: Implementation and field execution officially commenced on September 1, fulfilling cabinet directives framed as a “national project for every citizen.”

$15 Billion Annual Budget Savings: Implementation of a modernized economic operating model for the state-owned refining sector, designed in collaboration with Ministry of Oil economists and engineers, which optimizes operational efficiency without affecting employee salaries, bonuses, or entitlements.

Key Milestone Breakdown

Milestone / Policy File Target Scope Current Achievement / Projected Impact Land Distribution Initiative 1,000,000 Plots nationwide 300,000 plots fully demarcated and serviced within 100 days Target Demographic Propertyless Iraqi households Direct land title allocations for home construction Refining Economic Model State refinery operations ~$15 Billion/year saved for the federal budget Workforce Protection Ministry of Oil personnel Zero cuts to wages, allowances, or baseline benefits

Al-Awadi emphasized that expedited cabinet resolutions and executive decision-making under Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s direct supervision enabled municipal and oil sector bodies to reach these milestones within the administration’s first 100 days.

By linking high-volume residential land grants with fiscal efficiency gains in downstream oil refining, the government seeks to direct newly unlocked state liquidity toward municipal services, road networks, and utilities required for the newly demarcated residential zones.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate increases against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced an increase on Monday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,541.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,540 Iraqi dinars on Sunday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,545 Iraqi dinars and 1,535 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate increased, fluctuating between 1,541.5 and 1,541 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary sentences kidnapper of US journalist to 15 years in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Central Criminal Court sentenced Amir Rahim Jabar Lazim, a member of the Iran-backed group Kataeb Hezbollah, to 15 years in prison under the country’s anti-terrorism law for kidnapping US journalist Shelly Kittleson on March 31.

Kittleson was kidnapped during the daytime on Saadoun Street in central Baghdad. Armed gunmen pushed her into a silver vehicle, while another getaway car crashed during the escape. Iraqi security forces intercepted the crashed car and arrested Lazim.

The US journalist was kept hostage for more than a week when Kataeb Hezbollah freed her in early April ahead of a US-Iran ceasefire.

Kittleson, who has extensively covered the Middle East for publications like the BBC and Politico, expressed her gratitude to the Iraqi justice system on X and affirmed her right to seek compensation.

This decision marks a rare court step against a major, Tehran-aligned armed group in Iraq.

The verdict comes at a critical time for Iraq’s new government, led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, which is under intense pressure from Washington to disarm pro-Iran militias and place all weapons under strict state control.

The effort to disarm Kataeb Hezbollah has pushed Iraq into a severe security and political crisis, as the group has rejected the government’s disarmament mandates and vowed to expand its military arsenal.

World.title: The Rs 2.05 crore question: Can Meta be blamed for what its glasses record?
World.content:
A Delhi man has sent a legal notice to an Instagram creator and Meta Platforms after he was allegedly harassed and covertly filmed at a cafÃ© using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.

The footage was subsequently posted on Instagram and viewed more than 4.19 lakh times.

He has demanded that the video be removed, an apology issued and â¹2.05 crore paid in damages.

But the notice, issued on August 24, goes beyond the actions of the creator. It seeks to hold Meta responsible in two capacities: as the owner of Instagram, which allegedly continued to host the reel after receiving complaints, and as the technology company behind the design and marketing of the camera-equipped glasses used to record it.

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF), which provided the victim pro bono legal assistance, says this is, to its knowledge, among the first legal actions in India to directly raise the liability of a smart-glasses maker for harm allegedly enabled by its product design.

The case has not been decided by a court yet and the claims in the notice, so far, remain allegations. The man, whose identity has been withheld and who is referred to as X, is represented by advocate Apar Gupta.





So, what allegedly happened?

According to IFF, X was sitting alone at a Costa Coffee outlet in Delhiâs Khan Market on July 24 when a stranger, who eventually turned out to be a creator, approached him.

The creator allegedly pestered and insulted him with unsolicited questions and remarks and followed him inside the cafÃ©. X complained to the staff and eventually moved to another seating area to get away from the unpleasant situation thrust upon him.

What he did not know, IFF says, was that the encounter was allegedly being recorded through Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. One or more of the creatorâs associates also allegedly filmed the exchange from other angles without his knowledge or consent.

The footage was posted as an Instagram reel on July 26. By August 6, according to IFF, it had received more than 4.19 lakh views, approximately 15,700 likes and over 500 comments.

X reported both the video and the account to Instagram on July 27. According to IFF, the reporting menu offered no category specifically covering invasion of privacy or non-consensual recording. The victim, therefore, selected âbullying or harassmentâ.

He also submitted a separate complaint to Metaâs grievance officer for India under âPrivacy violation â sharing of personal information or representation without consent.â

Instagram subsequently informed him that the reported material doesnât go against its âCommunity Standardsâ, according to IFF.

Why has Meta been named?

The most significant part of the notice concerns the glasses themselves.

Developed by Meta in partnership with eyewear company EssilorLuxottica, Ray-Ban Meta glasses resemble conventional eyewear but allow users to take photographs and record videos hands-free. They were launched in India in May 2025 at a starting price of â¹29,900.

The glasses have a small white capture LED on the front that indicates when the camera is being used. The notice argues that this warning is inadequate because it can easily be missed by someone who does not know that the glasses contain a camera.

âThe recording indicator on the said devices is inadequate and easily overlooked, and the harm that eventuated to our client is due to a design that is foreseeably enabled,â the notice states.

It argues that Meta âowed and breached a duty of careâ to X and was negligent in contributing to the alleged intrusion into his privacy.

Crucially, the notice argues that this liability arises from Metaâs own product-design and marketing decisions and is therefore separate from its role as an online intermediary.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Section 79 of the Information Technology Act provides conditional protection to online intermediaries against liability for content posted by third parties.

The notice contends that such protection cannot extend to a negligence claim arising from Metaâs own product design.

That argument has not yet been tested in court.

The Delhi dispute could now test a different question: whether a company that makes wearable cameras has a responsibility not merely to indicate that recording is taking place, but to ensure that an unsuspecting bystander can reasonably understand that they are being filmed.

World.title: As Pakistan takes SCO Chair, Modi slams use of terrorism as strategic asset
World.content:
PM Narendra Modi at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Framing security as a non-negotiable prerequisite for regional progress, PM Narendra Modi delivered a thinly veiled warning to Pakistan over state-sponsored terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. With Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif in attendance, Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.The remarks by PM on this occasion are significant also because of the timing. Pakistan assumed the rotating chairmanship of the SCO from Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday and will host the heads of state summit next year, for which it will invite Modi along with all other leaders.Modi made the remarks while expanding on Indiaâs SCO vision - Security, Connectivity and Opportunity - that he articulated in Tianjin last year. With Chinese President Xi Jinping also present, the PM reiterated India's position that all connectivity initiatives must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States as this is also the "fundamental spirit" of the SCO Charter.Modi said that terrorism continued to pose a serious challenge to humanity and itâs important to not remain confined to an action-reaction approach in the fight against the menace.âWe must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,â said the PM, without naming Pakistan as the SCO Charter doesnât allow members to raise bilateral differences.India and Pakistan together joined the China-dominated Eurasian grouping as full members in 2017. For India, the security-oriented SCO has served as a platform not just to assert its strategic autonomy but also flag regional risks from state-sponsored terrorism.Modi said that the blocâs shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan and that India will continue to contribute to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to the people of the country.Modi also addressed the West Asia crisis in his remarks saying it was affecting energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains around the world and recalling his message earlier that conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield. âThe countries of the Global South bear the greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on the battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy,â he said.While underlining the importance India attaches to SCO, Modi said that at a time the world is passing through uncertainty and instability, the Organisation must transform the shared geography into shared opportunities and bring about positive change in the lives of the people. Describing SCO as a confluence of great civilisations, cultures, and ideas, he said that over the next 25 years, people-to-people ties should remain at the heart of cooperation among the member-states.âThe true measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts create for young people, how many new markets open up for our entrepreneurs, how much our farmers benefit from technology, and how much better the lives of our citizens become,â said the PM.According to an Indian readout of Modiâs participation in the summit, Modi stated that strong and trusted connectivity initiatives were important for the groupâs shared progress and prosperity.âUnderlining that India supports connectivity efforts that link markets, enhance trade and open new opportunities for development, he reiterated that such efforts should respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of nations. He further elaborated that technology, entrepreneurship, innovation, start-ups and people-to-people initiatives open immense opportunities for people in the SCO countries,â said the Indian readout.

World.title: Fish video row: UP Congress chief Ajay Rai files defamation case against CM Yogi for 'hurting faith'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The political row over an alleged âfish feastâ at a Congress event in Ayodhya escalated on Tuesday, with Uttar Pradesh Congress president

filing a defamation case against

, alleging that the chief minister's remarks had âhurt his faith.â

Rai approached the MP-MLA court in Lucknow, the UP Cong chief also denied eating fish at the event, saying he is a vegetarian. âWe do not eat non-vegetarian food. The allegation of a fish feast against me is wrong. The chief minister's statement has hurt my faith,â Rai told ANI.

Rai said he had filed the defamation case to seek legal action and challenged the chief minister to produce evidence in court.

âYogi cast aspersions on my character and my dietary habits; he claimed that I visit Hanuman Garhi, apply the tilak and sandalwood paste, and pay obeisance to Lord Ram, only to subsequently feast on fish.

The fact is, we are not non-vegetarians; we hail from Kashi, the city of Baba Vishwanath. The chief minister levelled a false allegation. I have filed a defamation suit here today. If the CM possesses evidence, he should present it in court and prove whether I am in the wrong or he is,â Rai said.

Explaining his presence at the event, Rai said he had been invited to a fish feast organised by the Nishad community and attended it out of respect for the organisers.





âI was invited to a fish feast organised by the Nishad community, a community whose livelihood involves rearing, selling, and consuming fish. I would not disrespect or insult anyone's event, so I attended and participated. He alleged that I consumed fish during the month of Sawan. I believe such tactics are characteristic of the BJP, not us,â Rai added.

The remarks came days after Uttar Pradesh CM

Adityanath launched a sharp attack on Rai over the alleged incident at an Ayodhya programme organised by members of the Nishad community.

The controversy erupted after a video showing fish being prepared at the Congress event surfaced on social media during the month of Shravan, when many Hindus observe dietary restrictions.

The event was held to welcome Rai, who had attended a programme organised by the Nishad community. The issue quickly became political, with the BJP targeting Rai over the alleged feast and the Congress rejecting the allegations.

Addressing a gathering in Raebareli on August 24, Adityanath accused Rai of âduplicityâ for visiting Hanumangarhi to offer prayers and later attending a programme where fish was allegedly served.

âYou saw the behaviour of the Congress state president: he goes to offer prayers at Hanumangarhi, but later outside he enjoys a feast of fish. He could have eaten whatever he wanted outside-anywhere other than Ayodhya.

Yet, this is the duplicity they display,â Adityanath said.

âEven a chameleon would be put to shame by these people; it would wonder what kind of human species this is-chanting 'Ram-Ram' inside the temple and feasting on fish the moment they step out,â he added.

The chief minister also accused Rai of not standing up to mafia elements in the past and referred to the killing of his brother, former MLA Awadhesh Rai.

âWhen a mafia don murdered his brother, this man did not testify against the criminal; instead, he knelt and bowed in submission before him,â he added.

Rai had earlier challenged Adityanath to produce evidence of him eating fish. In an open letter to the chief minister on August 28, he said he was a vegetarian and would quit politics if proof was produced.

âIt is an immutable truth that I am a vegetarian. If you have any authenticated photograph or video of me eating fish, make it public. I will retire from politics,â Rai said.

World.title: NCLT bars Subhash Chandra from alienating assets, stays Rs 6.5-crore settlement order
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) on Tuesday restrained Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra from alienating his assets and stayed an earlier order approving a repayment plan that would have allowed him to settle claims arising from personal guarantees for about Rs 6.5 crore.

A five-member special bench headed by NCLT president Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal said there was no clear majority in favour of the plan and the August 25 order could not be implemented.

"It is manifest that as per Section 419(5) of the Companies Act, there is no clear majority view capable of being given effect to. Therefore, the order dated August 25, 2026 of the third member, Nilesh Sharma, Member (Judicial) is stayed," the bench said.

The tribunal directed that Chandra, as the personal guarantor, "shall not alienate any assets whatsoever either directly or indirectly" and issued notices to all parties.

The restraint was sought by solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for dissenting creditors including LIC Housing Finance, Canara Bank and Union Bank. He warned that the "substratum" of the matter could otherwise be lost.

"We will hear you at length," the bench told Chandra's counsel after he sought to make a brief submission.





The matter will next be heard on September 23.

The dispute is also before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), where dissenting lenders have challenged the repayment plan. A three-member bench led by officiating chairperson Justice Yogesh Khanna heard the matter on Tuesday after Mehta sought time to decide whether the lenders would pursue the appeal.

The case follows conflicting views in Chandra's personal insolvency proceedings.

An original two-member NCLT bench delivered dissenting judgments in September 2025, with Ashok Kumar Bhardwaj approving the plan and Reena Sinha Puri rejecting it over alleged irregularities in the admission and voting on claims.

Third member Nilesh Sharma subsequently approved the plan on August 25, subject to changes involving disputed claims. The lack of a clear majority led to the constitution of the five-member special bench.

Under the proposed plan, creditors would recover around Rs 6.5 crore against claims of roughly Rs 22,006 crore. Chandra has disputed the larger figure, saying it includes liabilities of Essel Group companies for which he had provided personal guarantees. He has put claims against his guarantees at about Rs 3,990 crore.

Following Tuesday's order, Chandra said according to news agency PTI, "We have complete faith and confidence in our judicial system."

World.title: Punjab health scheme covers 12,467 sepsis treatments worth Rs 51.58 crore
World.content:
Punjab Health and family welfare minister Balbir Singh

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

CHANDIGARH: Punjabâs Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana (MMSY) has covered 12,467 treatments for severe sepsis and septic shock at a cost of Rs 51.58 crore till September 1, highlighting the growing medical and financial burden of the life-threatening condition.According to data released by the Punjab health department, 10,961 treatments for severe sepsis accounted for Rs 44.33 crore, while 1,506 septic-shock treatments involved expenditure of Rs 7.25 crore. Health and family welfare minister Balbir Singh said timely recognition was critical as sepsis could rapidly progress to organ failure and septic shock.Sepsis occurs when the body's response to an infection becomes dysregulated, potentially causing tissue damage, organ failure and death. Almost any infection can lead to sepsis, with infections affecting the lungs, urinary tract, skin and gastrointestinal tract among common sources.âWhen sepsis leads to serious circulatory problems and inadequate blood flow to vital organs, the patient may progress to septic shock,â Singh said.Patients with septic shock may require intensive care, intravenous fluids, antibiotics, medicines to maintain blood pressure, oxygen or mechanical ventilation and other organ-support measures.The cost of such treatment can rise rapidly, making financial coverage crucial for families.Under the MMSY, eligible families receive cashless health coverage of up to Rs 10 lakh annually. The government said the scheme is intended to ensure that financial constraints do not delay access to critical treatment.Doctors also flagged the particular vulnerability of newborns to sepsis. Dr Shashi Kant Dhir, professor and head of the department of paediatrics at Guru Gobind Singh Medical College, Faridkot, said even subtle changes in a newbornâs behaviour could indicate serious illness.Premature and low-birth-weight babies can deteriorate rapidly, he said. Poor feeding, unusual sleepiness, feeling cold and changes in breathing should prompt immediate medical assessment.Antibiotics are essential when bacterial infections are suspected or confirmed, but their inappropriate use can contribute to antimicrobial resistance. Doctors advise against self-medication, using leftover antibiotics or stopping prescribed treatment without medical advice.Warning signs of sepsis in adults can include confusion, breathing difficulty, extreme pain or discomfort, fever or unusually low body temperature, clammy skin and a rapid heart rate.The health department said the treatment figures reinforce the need for both early recognition of sepsis and adequate financial protection when patients require intensive care.

World.title: Evening Newswrap: CJP calls off Sept 5 march after SC quashes FIRs; Congress says GDP must mean jobs & more
World.content:
The CJP on Tuesday called off its September 5 march after the Supreme Court quashed FIRs against students who participated in NEET protests.

BJP and Congress clashed over Indiaâs economic performance after GDP growth touched 7.8% in Q1 FY27. Congress questioned whether the growth was translating into jobs.

PM Modi at the SCO Summit called for a united fight against terrorism, urging countries to dismantle its financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe-haven networks.

TMC chief Mamata Banerjeeâs 28-year-old niece, Bristy Mukherjee, was found dead at her home in Birbhum on Tuesday, with police treating the case as suicide.

Karachiâs power crisis has worsened, with residents in several areas reporting outages lasting up to 24 hours.

Here are the top 5 stories of the day:

CJP calls off Sept 5 march after SC quashes all FIRs against protesters on Centre's request

The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Tuesday withdrew its call for a September 5 march after the Supreme Court, at the Centreâs request, quashed FIRs registered against students involved in NEET protests.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the court that the Centre remains committed to its three assurances to CJP leaders, not pursuing FIRs registered between July 20 and 25, not filing fresh FIRs in connection with the protests, and providing compensation to families of students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak.

BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad hailed the figure as a sign of economic resilience despite global disruptions, while Congress leader Pawan Khera argued that GDP growth must translate into jobs, higher incomes and better prospects for youth, farmers and workers.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday called for a united and uncompromising fight against terrorism at the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, saying there can be no âdouble standardsâ on the issue.





He urged the dismantling of terrorismâs entire ecosystem, including financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens, and called for stronger action against countries that support terrorists.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday invoked its special powers and quashed all FIRs registered against student protesters in different parts of the country during the NEET paper leak protests.The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said the order had been passed in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and shall not be treated as a precedent.The apex court said it was invoking its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution considering the future of the students who bona fide participated in the protests.The court, however, allowed Delhi Police to pursue the FIR against 2,873 individuals who were present at the Jantar Mantar protests, citing their serious criminal antecedents.This comes a day after the Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIRs registered against student protesters over alleged violence during protests against the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, also informed the apex court that the Centre remained committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to CJP leaders during their meeting with the government.Under the first assurance, the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25. The second was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.The third assurance was that the government would provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak."The Centre is committed to honouring the assurance given to CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after the NEET exam cancellation; however, three months are needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told the Supreme Court."As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.Following the apex court hearing, Cockroach Janata Party called off its September 5 protest against the Centre for failing to honour the promises made to persuade the group to withdraw the agitation."I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the Government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the CJP deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.After the hearing, Das said welcomed SC's order but also questioned why were these 'hardend criminals' allowed to roam freely in the society in the first place."Regarding the Delhi Policeâs apprehension, based on facial recognition technology, that around 2,800 alleged hardened criminals were present at the protest site, we argued during negotiations with the government that if these 2,800 hardened criminals were indeed present, the first question was why they were roaming freely in society in the first place," Das said while talking to reporters."Secondly, if they committed any heinous crimes, such as rape, murder, or other grave offences, at the protest site, then they should be prosecuted, investigated, and imprisoned," he added.During a hearing on August 18 on petitions related to the student protests, Supreme Court had indicated that it was inclined to quash the FIRs by exercising its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution.The indication came after the court was informed of legal complications in withdrawing the FIRs. Once registered, the cases can be closed only through a closure report, which the concerned Magistrate has the discretion to reject.Earlier, Supreme Court had also constituted a committee to examine allegations of excessive use of force by security personnel against students during the July 20 march over the NEET paper leak.

World.title: NMC opens eligibility certificate window for FMGE aspirants from Sept 1
World.content:
NMC opens FMGE Eligibility Certificate portal from September 1 to 30. Photo credit: IANS

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) will open its online portal for applications for the Eligibility Certificate (EC) for Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) aspirants from 10 am on September 1 to 6 pm on September 30, giving candidates who have not yet obtained the certificate an opportunity to apply.The EC is mandatory for candidates required to appear for the FMGE. The NMC has said candidates without an Eligibility Certificate issued by the commission will not be permitted to apply for the screening test. The next FMGE may be scheduled by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) in the coming months.The NMC, in its public notice and advisory, has advised candidates to carefully verify all details against their original documents before submitting their applications. It has also cautioned candidates against using proxies and advised them to keep their documents ready before beginning the application process.Candidates have been asked to provide an active mobile number so that any deficiency in their application can be communicated promptly. The commission has advised applicants to rectify any deficiency at the earliest to avoid delays in processing.For queries regarding the status of an application, candidates must mention the File Tracking Number generated at the time of submission. The NMC said no response would be sent in the absence of the File Tracking Number.Candidates who have already submitted an application for the Eligibility Certificate to the NMC in the past need not apply again, the commission clarified.

World.title: Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee’s niece found dead at Birbhum residence
World.content:
A 31-year-old woman, who was the niece of former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, was found dead at her residence in West Bengal’s Birbhum on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).

Police said that she was the daughter of one of Ms. Banerjee’s maternal cousins who was also a local Trinamool Congress leader in Birbhum’s Kusumba village under Rampurhat Police Station. On March 2023, she was also among 842 candidates of 2016 West School Service Commission panel whose jobs were scrapped as per a direction by the Calcutta High Court.

According to the police, the incident took place at noon when her body was discovered by family members on the second floor of her house. However, no note has yet been found from her belongings.

“Prima facie, her family members stated that she had been suffering from severe depression for the last few years. She was also undergoing psychiatric treatment and medication regularly. She got married in 2012. The victim was probably under stress owing to the ongoing divorce case,” said Santanu Adhikary, the inspector of Rampurhat Police Station.

The victim was among the 842 candidates who were terminated from their jobs in the State-run schools on March 11, 2023. The move came a day after the Calcutta High Court directed the West Bengal School Service Commission to cancel the appointments of all Group C staff who had secured jobs by unfair means, including manipulation of OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) sheets. These 842 included many more with ties to the then-ruling party, Trinamool Congress, and also the Bharatiya Janata Party.

The victim ranked 608 in 2016 State Level Selection Test (SLST) conducted by SSC and was used to work at Bolpur Government High School as non-teaching staff.

To be sure, the entire 2016 panel of SSC was later scrapped by the Calcutta High Court on April 22, 2024, in view of a large-level irregularities and favouritism in exchange for money to secure the jobs. Nearly 26,000 people lost their jobs after this verdict, who moved the Supreme Court. However, the Supreme Court further upheld the verdict on April 3, 2025.

“Her family members and relatives are being questioned. An initial unnatural death report has been lodged. The body has been sent for an autopsy,” said Mr. Adhikary.

World.title: Nepal flash floods aftermath LIVE: Disaster a climate 'warning signal,' says Nepal's Foreign Minister as death toll crosses 1,000
World.content:
Devastating floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 1,050 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), with nearly 4,000 more missing. Security forces are recovering more bodies from eight districts of the country, officials said. Around 4,000 people remain missing, while nearly 12,000 have been rescued, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said.

ALSO READ | Nepal disaster, a grim reminder to rethink preparedness | Data

A devastating glacial collapse in Nepal that unleashed deadly floods was a “warning signal” over the growing risks climate change poses to the Himalayan nation, its Foreign Minister says on Tuesday (September 1). “We believe that this disaster should be seen as a warning signal to the risk that climate change poses to Nepal,” Shisir Khanal said in an interview nearly a week since the tsunami-like wave of freezing water, rocks and debris carved a trail of destruction.

ALSO READ | The Bhotekoshi flood | A Himalayan tragedy

Flash floods, triggered by a collapse or avalanche of ice and rock near the Nepal-Tibet border, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal on August 26. The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

As many as 321 bodies were recovered in Chitwan district, followed by 216 in Nawalparasi East, 170 in Nawalparasi West, 95 in Nuwakot, 65 in Gorkha, 57 in Dhading, 41 in Rasuwa and 38 in Tanahun, according to NDRRMA.

World.title: TNAU ties up with Novonesis to find biological solutions for coconut root wilt disease
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Coimbatore, has tied up with Bengaluru-based Novonesis to develop biological solutions for managing coconut root wilt disease (RWD), and improving soil and palm health.

The MoU with Novonesis, subsidiary of Lyngby, Denmark, envisages expenditure of ₹67-lakh over a three-year duration for developing and validating probiotic bacterial consortia and nutrient-based biological solutions, with field trials and farmer participation forming key components of the initiative.

Krishna Mohan Puvvada, Regional president, Novonesis, exchanged MoU documents with M. Raveendran, Registrar and Acting Vice-Chancellor, TNAU.

The collaboration aims to translate research into practical and scalable technologies for sustainable coconut production.

A TNAU press release said coconut root wilt has emerged as a major concern in Tamil Nadu’s coconut-growing regions, particularly Pollachi, Coimbatore and Theni. Yield losses in affected areas have been reported at 30–60%, with losses of around 60% indicated in severely affected pockets.

Alongside assessing beneficial probiotic microbiomes and suitable nutrients for improving soil health, palm vigour and nut yield, the project also entails establishing a knowledge hub and conduct farmer skill-development programmes, field days and awareness campaigns in coordination with extension agencies and Farmer Producer Organisations.

World.title: Businessman honours late wife by building library at her alma mater
World.content:
:

A businessman Gandham Prasad is building a library and computer room at the Government Girl’s Junior College in Rajam, Vizianagaram district, in memory of his wife Bharati who passed away after an illness. Mr. Prasad chose the college for the project as his wife studied there about three decades ago.

His children Satish and Amulya are supporting him. Mr. Satish is a software engineer, while Ms. Amulya is associated with a corporate hospital in Hyderabad.

Municipal Commissioner Akurati Ramachandra Rao, the College Principal K. Janardhana Rao hailed the initiative.

Mr. Prasad who is popularly known as Balaraju in Rajam and surrounding areas assured officials that the construction would be completed within a couple of months.

Indian Red Cross Society chairman Kotta Sai Prasanath, IRCS-Srikakulam wing Public Relations Officer Penki Chaitnya said that the library and computer room would benefit students preparing for competitive examinations, especially girls as they will no longer have to travel to access study resources. .

World.title: Telangana Mahila Congress protests FIR against Rahul Gandhi
World.content:
The Telangana Pradesh Mahila Congress, led by president Errabelli Swarna, on Tuesday staged a protest at Gandhi Bhavan, demanding the withdrawal of the FIR registered against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and action against BJP and RSS workers over the alleged humiliation of dalit community members in Haldwani, Uttarakhand.

Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Swarna alleged that the FIR against Mr. Gandhi reflected the BJP’s “vindictive politics”. She also demanded registration of a case under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against those allegedly involved in “purifying” with Ganga water the place where Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge sat during a public meeting.

Mahila Congress leaders attempted to organise a rally under the banner of “Dar Mat” from Gandhi Bhavan but were stopped by the police, following which they staged a protest in front of the premises.

Ms. Swarna alleged that cases were being registered against Mr. Gandhi for raising issues including a caste census and women’s reservation, and said the party would continue its fight against such actions.

District Mahila Congress presidents, State office-bearers and party workers participated in the protest.

World.title: Lokayukta court sentences former sub-tahsildar to 4 years for taking bribe
World.content:
The 1st Additional District and Sessions and Special Court in Shivamogga on Tuesday sentenced a former sub-tahsildar to four years in prison and imposed a fine of ₹40,000 for accepting a bribe from a farmer seeking disability pension for his father.

The accused, Pushpalatha, then sub-tahsildar at the Nadakacheri in Kallihal, Holehonnur hobli, Bhadravati taluk, was convicted in a Lokayukta trap case registered in 2017.

According to the Karnataka Lokayukta, complainant Gireesh, 33, farmer from D.B. Halli in Bhadravati taluk, had approached Pushpalatha after obtaining a medical certificate stating that his father Parameshwarappa was speech and hearing impaired. He sought assistance in obtaining disability pension for his father.

The official allegedly demanded ₹10,000 as bribe for processing the pension. On September 21, 2017, the Lokayukta officials trapped Pushpalatha while she was allegedly accepting ₹5,000 from Gireesh at the Bhadravati taluk office.

Police Inspector J.S. Thippeswamy, who investigated the case, subsequently filed a chargesheet against the accused before the court.

After hearing the case, the court on September 1, 2026, found Pushpalatha guilty and sentenced her to four years’ imprisonment and ₹40,000 fine. Special Public Prosecutor Sundar Raj represented the government in the case.

World.title: Telangana MHSRB releases second provisional merit list for MPHA posts
World.content:
The Telangana Medical and Health Services Recruitment Board (MHSRB) on Tuesday released the second provisional list for the recruitment to the post of Multi Purpose Health Assistant (Female). The board also announced the schedule for certificate verification.

Certificate verification of shortlisted candidates will be conducted from September 16 to September 26, at the Indian Institute of Health and Family Welfare, Vengalrao Nagar, Hyderabad. September 28 has been kept as reserve day for candidates who are unable to attend the verification on the date allotted to them.

Candidates have been asked to bring their original certificates and documents along with two sets of photocopies for verification. These include the online application form, Aadhaar card, date-of-birth certificate, community certificate, qualifying examination certificate and the relevant Multi Purpose Health Worker (Female) training certificate.

After completion of certificate verification, the final merit list and selection list will be released in due course. The recruitment process will also remain subject to the final outcome of writ petitions pending before the Telangana High Court, the board said.

World.title: Varapuzha Archdiocese begins decade-long celebrations ahead of 150th anniversary
World.content:
The Varapuzha Archdiocese on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) commenced the celebrations into the run-up to the sesquicentennial of its elevation as an archdiocese which will fall in 2036.

Archbishop Joseph Kalathiparambil hoisted the jubilee flag marking the beginning of the 10-year-long celebrations at St. Francis Assisi Cathedral on the occasion of the 140th anniversary of the archdiocese. The flag was also hoisted at all parish churches under the archdiocese.

The Archbishop led the Holy Mass at the cathedral in connection with the 140th anniversary celebrations.

The Vicariate of Verapoly was raised to the status of an Archdiocese on September 1, 1886, through an Apostolic Letter issued by Pope Leo XIII, according to a release from the church.

World.title: 5 security personnel among 6 martyred in Balochistan Customs House attack, 21 terrorists killed across province: ISPR
World.content:
Five security personnel, including two officers, and a Customs official were martyred during a “coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House” on the night of August 31-September 1 in Balochistan, the military’s media wing said.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that on the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, during multiple incidents in Nokcha, Chagai District, and Ziarat Cross, Pishin District, twenty-one terrorists belonging to Indian-sponsored proxies of Fitna al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij were sent to hell due to effective responses by the Security Forces.

The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

“During the night of Aug 31-Sep 1, terrorists belonging to Fitna al- Khawarij launched a coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House.

“Security forces responded effectively and, after an intense fire exchange, killed 10 terrorists,” ISPR added.

Moreover, fleeing terrorists were also engaged by the security forces, inflicting further casualties, the ISPR said.

“During the exchange of fire, six brave sons of the soil, including two officers and a government official from the Customs Department, made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty and embraced shahadat,” it said.

The attack on the Customs House was a “manifestation of the terror-crime nexus, orchestrated to prevent Customs officials from performing their lawful duties and thereby facilitate the continuation of criminal activities in the area”, the ISPR stated.

It added that the sanitisation operations were continuing in the surrounding areas to eliminate any remaining terrorists and ensure the safety and security of the local population as well as the vital national highways.

Separately, on 31 August, terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan attempted to disrupt the peaceful movement of commuters along N-40 Quetta–Taftan Highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion, ISPR said.
