World.title: Russia criticizes Japan-U.S.-Australia military drills featuring Typhon missile system
World.content:
Russia on Tuesday slammed large-scale joint U.S.-Japan-Australia military exercises scheduled for later this month, delivering a formal protest to the Japanese Embassy in Moscow about the deployment of U.S. Typhon missile launchers for the drills.

The Orient Shield exercises will run ​from Sept. 8-24 across Japan — including in Hokkaido — and will see the deployment of the powerful Typhon midrange missile system for the first time, according to the Defense Ministry in Tokyo. The advanced weapon can fire Tomahawk cruise missiles as far as 1,600 kilometers — effectively putting parts of Russia and China within striking distance.

“The Japanese Embassy was clearly informed that the deployment of this type of weapon on Japanese territory, including under the pretext of military exercises, is absolutely unacceptable, as it poses a threat to Russia’s security,” Russia’s RIA news agency quoted Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova.

World.title: USJ to expand theme park site for first time
World.content:
USJ, the operator of Universal Studios Japan, is set to expand the site of the movie theme park in Osaka for the first time since its 2001 opening.

The Osaka Municipal Government said Tuesday that it will lease a land plot adjacent to the northern side of the theme park to the company. A lease contract is expected to be concluded in 2028.

By building new attractions on the site, the company hopes to attract more visitors to the popular theme park.

The site of about 30,000 square meters, currently leased to Nippon Steel, is scheduled to be returned in June next year, according to the city.

USJ approached the city in April this year about a lease of the land and aims to finalize the contract while conducting a survey on possible soil contamination at the site.

“This is a very welcome proposal for us because we aim to revitalize the entire Osaka Bay area,” Osaka Mayor Hideyuki Yokoyama said at a news conference Tuesday.

The theme park currently stands on a site of about 540,000 square meters. It had about 16 million visitors in fiscal 2024.

The company said that it “supports the city’s tourism and economic development goals and has entered into preliminary discussions” with the municipal government to “explore the potential long-term lease of the site.”

World.title: Ex-prosecutor who accused boss of rape urges reform
World.content:
An ex-prosecutor who publicly accused her boss of rape said on Tuesday that her former office needs reform, adding that victims’ allegations are not properly investigated.

Very few women in Japan speak out about sexual assault, but the prosecutor, who uses the pseudonym Hikari, in 2024 accused Osaka’s then-top prosecutor of raping her six years earlier.

Kentaro Kitagawa, who retired after serving as head of the Osaka District Public Prosecutor’s Office, was arrested and admitted the assault but later withdrew his statement, saying the sex was consensual.

World.title: In Japan’s mountains, a different way to manage bears
World.content:
As a sensor sounded, scientist Akiko Takii hurried to a bear trap deep in the forests of Nagano Prefecture, where rising nationwide attacks have brought fear and resulted in the culling of thousands of the animals.

“It’s a small bear, I think, about a year-and-a-half old,” Takii said as she peered at the 15-kilogram (33-pound) Asiatic black bear thrashing in the cage. “It must have just parted from mum.”

Its mother wasn’t around, and Takii took blood and fur samples after her co-researcher tranquilized the young female. The animal was too small to be tagged with a GPS tracker, so she was released.

World.title: Japan arrests man in Iwate twice for hamster massacres
World.content:
Police said Tuesday they had arrested a man over the killing of 30 hamsters at a hotel, weeks after he was detained for stomping to death 20 others.

The 36-year-old high school staffer in Iwate Prefecture teamed up with two different women at love hotels, where police said he massacred hamsters in a violation of animal protection laws.

The two women have also been arrested, said Hiroyuki Nasu, a senior police official in the city of Miyako, Iwate.

The main suspect’s arrest on Monday was for his “gratuitous killings” in late March of about 30 hamsters, carried out in collusion with a 20-year-old woman, Nasu said.

The suspect’s smartphone confiscated by police contained videos filming the killings, as well as text messages with the woman that showed them plotting the act.

“Where are we going to kill the hamsters and have fun?” Nasu quoted one of the exchanged messages as saying.

The suspect was first detained in July for the separate killing in February of around 20 hamsters with a 19-year-old woman.

Police will continue to investigate the suspect and examine whether he may have committed other similar acts, the police official said.

World.title: Over 1 in 3 young Japanese not interested in tying the knot, survey finds
World.content:
More than 1 in 3 young people in Japan have no intention of getting married, according to preliminary results of a large-scale survey released this week by the Children and Families Agency.

The agency surveyed more than 100,000 people between the ages of 15 and 39, receiving around 68,000 responses between late May and early August. However, the figures released as of Monday track only the 43,529 responses given until July 23. The survey covered personal topics such as mental health, childhood experiences, and life concerns.

On marriage, 35.1% said they had “no intention” of getting married, while 27.4% said they wanted to get married within the next five years, and an additional 37.5% said they wanted to do so “eventually.”

Among those with no intention to marry, 53.1% answered that it was because they didn’t want to. When asked about what they prioritize over marriage, nearly 60% said free time and hobbies.

Economic factors were also cited as a reason not to marry, with 23.5% answering that uncertainty over income to support a marriage was a hurdle and 34.9% saying that they prioritize a stable income and employment over marriage.

Similar concerns were reflected among all respondents of the marriage question. The largest overall hurdle to marriage was income worries at 40%, with income security and building savings among respondents’ top priorities.

The low interest in marriage could have a negative impact on the Japanese population, which has been declining for almost two decades.

The latest figures on those who have no plans to marry are lower than similar polling conducted last year by the agency.

According to the August 2025 poll of 10,000 single people between the ages of 16 and 49, 46.5% of respondents said they had no intention of getting married, an increase of over 4 percentage points from when the same question was asked in 2023.

Although those in their 40s had the highest proportion of that answer in the 2025 survey, the figure was still well over 40% for people in their 30s and below.

World.title: Foreign Ministry sets up Cyber Security Policy Division to combat cyberattacks
World.content:
The Foreign Ministry on Tuesday established the Cyber Security Policy Division within its Foreign Policy Bureau in response to the growing risk of cyberattacks driven by advances in artificial intelligence.

The division will be responsible for further strengthening coordination with allied and like-minded countries, as well as other partners, while also contributing to international rule-making, the ministry said.

The unit was first created in 2016 under the bureau but was later merged into the National Security Policy Division as part of an organizational reform.

Amid increasing cyber threats, however, the ministry determined that a dedicated division is necessary.

About 10 to 20 staff personnel at the National Security Policy Division concurrently serve as members of the newly launched division, working to promote Japan’s cyber diplomacy, such as offering capacity-building support to developing countries.

World.title: Japan’s top court to test use of AI in civil trials
World.content:
The Supreme Court plans to examine in the next fiscal year whether generative artificial intelligence (AI) can be used in civil trials.

On Monday, the top court announced its budget request for fiscal 2027, which included some ¥60 million for expenses related to the use of AI. This is the court’s first budget request including such expenses.

According to the Supreme Court, records of settled lawsuits will be used in a demonstration test on AI use. Judges and other officials will input documents into an AI system to create, for example, rough drafts of record summaries and lists of points of contention.

The court will also develop a system to prevent the leakage of personal information about parties to lawsuits and companies’ trade secrets.

In January and February this year, a research group of six midcareer judges from the Tokyo and Osaka district courts conducted a test based on mock trial records.

Through the test, the group found that, while AI could be helpful in creating summaries and organizing points of contention, it could also reinforce judges’ biases by omitting important facts and points of contention and providing plausible yet incorrect answers. The group concluded that AI should be positioned as an assistant to judges.

As prolonged civil trials have become a problem in recent years, Masayuki Nagata, a senior official at the Supreme Court’s digital policy planning office, said, “Using AI is expected to streamline and shorten trials further.”

“We hope to present the results of the demonstration test within the next fiscal year,” Nagata added.

The Supreme Court’s budget request also included about ¥38.7 billion for expenses related to the digitalization of trial procedures, including for criminal and domestic cases.

World.title: Power failure halts trams running between Hong Kong’s Wan Chai and Admiralty
World.content:
Tram services between Wan Chai and Admiralty in Hong Kong were suspended Tuesday night due to a power failure, the second such incident in two days.

The Transport Department issued a special traffic bulletin at 9.37pm, saying it had been notified by Hong Kong Tramways that eastbound and westbound services between Admiralty MTR station and Tonnochy Road were suspended because of an electricity fault.

It marked the second consecutive day of tram disruptions.

On Monday night, services on the westbound line between North Point terminus and Tin Lok Lane stopped at about 6pm after a power failure. The suspension lasted until 11.30pm.

World.title: ‘Worst yet to come’ as Hong Kong schools cut record 126 Primary One classes
World.content:
Hong Kong public schools have slashed a record 126 Primary One classes for the 2026-27 academic year amid a shrinking student population, prompting a sector leader to warn that the “worst is yet to come”.

According to the latest Primary School Profiles, the total number of Primary One classes across public schools dropped from 1,558 in 2025-26 to 1,432 in 2026-27, representing a net decrease of 8 per cent.

The guide covers more than 500 local primary institutions and is compiled by the Committee on Home-School Co-operation to help parents select schools for their children.

The contraction hit Kwai Tsing the hardest, where nearly half the district’s 31 primary schools – 14 campuses – were forced to trim their Primary One intake. Tuen Mun and Eastern districts followed, each losing 13 classes.

The latest profiles of more than 500 primary institutions serve as reference materials for parents selecting schools for their children.

World.title: Suspected cyberattack puts data of 33,054 customers using group-buying app at risk
World.content:
The private data of about 33,000 customers of TVB-owned group-buying platform Neigbuy has been compromised in a suspected cyberattack, with police saying they have received six reports of scammers posing as staff.

The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data confirmed on Tuesday that it had received a data breach notification from the company on Sunday, and had initiated a formal investigation.

The platform, founded in 2018 and majority-owned by free-to-air television broadcaster TVB, offers limited-time deals on groceries, fresh produce, household goods and other products.

The privacy watchdog said that signs of a suspected cyberattack, involving unauthorised data access, were first detected on August 24.

The security incident had affected 33,054 customers, with the potentially compromised information including their names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and online shopping order histories, it said.

The office advised Neigbuy customers to change their account passwords and enable multi-factor authentication. They should also remain vigilant if contacted by unknown or suspicious parties, it urged.

World.title: Welfare groups seek clarity on breed classification amid third fighting dog case
World.content:
A Hong Kong man has surrendered his dog after authorities detained it and classified it as a fighting breed – the third known case in a week following a spate of attacks in the city.

The case came as animal welfare groups called for clarity on the government’s breed-classification procedures and a transparent appeal mechanism. They warned that heightened anxiety could lead to more pet abandonment and unfair stereotyping of certain breeds.

Jacqueline Cheung, founder of the non-profit Love Adopt Animal Society, told the South China Morning Post on Tuesday that she took ownership of seven-year-old Bobo the previous day after the animal’s owner relinquished her at the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD).

The original owner had taken his licensed pet to the department for vaccination last Wednesday but was later told that the dog was suspected of being a fighting breed. The animal was held until Monday and subsequently classified as a pit bull terrier crossbreed.

The owner reportedly has brain cancer and was unable to cope with the pressure of caring for Bobo. He sought help from volunteers, who eventually put him in touch with Cheung.

According to Cheung, a former veterinary nurse, Bobo was well behaved but had severe eye inflammation and was covered in ticks when she collected her from the department. The dog was also diagnosed with heartworm, which typically takes at least six months to develop after a dog is bitten by an infected mosquito.

World.title: Hong Kong tycoon empires and foundations pledge 30m yuan for flood relief
World.content:
Hong Kong tycoon Li Ka-shing and his business empire, along with Henderson Land Development and the Lee Shau Kee Foundation, have pledged 15 million yuan (US$2.2 million) each to support relief efforts for victims of the deadly flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border.

Nina Wang Charitable Management also pledged HK$10 million (US$1.27 million) to support relief efforts.

CK Asset Holdings, CK Hutchison Holdings and the Li Ka Shing Foundation, as well as Henderson Land and the Lee Shau Kee Foundation, expressed their condolences to victims of the disaster.

The donations were made through the central government's liaison office’s disaster relief account.

Last Wednesday, a massive wall of mud and rock collapsed into a river along the Himalayan border between Nepal and Tibet, triggering catastrophic flooding.

According to Nepalese police, 1,058 bodies had been recovered as of 2pm on Tuesday, with 4,606 people still missing.

Chinese authorities have confirmed 16 deaths and 546 people missing, taking the death toll on both sides of the border to 1,074.

World.title: Subdivided-flat registration rate at 42.5% as ‘early bird’ phase deadline passes
World.content:
Property-ownership complications and low public awareness have slowed landlords’ registration of Hong Kong subdivided flats under new housing regulations, industry observers have said, after the government received only 42.5 per cent of the applications expected in the first phase.

Monday marked the deadline for the initial six-month “early bird” registration phase under the Basic Housing Unit Ordinance. Landlords who applied during this period were eligible for a waiver of HK$3,000 (US$382) in certification fees per subdivided flat for each of the first three years.

The legislation came into force in March to phase out substandard subdivided flats. The government estimates that about 80,000 flats across the city could be accredited, but only about 34,000 units were registered during the first six months.

Scott Leung Man-kwong, deputy chairman of the Legislative Council’s housing panel, described the 42.5 per cent application rate as acceptable but said the HK$3,000 discount was not a significant incentive for landlords to apply early.

“For inherited properties, sometimes the verification of legal ownership could delay the application,” he told a radio show on Tuesday.

“We’ve seen cases where a son inherited a flat from his father that is already subdivided. The tenants continued to pay rent and they did not process the legal transfer of the property. But now, with the application for basic housing units, they will have to do so.”

World.title: Hong Kong school starts academic year without replacing head fired for swearing
World.content:
A Hong Kong secondary school has begun the new academic year without a principal while authorities vet a replacement for the former head, who was fired for swearing at security guards during a Singapore study trip.

Former lawmaker Edmund Wong Chun-sek, who is also a manager of San Wui Commercial Society Secondary School, said on Tuesday that the Education Bureau was currently conducting background checks on the candidate.

The school, located in Tuen Mun, was under the temporary leadership of its deputy head for now, he added.

“We have completed the recruitment procedures and decided on one candidate, but the Education Bureau is still vetting the appointment,” Wong said. “Of course, the sooner we welcome the new principal, the better.”

Wong said the wider process could take time since the bureau had taken three months to vet the previous incumbent.

But he stressed that the school would operate as normal, adding that teachers and the institution’s governance team were on the same page.

In response to the South China Morning Post’s inquiry, the bureau said on Tuesday that it had reminded the school to strictly follow the relevant procedures in its application and take appropriate administrative measures to ensure that its operations were not disrupted and that students’ wellbeing was safeguarded.

World.title: Former economic crime chief to head discipline team at Hong Kong, Macau office
World.content:
A veteran mainland Chinese economic crime investigator and former police official has been appointed to lead the discipline inspection and supervision group at Beijing’s top office overseeing Hong Kong affairs.

Hua Liebing, a former director of the Ministry of Public Security’s economic crime investigation bureau, fills the vacancy at the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office (HKMAO) left by Geng Changyou, who stepped down last year to become secretary of Hebei province’s Commission for Discipline Inspection.

The new appointment was revealed on Tuesday when the office updated its organisation chart on its website.

It marked another change in the office’s top ranks following the selection of Zhang Dongmei, a former vice-president of the All-China Women’s Federation, as a deputy director in March.

Hua’s appointment brings the HKMAO’s senior leadership to seven members. They include Xia Baolong, who has led the office since 2020, and deputy director Zhou Ji, who also serves as the director of Beijing’s liaison office in Hong Kong.

The appointment came a day after a meeting of the HKMAO’s leading group for Communist Party building, which was also attended by members of the discipline inspection and supervision group.

World.title: Education, health fees among key concerns
World.content:
China to legislate on preschool education

China will push for legislation on preschool education to provide a legal guarantee for the operation and management of such institutions, Vice-minister of Education Tian Xuejun said on Nov 30.

Tian made the remarks at a news conference organized by the State Council Information Office regarding a child abuse case at RYB Education New World Kindergarten in Beijing that received widespread attention in November. He said the Ministry of Education was already doing research on the legislation.

"The ministry will also complete the requirements on qualifications of teachers engaged in preschool education and is considering formulating a code of ethics for them," Tian said.

He also said a plan is on the way to step up supervision of kindergartens and solve the problem of insufficient resources for preschool education. Tian said the case exposed the conflict between public demand for preschool enrollment and insufficient development of preschool education.

"It also showed that some local authorities and kindergartens still have problems of unsound management and failure to implement or fully implement regulations," he said.

Rural health fee increase explained in detail

The National Health and Family Planning Commission recently responded to public concern of newly increased fees for a new rural cooperative medical system.

Fees charged in the new rural cooperative medical system have recently been raised from 30 yuan ($5.5) to 180 yuan.

The NHFPC explained that while fees for individuals have been raised, government financial subsidies to individuals have also been raised accordingly in recent years from the previous 20 yuan per person to 450 per person. At the same time, the government has a comprehensive medical assistance system for those unable to afford such fees. Also, the reimbursement proportion for hospitalization costs for those in the new rural cooperative medical system has also been raised from 35 percent to 75 percent.

Anti-espionage law will help national security

The State Council issued a circular on China's anti-espionage law on Wednesday with detailed rules for implementing the law.

The circular explains several terms in the law, including overseas institutions and organizations, individuals, spy organizations, spy organization agents and hostile organizations. It was made clear that national security departments under the State Council will identify unacceptable behavior.

According to the circular, providing funds, venues and materials to spy organizations and individuals will be identified as helping them.

Conducting espionage activities in the territory, accepting overseas funds to endanger national security or connect them for spying activities will also be deemed as collusion.

Staff members at national safety departments are authorized to arrest and hunt criminal suspects, and their anti-espionage activities will not be interrupted by any other illegal actions.

It said that Chinese people and organizations retain the right and privilege to secure national safety, and their contributions such as providing clues about spying activities, collaborating with national security departments and fighting espionage activities will also be rewarded.

World.title: International group praises green revival
World.content:
High-level advisory panel pitches 15-year pollution fight, but holds China up as model

A high-level international advisory body applauded China's efforts to improve the environment and suggested a 15-year strategy against pollution in a draft recommendation report on Monday.

China has made building an ecological civilization an important goal and has taken comprehensive measures to improve the environment. This has resulted in positive results, including improved air quality, Vice-Premier Zhang Gaoli said when chairing the annual meeting of the China Council for International Cooperation on Environment and Development, a high-level international advisory body.

Like Zhang, Erik Solheim, executive director of the United Nations Environment Programme, said he was impressed by China's tremendous achievements regarding its environment in recent years, in particular curbing much of the smog problem.

"China is capable of solving the environment problems themselves," said Solheim, the council's vice-chairman, adding the best practices taken by China could provide guidance to other areas facing similar issues.

His praise of China's approaches to move toward being an ecological civilization won wide support from other members of the environmental council, which includes senior officials and experts from home and abroad.

The council's draft recommendation presents highlights of the war against pollution in air, water and soil, and suggests the creation of a 15-year strategy that will be "focused on cost-effectiveness, synergies and ways to build public confidence about eventual results".

Ideally, the integrated rollout should be ready before 2020, to be in line with the 2035 pivot point, when China expects to be a "basic modern country", the draft said.

Solheim said he is confident that China can reach the 2035 goal to build a "beautiful China", considering the determined and effective efforts adopted in recent years.

Along with the longer-term strategy to curb pollution, council members suggested creating conditions for fair competition and incentives for green industries.

Based on the input from Monday's meeting, the advisers and their support teams will modify their proposal and provide a final version to the State Council through the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

zhengjinran@chinadaily.com.cn

World.title: Beijing, Moscow drill for potential missile warfare
World.content:
China and Russia kicked off their second joint computer-assisted anti-missile drill on Monday, a move experts said could deter potential missile threats amid rising tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

The drill began on Monday in Beijing and is expected to conclude on Saturday, China's Defense Ministry said on its website on Monday. "This is a practical measure in fulfilling the important consensus reached by both countries' leaders on deepening Sino-Russian antimissile cooperation," it said.

"It will strengthen Sino-Russian mutual strategic trust, improve anti-missile cooperation between the two militaries and has great significance in jointly dealing with regional ballistic and cruise missile threats," the ministry said.

The exercise does not target any third party, it said. "China and Russia oppose the development of global anti-missile systems. The two militaries will increase practical cooperation in anti-missile defense, and jointly safeguard Chinese and Russian security interests and regional strategic balance."

The goal of the exercise is to "jointly train for anti-missile combat planning and preparation, launch command and firing coordination," Senior Colonel Wu Qian, the Defense Ministry spokesman, said in a news briefing in November.

Tension on the Korean Peninsula has been mounting since the Democratic People's Republic of Korea launched its Hwasong-15 intercontinental ballistic missile in November. DPRK media reported the missile could carry nuclear warheads and reach the continental United States.

Su Hao, a professor at the China Foreign Affairs Academy, said that it is crucial for China and Russia to bolster strategic trust and cooperate in anti-missile defense to protect their nations from potential threats.

zhangzhihao@chinadaily.com.cn

World.title: Memorial Day a time to 'remember', 'inspire'
World.content:
A memorial service to mark the 80th anniversary of the Nanjing Massacre committed during the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression (1931-45) brought together hundreds of activists and members of the Chinese and other Asian communities on Sunday in San Francisco.

The memorial, organized by the Rape of Nanking Redress Coalition, the Committee to Promote Reunification of China, the Alliance for Preserving the Truth of Sino-Japanese War and Comfort Women Justice Coalition, has been held annually for the past 20 years with the aim of exposing the Japanese Imperial Army's war crimes and encouraging people to understand and never forget the dark chapter of history.

"The Japanese army blatantly violated international conventions and committed the extremely cruel atrocity in Nanjing, where 300,000 Chinese were murdered and one-third of the buildings were destroyed," Zha Liyou, acting Chinese consul general in San Francisco, said at the service.

Japanese troops captured Nanjing, which was China's capital at the time, on Dec 13, 1937. It then began a slaughter that lasted more than 40 days. Tens of thousands of women were raped.

"Our stories are linked. The fate of over 400,000 women sexually enslaved by the Japanese Imperial Army during World War II is part and parcel of what happened during the Nanjing Massacre," said Judith Mirkinson, president of the Comfort Women Justice Coalition.

She said the 20th century has been called the most violent century in the history of the world, and that one way to ensure peace in the 21st century is through truth and reconciliation.

"Reconciliation does not come without truth. So the Japanese government must acknowledge their crimes," she said.

"They must give justice to those few people who still survive from the Nanjing Massacre and to the memory of what happened there," she said.

From the time that Japan invaded Northeast China in September 1931, followed by a full-scale invasion that started on July 7, 1937, around 35 million Chinese soldiers and civilians were killed or injured during the occupation, which continued until 1945.

To honor the victims and the survivors and to pursue justice and an enduring peace, the Chinese community worldwide joined hands this year to commemorate this historic event, which was designated by the Chinese government as National Memorial Day for Nanjing Massacre Victims.

"To remember the atrocities committed by the Japanese army during World War II does not mean to pass on the enmity but rather to remind people not to forget the history and inspire them to love peace," said Zha Liyou.

In 2015, the Nanjing Massacre was entered onto the UNESCO Memory of the World Register, a compendium aimed at preserving documented heritage of universal value.

liazhu@chinadailyusa.com

World.title: More military technologies targeted for civilian sector to boost economy
World.content:
Greater integration will spur innovation and cultivate new engines of growth

China will strengthen innovation by developing high-tech industries with military technologies to boost military-civil integration, a move that aims to cultivate new growth drivers and boost the economy, said a recent State Council guideline.

This was one of the seven key tasks set by the guideline on deepening the military-civil integration in the defense technology industry, which was released by the State Council, China's Cabinet, on Monday last week.

The guideline targets sharing technological innovation bases and facilities between military and civilian sectors while more efforts will be made to apply military technologies to non-military areas.

The military integration will also focus on key areas such as space, cyberspace and maritime sciences, while private capital is encouraged to enter military industries, the document said.

The guideline was the latest move by the central government to promote the military-civil integration to widen military contract orders to civilian sectors and apply high-end military technologies for civilian purposes as part of the supply-side structural reform.

In June, the General Office of the State Council released a guideline on civil aviation development to open airspace less than 3,000 meters in altitude and other industries such as cybersecurity and satellite navigation.

Shi Haiming, an associate professor at the National University of Defense Technology, said the guideline brings benefits for both private and military enterprises while pre-entry approvals will be changed into post-entry reviews to streamline administration, except those linking strategic weapons.

Meanwhile, Shi said the guideline lowers the access threshold for enterprises to enter the field of weaponry equipment and will make the process more transparent.

The document also will further reduce institutional costs for private enterprise by building better platforms to promote military-civil integration, he said.

In fact, many developed economies are highly reliant on military-civil integration.

For example, the United States' airplane maker Boeing sells China civil aviation aircraft worth billions of dollars each year and is known for its high-end military aircraft. Many Japanese multinational companies such as Toshiba and Mitsubishi have a department to take military orders.

The integration is a worldwide trend to fully improve the national defense capability, said Jiang Luming, a professor at the National Defense University of the People's Liberation Army.

In countries such as the US, the United Kingdom and Germany, less than 15 percent of military technologies are solely for military purposes and more than 80 percent are used for civilian purposes, Jiang said.

Jiang said in October last year that China has about 290,000 national defense intellectual property rights not being used due to the previously separated military and civil industries.

For example, breakthrough technologies such as engines and aluminum alloy materials can help ease production overcapacity and transform China's economy, he said. These new technologies can essentially boost economic growth and national defense, Jiang said.

The military industry has the priority to apply cutting-edge technologies and also make breakthrough innovations, Lu Guangshan, chairman of the Avionics System Co under the Aviation Industry Corporation of China, was quoted by Shanghai Securities News as saying.

"For example, virtual reality headsets were first used in helmets for fighter jets and my company has developed six civilian industries such as virtual reality, drones, robotics and smart wearing," Lu said.

Military companies are encouraged to work with local governments to promote their advantageous expertise and develop a large number of new high-tech industries, Long Hongshan, chief engineer at the State Administration of Science, Technology and Industry for National Defense, told a news conference last week.

These new industries will play a vital role in promoting local economic growth and creating new employment opportunities, Long said.

Currently, 30 percent of products made by China's military companies are for military purposes and the other 70 percent for civilian purposes, he said.

In the future, high-tech industries will cover half of the military-related economy, Long added.

World.title: Dangerous stunts get thumbs-down from video platforms
World.content:
Multiple social media and video streaming platforms will limit who can view videos that depict dangerous stunts - and may even prohibit such material - in an effort to discourage imitators.

In November, daredevil stunt climber Wu Yongning fell to his death while scaling a skyscraper in Changsha, Hunan province. Wu, 26, had more than 1.3 million followers on social media who regularly devoured his breathtaking videos and photos. He climbed with no protective gear.

Last month, Wu's account on Sina Weibo stopped updating, leading followers to worry about his well-being.

On Friday, Wu's girlfriend confirmed on social media that the "rooftop daredevil" had fallen and died.

"Today is Dec 8. It makes me think of Nov 8, the day that you left us, left this world," she wrote.

Wu's family also confirmed his death to Jiefang Daily, a newspaper in Shanghai.

Meipai, Kuaishou, Xiaohuoshan and other video platforms on which Wu posted content, expressed their condolences, according to ThePaper.cn. Platform representatives told the news outlet that China currently has no law regulating extreme stunt videos, but each platform will update its content policy to discourage imitators.

Kuaishou said Wu's account had been restricted - meaning that only the uploader can see it - in September because of its depictions of dangerous acts.

Xiaohuoshan said it will ban video livestreams of dangerous stunts because live interactions between the performer and the audience could be a distraction and lead to catastrophic results.

The platform also said it will respect the desires of Wu's family in dealing with the videos.

All of Wu's stunt videos on the three platforms had been restricted or taken down as of Monday. A cellphone video of Wu performing his last stunt and falling to his death on Nov 8, has also been taken down.

Wu was part of an informal community of young thrill-seekers around the world who engage in "roof-topping" - climbing to the top or to high ledges of buildings, often without a permit or protective gear, to take stomach-churning pictures and videos. The activity is generally illegal.

In January, an 18-year-old identified as Alexander Sh, fell to his death from Europe's second-tallest building - the 350-meter OKO Tower in Moscow. He was trying to take a selfie when he slipped and fell, Russian media reported.

zhangzhihao@chinadaily.com.cn

World.title: Taiwan's New Party vows to help improve relations
World.content:
Delegation to Beijing reaffirms support for one-China, rejection of agitators

Top political adviser Yu Zhengsheng met with a Taiwan delegation representing the island's New Party in Beijing on Monday to discuss the peaceful development of cross-Straits relations and how to achieve the "great rejuvenation" of the Chinese nation.

Yu praised the New Party's unbroken stance upholding the 1992 Consensus, which embodies the one-China principle, since the party's establishment, as well as its peaceful approach to relations.

The 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, which was held in October, further clarified the guidelines and policies addressing Taiwan, Yu said.

In his opening address to delegates during the congress, Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Central Committee of the CPC, called the one-China principle the political foundation of cross-Straits relations, and said that attempts to move toward "Taiwan independence" in any form will be defeated.

Taiwan will share development opportunities on the Chinese mainland, and its residents will enjoy the same treatment as mainland people as they pursue studies, start businesses, seek jobs or come to live on the mainland, Xi said in the address.

Yok Mu-ming, chairman of the New Party and head of the Taiwan delegation, said the party has firmly upheld the one-China principle and promoted peace.

The delegation also met on Monday with Zhang Zhijun, head of the State Council's Taiwan Affairs Office.

Zhang and Yok agreed that the one-China principle must be upheld going forward, expressed firm opposition to separatist activities and vowed to make efforts toward peaceful relations.

Both sides agreed to establish and improve mechanisms of communication, share opinions on major issues in the relationship and promote exchanges and communication in all fields - especially between youth. They further agreed to create a constructive and convenient environment for the development of Taiwan youth on the mainland.

Zhang said cross-Straits relations have faced challenges because the island's Democratic Progressive Party has refused to clearly express support for the one-China principle, which led to the mainland suspending official communications with the island.

He said that a "Taiwan independence" force had recently stirred up the island, proposing the removal of Chinese mainland elements in a variety of fields.

"Its aim is to cut the historical ties between Taiwan and the mainland, reduce public awareness that Taiwan people are part of the Chinese nation and limit many cultural influences on the island," he said.

Some people advocating "Taiwan independence" have pushed for amending the law, and have proposed changing the island's constitution. "This shows that separatist activities and the group supporting 'independence' pose the most serious threat to the peaceful development of cross-Straits relations," Zhang said.

He warned that people from both sides should be vigilant and firmly oppose such activities.

luowangshu@chinadaily.com.cn

World.title: Former Chongqing political official facing corruption investigation
World.content:
Sun Zhengcai, the former secretary of Chongqing Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China, has been placed under investigation on suspicion of accepting bribes, according to the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Monday.

According to the procuratorate, Sun has been placed under "coercive measures", which may include summons by force, bail, residential surveillance, detention and arrest.

The investigation is underway, the procuratorate said in a statement released on Monday.

In July, the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection launched an investigation into Sun for "serious violations of Party discipline".

The CCDI said in a news release that Sun betrayed Party principles and ignored the Party code of conduct and rules.

He was found to have seriously violated the CPC's eight-point code on frugality and maintaining close ties with the masses, seeking pomp, ostentation and privileges, according to the CCDI.

The CCDI said he was guilty of nepotism and seeking benefits in selection of officials. He was found by the CCDI to have leaked confidential Party information and seriously breached Party rules on integrity.

Moreover, he abused power and used his job to gain benefits for others, then accepted their huge bribes in return, either paid in cash or properties, the CCDI said. He was found to seek substantial benefits for his relatives' businesses and accepted valuable gifts, the CCDI said.

The anti-graft inspectors also accused Sun of bureaucracy and sloth in work and degradation and power-for-sex trades, according to the CCDI.

Sun totally deviated from the Party spirit and political requirements of senior officials, the CCDI said in the statement, adding that his misconduct betrayed the trust of the CPC Central Committee and the public, inflicting huge harm to the Party and the country with "extremely bad" social influences.

The CCDI transferred the criminal evidence involving his case to judicial authorities for further investigation.

In September, the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee expelled Sun from the Party and dismissed him from public office.

China Daily - Xinhua

World.title: Months before ICC trial, Duterte wants prosecution to refile cases vs him
World.content:
Former president Rodrigo Duterte wants the prosecution to refile a document that 'frames the charges in terms of counts with a defined scope, being crimes under the ICC Statute'

MANILA, Philippines – Just a few months before his scheduled historic trial, former president Rodrigo Duterte asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III to order the prosecution to refile the cases against him.

“The [defense] accordingly requests the Trial Chamber to order the prosecution to re-file a document before the Pre-Trial Chamber that frames the charges in terms of counts with a defined scope, being crimes under the ICC Statute, and with an exhaustive list of underpinning acts, which represent the entirety of the charges against the accused,” said the Duterte camp’s motion dated August 31.

In the motion, Duterte’s lead counsel Peter Haynes argued that the prosecution’s document containing the charges or DCC “is not fit for [its] purpose” and should be struck out.

This is the Duterte camp’s latest bid to challenge his case before the ICC after recent legal defeats.

Just last April, the ICC pre-trial chamber confirmed all three counts of Duterte’s crimes against humanity case, thus sending him to trial that will start in November.

Even on the issue of jurisdiction or whether the ICC was the right platform for the cases, Duterte did not score a win. The ICC Appeals Chamber junked his jurisdiction challenge and cleared the way for the trial.

The latest defeat was in May, when the pre-trial chamber denied Duterte’s request to appeal the ruling that confirmed his ICC cases.

In their August 31 motion, the Duterte camp said the prosecution’s DCC was framed around “illustrative non-exhaustive incidents.” They argued that the way the charges were framed violated Duterte’s right to be informed in detail of the nature, cause, and content of the charges against him under 67(1)(a) of the Rome Statute.

They said the only effective remedy to this is for the prosecution to refile the charges that properly inform Duterte about his case.

According to the defense, the prosecution’s decision to frame the charges that way makes it impossible for Duterte to know what case he has to meet at the upcoming trial.

“The Prosecution’s desire and intention to add further incidents is noteworthy as it plainly indicates that the Prosecution, at least, does not believe that it needs to prove all or most of the incidents. However, with a trial due to start in three months, the [defense] has no idea what is regarded as necessary proof of a ‘count’ on this DCC,” said the motion.

Duterte’s camp further argued that the prosecution’s charge document — which has broad topical headings rather than charged crimes — would allegedly be unacceptable in any criminal jurisdiction.

“The accused cannot even begin to make strategic decisions about how to approach this case, because he does not know what case he has to meet. The Duterte charges are a literal moving target; a non-exhaustive, illustrative list of events whose proof beyond reasonable doubt may or may not trigger liability for thousands of others, and whose evidential value remains entirely unclear,” the camp added. – Rappler.com

World.title: Michael Poa as witness: Good or bad idea for the prosecution?
World.content:
POA. Defense team spokesperson Atty. Michael Poa speaks to the media before the start of the fourth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 13, 2026.

Poa's wealth of legal experience is evident every time he does cross-examination for the defense. He is calm and collected, but extracts the information needed by the defense.

People know him as the spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte, apart from being part of the defense team for her impeachment trial.

But Michael Wesley Poa will take on a different role on Wednesday, September 2 — as the prosecution’s witness for the trial. The court is hearing the prosecution’s evidence of Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds of both the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Education.

This makes sense in a way, considering that Poa was chief of staff and spokesperson when Duterte was the DepEd chief. So, sure.

But is this a good idea for the prosecution?

Let’s not forget, Poa himself is no ordinary lawye; he’s a litigator. He knows how court proceedings work and understands the law. He knows how to argue before a court.

Poa’s wealth of legal experience is evident every time he does cross-examination for the defense. He is calm and collected, but manages to extract the information needed by the defense.

He even held his own when he faced House prosecutor Chel Diokno during oral arguments on the request to subpoena Duterte’s financial records last month.

Additionally, Poa would also be somehow freer in expressing his thoughts because he will not be acting as counsel, but as a witness.

Poa said he will answer whatever question is thrown at him, as long as it’s within his personal knowledge about DepEd’s confidential funds.

“If the questions cover or will be about DepEd and my participation [in] the audit observation memorandum (AOM), the reply to the AOM, I will answer them just like what I did in the House,” the defense spokesperson said on August 26.

Also, Poa really had familiarity with the issue. Under him, COA cleared DepEd over questions on the P75-million confidential funds.

So putting the defense lawyer on the witness stand might be a gamble for the prosecution. A challenge, definitely, but if the prosecutors are successful in getting the information they need from Poa, then it would be a plus to their case against Duterte.

Another challenge, of course, is Poa’s obvious inclination toward the defense.

To dispel any claim, any allegation of witness tampering, Poa stayed inside the holding area for the witnesses on Tuesday. This was according to defense deputy spokesperson Justin Nicol Gular.

Poa also did not sit beside defense lawyers inside the Senate plenary hall as would be usual; nor did he enter the defense lawyers’ holding area.

At this point, only Poa knows how his responses will go. For Gular, the public should just wait for the Wednesday trial.

“Let’s just wait for his testimony,” said the deputy spokesperson. – Rappler.com

World.title: What prompted Escudero’s reminder on digital devices ban at impeachment trial?
World.content:
Over the weekend, some netizens spotted what seemed like an earpiece purportedly worn by Office of Vice President (OVP) Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio as he testified at the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte earlier in the week.

The photos went viral, with some social media users speculating he was being coached, some even linking the appearance of OVP Chief of Staff Zuleika Lopez at the Senate with his testimonies.

But was Ortonio indeed being assisted in his testimony?

On Day 20 of the impeachment trial, presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero put the matter to rest as he debunked the social media posts. He said that upon verification, the viral photos were confirmed to be generated through artificial intelligence (AI).

“Hindi totoo ‘yung mga lumalabas na litrato na diumano mayroong earpiece si Mr. Ortonio, ‘yun po ay AI. What he had was an ear piercing in the front fold helix of his ear, not an earpiece,” said Escudero.

(The photos circulating online that Mr. Ortonio was purportedly wearing an earpiece was false. It was AI-generated. What he had was an ear piercing in the front fold helix of his ear, not an earpiece.)

Escudero said the controversy underscored the “need for a uniform safeguard,” prompting him to remind witnesses about the ban on the use of any hearing, listening, or electronic device during their testimonies. He also said they must testify “solely from his or her knowledge free from coaching or influence from counsel or any other person.”

He then directed the clerk of court to inform the witnesses about the ban, secure their electronic devices before taking the stand, and obtain their express consent vowing they would testify based only on their own will and without assistance from any device.

“Accordingly, no witness while testifying shall possess, have access to, or use any earpiece, headsets, cellphones, smart watch, smart glasses or any other similar device capable of transmitting or receiving information or communication,” Escudero said.

“Witnesses are also prohibited from receiving or attempting to receive any communications, suggestion, answer signal, message or prompt for any person whether inside or outside of this court, regardless of the means employed. The prohibition shall remain enforced during recesses and until the witness is formally discharged by the court,” he added.

Legitimate alias vs fake name

During the trial, Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III also made a manifestation, this time clarifying the difference between the use of alias and fictitious names.

Sotto cited Republic Act (RA) No. 6085 or the Anti-Alias Law, saying the use of pseudonyms is “permitted only for literary, cinema, television, radio, athletic, or other entertainment purposes, provided an actual living person is behind the name.”

“If there is a person behind the alias, then it is an alias. If there is no person behind the name, it is a fictitious name or a fake name,” he said.

Sotto, in raising the manifestation, rejected news reports that House private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia was not given the chance to answer Senator-judge Robin Padilla during his interjection over the use of aliases in the documents tied to the OVP’s confidential funds.

“We confirm that indeed, Atty. Mae was able to give an answer to the query of Senator-judge Padilla, also she was not able to give that much detail that the good senator-judge made,” Escudero said.

There were 16 senator-judges at the impeachment trial on Tuesday, September 1. Among those absent was Senator-judge Loren Legarda, who remains under extended medical leave until Wednesday, September 2. – Rappler.com

World.title: Haze and air quality index: Things to know
World.content:
AIR QUALITY. Haze blankets the Metro Manila sky on September 1, 2026, due to smoke from forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia. The Manila local government advises residents to take precautions and wear face masks when going outdoors.

Here's what you should know about air quality indexes and how they help identify the health risks brought by haze

MANILA, Philippines – It may look like a harmless fog blanketing the skies, but haze carries small particles in the air that can lead to serious health risks.

Here’s everything you need to know about haze, how to protect yourself from its effects, and how air quality indexes help in measuring risks.

What is haze?

Haze is smoke, dust, moisture, and vapor in the air that affects visibility. It originates from large-scale forest or land fires.

These fires create very fine particles with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers (PM2.5) or smaller that go into the air.

Unlike coarse particles that dissolve in the atmosphere within hours, fine particles can stay in the atmosphere for up to weeks and can travel for hundreds to thousands of kilometers.

These often grow in size as humidity increases and affect air quality by filling the atmosphere with high concentrations of fine particles.

This poses health risks, especially for those with respiratory diseases.

How does haze affect health?

Haze is a form of air pollution that leads to health risks when particles are inhaled.

According to the Department of Health, it could lead to the following:

difficulty breathing

coughing

chest pains

watery eyes or excessive tearing

itchy nose

worsening of respiratory disease

The health department advises people experiencing these symptoms to proceed to the nearest health center for treatment.

What are air quality indexes?

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) reviewed air quality indexes in compliance with the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.

In 2020, it formulated the PM2.5 air quality index breakpoints, which are divided into six levels from cleanest to most polluted.

It is used to inform the public about potential health risks.

Below are the air quality indexes, their corresponding colors, and cautions to follow:

Good (Green) – air quality is clean and safe

Fair (Yellow) – safe but with a presence of pollution

Unhealthy for sensitive groups (Orange) – people with respiratory disease should limit outdoor exposure

Very Unhealthy (Red) – avoid traffic-heavy areas, and people with respiratory disease should stay indoors and rest as much as possible; trips are encouraged to be postponed, and the use of vehicles is restricted

Acutely Unhealthy (Purple) – people should limit outdoor exposure, and those with respiratory disease should stay indoors and rest as much as possible; unnecessary trips should be postponed, motor vehicle use may be restricted, and industrial activities are limited

Emergency (Maroon) – everyone must stay indoors with windows and doors closed unless heat stress is possible; motor vehicles are only allowed for emergencies, and industrial activities (except those vital for public safety and health) are limited

How to protect yourself from the haze

Here are some tips from the health department to avoid the risks brought by haze:

Stay indoors as much as possible.

Wear a KN95 face mask if going outside.

Close all doors and windows and use a wet cloth to cover their crevices.

Use headlights or fog lights when traveling, especially during nighttime.

Stay away from low-lying areas where smoke and suspended particles may settle.

Public events in open areas may continue but must observe air quality before deciding whether to push through or cancel.

Using masks is also encouraged in classrooms, with teachers keeping a close eye on sick students or those with existing heart and lung conditions.

When the haze worsens, vulnerable people (elderly, pregnant, with health conditions) should be stopped from doing long outdoor work. – Rappler.com

World.title: Comelec seeks bigger budget for 2027 as it prepares for 2028 elections
World.content:
ELECTIONS. Voters cast their vote at polling precincts of Guadalupe Elementary School in Cebu City, in the midterm elections, on May 12, 2025.

Speaking at a House budget hearing, Comelec Chairman George Garcia says P9.12 billion was cut from the poll body's budget for preparation for the national and local elections

MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Elections (Comelec) on Tuesday, September 1, appealed to the House of Representatives to restore its proposed P52.66-billion budget request for 2027.

The Comelec requested a higher budget in preparation for the national and local elections in 2028. The Department of Budget and Management (DBM), however, only recommended a P44.7-billion budget for the poll body in 2027.

Speaking at a House budget hearing, Comelec Chairman George Garcia said P9.12 billion was cut from the Comelec’s budget for preparation for the national and local elections.

He warned that the cuts could compromise the poll body’s preparations if the budget proves insufficient.

The Comelec estimated that there would be around 74 million voters by 2028, which would also increase the demand for a higher number of voting precincts.

The DBM also slashed P5.75 billion from the Comelec’s proposed budget for regular operations and P345 million from its other locally funded projects.

If the budget cuts were not restored by Congress, the Comelec said there would be a shortage of 9,310 election counting machines. This could increase the number of voters assigned to each polling precinct, resulting in longer lines and voting times on election day.

Garcia said the cuts would also affect the printing of ballots, forms, and voter information sheets, as well as the deployment of machines and supplies to polling places. Other affected expenses include ballot packaging, consultancy for an international certification entity, and overtime pay.

The DBM also removed the P118-million budget proposal of the Comelec for the lease of warehouses and venues. Without this, Garcia said they will not have a venue for the filing of certificates of candidacy in September 2027.

The filing of certificates of candidacy is typically held in October, but the Comelec wants to set the filing period from September 20 to 27, 2027.

The Comelec said an earlier filing of certificates of candidacy will allow the poll body to print ballots earlier.

The 2027 budget proposal also contains no allocation for the Comelec’s capital outlay, which covers physical assets such as buildings. Garcia said the commission’s lack of adequate office space has long been a problem. – Rappler.com

World.title: Purple harvest: Safeguarding the future of the ube industry
World.content:
VISCA UBE-2. One of the nationally recommended variants of ube from the Philippine Root Crops Research and Training Center.

As demand for ube surges worldwide, Leyte farmers call for laws that may help stop raw ube from being sold abroad

BAYBAY CITY, Philippines — “Hulog ng Langit.” (Unexpected blessing.)

This is how Olegario Paredes Jr., a root crop farmer from Eastern Visayas, describes the rise of ube (purple yam) in global food trends.

Ube has been steadily finding its place in the global market in recent months, earning comparisons to Japan’s matcha as a distinctly Filipino product with growing international appeal.

Transparency Market Research values the global ube market at roughly US$455 million in 2024, with projections climbing to $943 million by 2035. For farmers like Paredes, it is a chance to turn a once-ordinary crop into a reliable source of income.

One of the founders of Organikong Magsasaka at Mangingisda ng Rehiyon Otso (OMMRO), Paredes previously cultivated sweet potato and cassava at the Juanito Eco Farm School for Practical Agriculture (JEFSPA) in Kananga, Leyte.

But ube changed farming for him.

“Labing pamatuod lang, ang ube ang maoy naghatag ug maayong kita sa akoa, sa JEFSPA, ug sa uban pa nga mga farmers,” Paredes says.

(More than anything, ube has provided a good source of income for me, JEFSPA, and other farmers.)

Global demand

Paredes started planting ube in 2023.

The crop that once seemed ordinary was beginning to attract an extraordinary amount of attention. Soon, the surge reached Eastern Visayas directly.

As international interest in ube spiked in 2024, the Fatima Multi-Purpose Cooperative, a cooperative that uplifts local farmers, fisherfolk, and low-income groups, began venturing into ube processing.

They reached out to Paredes for an organic supply agreement.

Soon, foreigners began visiting the region in search of ube suppliers, Paredes tells Rappler.

“Niabot sa farm, niari sa region para pagkita sa amo production area ug ang processing sa Fatima,” Paredes recalls.

(They visited the farm and came to the region to see our production area and the processing facility in Fatima.)

FOREIGN INTEREST. Moroccan nationals visit Paredes’ farm to get ube supply deals. Photo Courtesy of Olegario Paredes Jr.

In March 2026, a Moroccan buyer who was looking for a steady source of ube powder visited Paredes. The buyer wanted 1,000 kilograms of ube every month for distribution across four countries.

That single order alone works out to roughly 80 tons of raw ube a month.

And that Moroccan buyer wasn’t an outlier.

Purple gold

Since he started planting ube, Paredes’ farm has fielded over 10 separate foreign inquiries.

That demand pushed him to convert more of his farmland to ube production.

As a general rule, 50 tons of ube, sold at P50 per kilo, brings in P2.5 million. However, that kind of sales, he says, is only possible with consistent monitoring and cooperative weather.

But ube farming can also be challenging.

Ube’s full production cycle—from land propagation to harvest—takes about a year, Paredes explains.

In the early days, Paredes’ crops were vulnerable to pathogens, waterlogging, and mistimed planting. All the risks are concentrated in the plant’s fragile first few months.

Starting an ube farm isn’t cheap, either. Testing and planting materials come at a cost, with each seedling running P30 to P40 which can potentially rise proportionally to the demand.

While ube is a resilient crop—which means it can handle intense weather conditions—Leyte’s frequent exposure to disruptive storms could still affect yield, particularly given that harvest season is from September to November.

Support system

To meet the demand in the long run, farmers need more than planting materials: they need proper ube production training, processing tools, and adequate funding support.

RESILIENT CROP. Ube can handle intense weather conditions, but ube farmers need support to protect ube varieties and meet global demand. Photo Courtesy of JEFSPA

For instance, right now, farmers are having difficulties sourcing seedlings, Paredes says. To help close that gap, he started supplying planting materials beyond his own region, with buyers often offering advance payment just to reserve stock.

The Department of Agriculture’s high-value crops division also distributed over 50,000 ube seedlings to OMMRO members and other farmers in the first quarter of 2026.

Paredes and OMMRO work with various institutions, including the Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Training Institute, and other local and international agencies to address these challenges.

Among these agencies is the Philippine Root Crops Research and Training Center (PhilRootCrops), which is based at Visayas State University (VSU) in Baybay City.

Established in 1977, PhilRootCrops is the country’s national research and training center for root crops and tubers. It conducts regular cultivation workshops and crop monitoring.

The center’s director, Professor Marlon Tambis, calls ube one of the most resilient crops in the Philippines. Ube is a perennial crop with strong economic upside, he notes, yet many farmers still lack the training to make the most of it.

Tambis says the crop’s potential is outpacing the resources needed to develop it. PhilRootCrops is currently developing new cultivation technologies but the funding hasn’t kept pace.

“While we are provided by VSU of P500,000 every year, it’s still very small,” Tambis says.

“Of course, that is not enough because we are a national center. We have a national mandate. We have clients from everywhere in the Philippines. That’s just one month’s expenses,” he says.

It’s been this way for years, Tambis says. Through PhilRootCrops’ long and continued efforts, the center has managed to acquire multiple partnerships that continue to fund its operations and development, a lifeline that has kept its research going even as government funding stays thin.

Safeguard ube

Ube’s rise is an opportunity too important to let slip away, Paredes points out. Securing that opportunity starts with protecting the crop itself.

SUPPORT SYSTEM. PhilRootCrops conducts regular cultivation workshops and crop monitoring to support ube farmers.

First, Paredes wants ube formally declared a priority crop by law, a status he believes would unlock more structured, long-term government support. He also calls for safeguarding the country’s ube varieties, beginning with a stop to raw ube from being sold abroad.

“Unta, ang gobyerno, dili nila i-allow na ibaligya sa gawas ang raw ube. Kung pwede, powder or processed product lang para maprotect nato ato mga gipananom na mga ube varieties,” says Paredes.

(Hopefully, the government will not allow raw ube to be sold abroad. If possible, only powdered or processed products should be exported so we can protect the ube varieties that we have cultivated.)

On August 22, Leyte 4th District Representative Richard Gomez filed House Bill No. 10225, known as the Philippine Ube Industry Development Act, to declare purple yam a national priority crop and boost production and exports.

Then there’s the matter of people.

Small farmer groups need to be organized and backed with real support so that big companies don’t end up monopolizing the industry and dictating prices at farmers’ expense.

Paredes says there should be a dedicated agency to help farmers navigate exports and move faster.

For years, farmers struggled with low demand for their crops. With ube, for the first time in a long while, that’s no longer the problem.

Whether Eastern Visayas farmers will be able to take full advantage of this demand depends on the support they get. – Rappler.com

Jennifer Jezreel Kaye Pading is an economics student at Visayas State University in Baybay City in Leyte. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, she is also the executive editor of Amaranth and community officer of AYEJ-Leyte Panaad Ha Sinirangan.

World.title: Tokayev Calls for Stronger SCO Cooperation as Experts See SCO Emerging as Key Multipolar Platform
World.content:
ALMATY – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has called for stronger cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) on security, trade, transport, investment and water, as the organization marks 25 years of development, while experts say its expanding agenda is positioning the SCO as an increasingly important platform in the emerging multipolar international order.

Speaking at the Sept. 1 SCO summit in Bishkek, the Kazakh President described the organization’s evolution from the Shanghai Five into a major international organization spanning much of Eurasia and representing almost half of the world’s population.

“The SCO operates outside the logic of military-political blocs and is not directed against any state. It is based on a completely different political philosophy – the ‘Shanghai Spirit,’ whose foundation is the idea of joint work for the sake of progress,” Tokayev said.

According to Prof. Dr. Zijad Bećirović, director of the International Institute for Middle Eastern and Balkan Studies (IFIMES) in Ljubljana, the organization’s transformation reflects broader changes in the international system.

“The transformation of the organisation reflects the wider transformation of the international system. The SCO has evolved from a regional security mechanism into a broader platform addressing security, trade, energy, investment, connectivity and economic cooperation,” he told the Astana Times.

“Its importance is not simply a matter of size. The organisation brings together major political, economic and demographic centers, making it one of the most significant institutional expressions of the emerging multipolar order,” he added.

From regional security to wider cooperation

Tokayev also called for stronger mutual trust and security cooperation, noting that the SCO brings together major Eurasian powers whose positions influence the emerging international order. He proposed holding an SCO ministerial conference on strategic stability and confidence-building measures in Eurasia, with discussions potentially covering reducing military risks, preventing a new arms race, and avoiding dangerous incidents.

“Of particular concern is the fact that the consequences of armed conflicts are already extending beyond the immediate zones of hostilities, affecting international markets, commercial shipping, and the sustainability of energy and transport links. This has significantly increased the risk of the cross-border spread of crisis phenomena,” Tokayev said.

Connectivity as a practical area of cooperation

Economic and transport cooperation was another major theme of Tokayev’s address. President Tokayev proposed establishing SCO cross-border trade zones based on existing border cooperation centers. Such zones, he said, could test simplified trade procedures, digital processes and modern payment mechanisms.

He also supported creating an SCO Development Bank and proposed directing its resources primarily toward infrastructure, technological and industrial projects.

Bećirović sees connectivity as one area where the SCO can translate its broad political ambitions into practical cooperation.

“The diversity of the SCO is both a challenge and an opportunity. Its members have different strategic priorities and, in some cases, serious bilateral disagreements. But economic cooperation does not require political uniformity. It requires identifiable interests that can be pursued together,” he said.

The strongest potential, in his view, lies in Eurasian transport connectivity.

“The geography of trade is changing rapidly, with new transport corridors, railways, ports, logistics centres, energy infrastructure and digital networks reshaping commercial links across the continent,” Bećirović added.

Kazakhstan links SCO agenda to global governance

Tokayev also used the SCO+ format to present Kazakhstan’s broader vision of the international system. Speaking during the extended meeting, he noted that the world needs an order in which confrontation and the “cult of force” give way to mutual responsibility, joint development and long-term cooperation.

President Tokayev proposed that the key principles of the SCO be reflected in a special UN General Assembly resolution dedicated to the International Day of Multilateralism and Diplomacy for Peace.

“The UN should remain the core of the international system, and its Charter – the universal foundation of international law,” Tokayev said.

Manarbek Kabaziyev, deputy chairman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute under Kazakhstan’s Foreign Ministry, also stressed that the SCO should not be regarded as a replacement for other international organizations, in a conversation with the Astana Times.

“The SCO occupies a somewhat different niche. It is primarily a platform for broad political dialogue and practical cooperation among Eurasian states, bringing together countries with different political systems, economic models, civilizational and cultural characteristics,” Kabaziyev said.

According to Tokayev, strengthening preventive diplomacy should be an important part of reforming global governance.

The Kazakh President also called for SCO support for Kazakhstan’s proposals to establish an International Water Organization under the UN and an SCO Water Issues Analysis Center.

Cooperation without political uniformity

The ability to pursue common economic interests despite political differences may ultimately determine how effective the SCO can become. The organization brings together China, Russia, India, Iran, Pakistan and the Central Asian states, among others, with different foreign policy priorities and economic models. Bećirović does not see this diversity as necessarily preventing cooperation.

“Its strategic value lies in its ability to bring together states with different interests and political systems and provide a framework for dialogue and cooperation,” he said.

Kabaziyev similarly notes that the emerging Eurasian approach should not be understood as a model based on uniformity.

“I would speak not so much of a ready-made ‘Eurasian model’ as of the formation of its individual principles and mechanisms,” he said.

He described the approach as based on “pluralism of development paths,” where countries can maintain their own political and economic systems while developing practical cooperation.

“Therefore, I would call it integration through connectivity, rather than integration through unification,” Kabaziyev said.

The test of the next years

The Bishkek summit therefore comes at a point when the SCO’s main challenge is no longer simply defining its areas of cooperation. Its agenda has already expanded considerably. The question is how effectively its members can turn that broad agenda into mechanisms and projects.

At the global level, Tokayev’s emphasis on multilateralism and the UN reflects Kazakhstan’s effort to position the SCO not as a replacement for existing international institutions, but as a regional platform contributing to a more multipolar system.

Bećirović believes the organization’s ability to maintain dialogue among states with divergent interests may itself become one of its most important functions.

“In an increasingly fragmented international environment this function is becoming more important,” he said.

Twenty-five years after its establishment, the SCO has grown far beyond its original security-focused mandate. Its next stage will depend on whether its members can use that diversity not as an obstacle, but as a basis for practical cooperation across the increasingly interconnected Eurasian space.

World.title: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic Meet US Fiscal Transparency Requirements, Report Finds
World.content:
ALMATY – Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic are the only Central Asian countries to meet the United States Department of State’s minimum fiscal transparency requirements, while Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan did not meet the criteria, according to the 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report released by the U.S. Department of State.

The report assesses whether governments receiving U.S. assistance meet minimum standards for the public disclosure of budget and financial information. The latest review covered the period from Jan. 1 to Dec. 31, 2025 and evaluated 139 governments.

Overall, the department found that 73 governments met the minimum fiscal transparency requirements, while 67 did not. Of the governments that fell short, 14 were assessed as having made significant progress toward meeting the requirements.

Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic were included among the 73 governments that met the standards. The three other Central Asian states – Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan – were included among the 67 governments that did not meet the minimum requirements. None of the three was identified as having made significant progress during the review period.

What the U.S. fiscal transparency assessment measures

The assessment focuses on whether governments make key public financial information available and whether citizens and other stakeholders can meaningfully examine how public resources are managed. The criteria include the public availability of national budget documents, including revenues and expenditures by ministry, as well as information on sovereign debt and the terms and conditions of sovereign loans made to foreign borrowers.

The department also examines the independence and effectiveness of supreme audit institutions, public disclosure of government audits, and transparency surrounding natural resource extraction and public procurement.

For the 2026 assessment, the U.S. strengthened the criteria by specifically requiring governments to make the terms and conditions of sovereign loans to foreign borrowers publicly accessible, including information on liabilities and collateralized assets.

The report said fiscal transparency contributes to effective public financial management, market confidence and economic sustainability. It can also reduce risks associated with corruption, financial crimes and unfair practices in international markets. At the same time, the State Department stressed that the assessment does not constitute an assessment of corruption. A country failing to meet the minimum fiscal transparency requirements does not necessarily mean that significant corruption exists, while meeting the requirements does not necessarily indicate a low level of corruption.

A broader concern for Central Asia

The contrasting assessments highlight differences in the region’s approach to fiscal disclosure. For Central Asian economies seeking to attract investment, the issue extends beyond compliance with a particular U.S. assessment. Greater transparency over government budgets, public debt, state-owned enterprises, natural-resource contracts and public procurement can affect how investors assess fiscal risks and the predictability of the business environment.

The State Department noted that fiscal transparency helps build market confidence and supports economic sustainability by giving citizens and markets greater visibility into government finances.

The 2026 report also warns that assessments can change from year to year because the U.S. government is required to update and strengthen its minimum criteria, while governments’ performance and available information can also change.

World.title: Tokayev Joins World Nomad Games Opening in Bishkek
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev attended the official opening ceremony of the sixth World Nomad Games in Bishkek and greeted Kazakhstan’s national team, which consists of 152 athletes competing across all 43 disciplines at this year’s games, reported Akorda.
